καθίδρυσις.definition: = of Artemis, D.S.4.51; Iamb.Myst.5.23 , cf. Poll.1.11, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.252; Cod.Just.1.4.26.6 ; foundation-festival, BGU1.28

καθιερεύω.definition: sacrifice, offer, Pl.Phdr.252c; Arist.EN1148b26; D.H.8.1: cf

καθιέρωσις.definition: dedication, Aeschin.3.46, D.H.6.1, J.AJ19.7.5, Ph.2.234, Plu.Publ.15, BMus.Inscr.481*.21 , etc.: Dor. Schwyzer 203.9

καθικετεύω.definition: Ion. strengthd. for entreat earnestly, Hdt.6.68; Hld.6.14; c. inf., Plu.Cat. Mi.32, cf. Parth.5.2, Ph.2.384:—also in Med., E.Or.324

καθιλαρεύομαι.definition: c. gen., and c. dat., sine expl., Suid

καθίμησις.definition: a letting down by a rope, Plu.2.264f

καθίννυμαι.definition: by-form of Hp.Fract.3,8; take a hip-bath, Id.Mul.1.84, cf. 2.154, al.; cf

καθιππάζομαι.definition: trans., ride down, overrun with horse, Hdt.9.14; metaph., trample under foot, A.Eu.150 ; ib.779 , cf. 731: later c. gen., D.L.4.47

καθιπποτροφέω.definition: squander a fortune in keeping horses, Is.5.43

καθοδηγέω.definition: guide, LXXJb.12.23, Plu.Cat.Ma.13: c. acc., Id.2.558d

καθοδηγός.definition: guide, Hellanic.51 J., Str.15.2.6, Orph.H.8.8, Apollod.3.4.1; PMag.Osl.1.338

καθομηρεύω.definition: express in Homeric language, Hsch. s.v

καθομιλέω.definition: conciliate by daily intercourse, win the; Pass., to be used in daily intercourse, to be current, esp. in pf. part. Pass., Plb.10.5.9; Phld.Rh.1.161S.; Alex.Aphr.in Mete.7.9, cf. Antig.Mir.8; also has become a proverb,…

καθόπλισις.definition: arming, making of arms, Philoch. ap. Anon.Oxy.1241V6; mode of arming, armour, Plb.6.23.14, Ael.Tact.2.7:—so Plb.11.32.7, Ael.Tact.2.9, SIG569.33 ; Plb.3.113.7; D.S.5.34

καθορίζω.definition: determine, Phld.D.1.14; bound, define, Hsch.:—Med., lay claim to, Sammelb.5240.9

καθορμίζω.definition: bring a ship into harbour, bring to anchor; metaph., hast brought thyself to such miseries, A.Pr.965; Plu.2.455c:—Pass., is suspended from them, Arist.PA671b25: metaph., Max.Tyr.30.3; of logical dependence, Simp.in de…

καθόρμιον.definition: = necklace, PMagd.42.5 , LXXHo.2.13, Phot., Suid.; Hsch

καθοσιόω.definition: dedicate, Poll.1.11, cf. OGI 383.109; betroth, J.BJ1.24.5

καθοσίωσις.definition: dedication, Poll.1.11; devotion, fidelity, POxy.2106.9 , Just.Nov.App.4.1; as a title, SIG905.11 , cf.Arch.Pap.1.298

καθυβρίζω.definition: Ion. treat despitefully, insult; c. dat., Hdt.1.212, Paus.4.27.3; also dub. l. in D.H.11.2

καθυγραίνω.definition: moisten well, Arist.Pr.863b23; liquefy, in Pass., Plu.2.953e

καθυμνέω.definition: sing of much or constantly, descant upon, Cleanth.1.6, Phld.Rh.1.221 S., D.S.11.11, J.BJ1.31.3, Plu.2.1117a; make a hymn of, Epicur.Fr.605

καθυπερέχω.definition: to be much superior, opp. Aristeas257: c. gen., Euryph. ap.Stob.4.39.27; in or by a thing, Plb.2.25.9; Callicrat. ap.Stob.4.28.18: rarely c. acc., TheanoEp.5.4: c. acc. pers. et dat. rei, Diotog. ap. Stob.4.7.62:—Pass…

καθυπερηφανέω.definition: strengthd. for Arg. Ar.Ach.: c. gen., treat with disdain, Phld.Vit.p.7J.:— also Hsch. s.v. Eust.561.1:—hence Subst. Phld.Vit.p.28J

καθυπερτερέω.definition: Astrol., of planetary influences, prevail, Heph. Astr.1.16, Porph.in Ptol.188: c. gen., Ptol.Tetr.119: c. acc., overcome, Vett.Val.102.14, al.:—Pass., Ptol.Tetr.88 : generally, c.gen., prevail over, Vett. Val.11.8, cf…

καθυπερτέρησις.definition: Astrol., prepollence, Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod. Astr.8.106, Ptol.Tetr.193, Vett.Val.5.15, al.: generally, prevalence, prob. in Herm. ap. Stob.1.42.7

καθυπέρτερος.definition: commonly metaph., having the upper hand, superior, Hdt.1.67: abs., Th.5.14; Hdt.7.233, cf. Th.7.56; A.Th.226 ; Theoc.24.99: c. gen., X.Mem.4.6.14, cf. Theoc.24.100, etc.: neut. as Adv., = Id.2.60 :— Sup. highest, Hdt.…

καθυπηρετέομαι.definition: assist, Sor.1.25; . . keeping up with . . , Sch.Pl.Phdr.244b

καθυπνόω.definition: Ion. fall fast asleep, Hdt.4.8, 7.12, al., X.Mem.2.1.30, Aen.Tact.18.17, Phld.Hom.p.25 O., IG4.952.51 : Ep. part. dub. in Maiist.16:—Pass., asleep, Hdt.3.69, 7.14, 17

καθυποβάλλω.definition: subject, Heliod.in EN109.20; place underneath, Aët.16.110

καθυπογράφω.definition: describe, Eust.974.13; append signature to a document or edict, Sammelb.5251.4 , PFlor.36.22 , Cod.Just.1.1.7.11, etc

καθυπόκειμαι.definition: strengthd. for to be 'in being', 'in evidence', Artem.1.1

καθυποκρίνομαι.definition: subdue by histrionic arts; c. inf., . . pretend to be some one else, Luc.DMar.13.2; Ph.2.280: c. acc., counterfeit, ib.520; Him.Ecl.3.2

καθυπονοέω.definition: suspect, c. acc. et inf., PRyl.127.15 (i; form a vague conception of, Dam.Pr.29: c. acc. et inf., suppose, Sor.2.64; perceive, understand, Phld.Rh.2.18 S

καθυποστιβίζω.definition: paint underneath with , in Pass., Nic.Dam.4 J

καθυποτοπέομαι.definition: place a sinister construction upon, EM762.15

καθυστερέω.definition: of Time, come too late for . . , PSI6.607.7 ; Plb.11.33.8; Id.5.17.7; Id.10.39.5, cf. D.S.5.53, Str.14.2.5: c. acc., shalt not be slow to offer, LXXEx.22.29: abs., Men.Mon.396; delay, Plb.5.16.5; of growing plants, to…

καθυφαίνω.definition: interweave, weave in, LXXEx.28.17:—Med., aor. 1 part. Lyr.Alex.Adesp.10.15:—Pass., to be inwoven, LXXJu.10.21

καθυφίημι.definition: give up, surrender treacherously; Med., give way, yield, c. dat. pers., X.HG2.4.23; slacken, Polyaen.8.24.1: abs., Luc.Abd.7

καθυφίσταμαι.definition: pf. inf. to be really existent, Jul.Or.5.163d

καίνισις.definition: renovation, J.AJ18.1.1; v.l. for in Ph.2.45

καινολογία.definition: strange language or phraseology, Plb.38.9.2, D.H.Lys.3; telling of strange tales, Str.1.2.8

καινοποιέω.definition: pf. Plb.4.2.4:—make new; make changes, innovate, Plb.1.4.5, etc.: abs., Luc.Prom.Es3, etc.:—Pass., what new-fangled, strange words are these? S.Tr.873, cf. Plb.9.2.4; innovations, OGI669.44 , cf. POxy.237 viii 42

καινοποιΐα.definition: complete change, Plb.4.2.10: c. gen., Vett.Val.48.10 , al

καινοπραγέω.definition: Gramm., coin new forms or phrases, in Pass., Eust.36.16

καινοπραγία.definition: innovation, f. l. for in D.S.15.8

καινοπρεπής.definition: novel, Hermog.Id.1.12; of innovations in law, Just.Nov.105.1. Adv. in a new-fangled manner: Comp. Arist.Metaph.989b6: Sup. D.C.79.11

καινοτομέω.definition: cut fresh into, in mining, open a new; mostly metaph., begin something new, institute anew, Ar.V.876 : abs., make changes or innovations in the state, Id.Ec.584 , Arist.Pol.1305b41, 1316b19, Plb.15.30.1, PLips.35.19 ,…

καινοτομία.definition: opening of new mines, Hyp.Eux.36; mostly metaph., making anew, inventing, Pl.Lg.715d; innovation, Plu.Cic.2: in Music, Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39 xxii 5; Mitteis Chr.96 ii 19 : pl., innovations in the state, Lat. res novae, …

καινουργέω.definition: make new, Alciphr.3.3; re-create; begin something new, Hp.VM21; what new plan art thou meditating? E.IA2 ; speak new, strange words, ib.838; coin, Dam.Pr.439: abs., Antiph.29: usu. in bad sense, make innovations, X.HG…

καινουργία.definition: making new: innovation in the state, Isoc.6.50; of Christianity, prob. in OGI569.18 ; renewal, recreation, Max.Tyr.41.4; of manufacture, J.AJ12.2.9, cf. D.H.Isoc.9, Hierocl.p.52A

καινόφιλος.definition: often changing one's friends, Phot., Suid

καινοφωνία.definition: vocum novitas, Gloss., cf. Phlp.in APo.11.7

καίνυμι.definition: overcome, Act. only in imper; later, to be adorned, equipped, Pi.O.1.27; is well furnished with . . , E.El.616; Ar.Eq.685; AP3.18.1 : abs., a well-armed band, A.Eu.766. — Poet. word

καίνω.definition: A.Ag.1562, Ch.886: fut. E.HF1074 : aor. 2 A.Ch.930; inf. Dor. Theoc.24.92: pf. S.Fr.1058:—Pass., A.Th.347 , E.IT27:—kill, slay, A.Th.630 , S. l. c., Timocr.1.9, Theoc.l.c.: once in X.Cyr.4.2.24

καίριμος.definition: = dub. in Macho ap.Ath.13.581b, cf. Al.Le.16.21; PElor.143.2

καιρομανέω.definition: prob. f.l. for guide in season, AP9.272

καίρωσις.definition: act of fastening them, Poll.7.33, Hsch

καιροσκοπέω.definition: gloss on Hdn.Epim.63; prob. in Men.Mon.307

καιρόφιλος.definition: lover or observer of times, epith. of an astrologer, Vett.Val.271.25

καιροφυλακέω.definition: watch for the right time, c. acc., D.23.173, Hyp.Phil.8; Arist.Pol.1337b41; Olymp.Hist.p.460 D.: abs., App.Pun.88, Mith.70; also, attend on, Luc.Abd.16:—Pass., Metrod.Fr.60

Καισαρεύω.definition: play the Caesar, D.C.66.8: the Caesarian party, App.BC3.91:—also, = PGnom.241 : worshippers of Caesar, IGRom.4.1348

κακαγγελία.definition: evil tidings, Antig.Mir.12, prob. in Man.4.556, cf. Hp. ap. Gal.19.107

κακάγγελος.definition: bringing ill tidings, A.Ag.636, cf. Plu.2.241b, Ant.Lib.15.4

κακανθέω.definition: bear such blossom, Sch. ad loc

κακεντρεχής.definition: active in mischief, Epich.[259], Plb.22.19.3, Str.7.3.7; Vett.Val.17.5

κακεργασία.definition: bad effect, prob. f.l. for Thphr.Sud.10

κακεργέτης.definition: evil-doer, nickname of Ptolemy Euergetes II, Ath.4.184c

κακεστώ.definition: ill-being, opp. Hsch., cj. in Democr.182

κακηγορέω.definition: speak ill of, abuse, slander, Pl.Smp.173d, R.395e, al.; Ps.-Phoc.226: abs., . . from evil-speaking, Pl.Lg.934e, cf. Arist.EN1129b23, Hyp.Fr.246:—Pass., to be abused, Pl.R.368b

κακηγορία.definition: evil-speaking, abuse, slander, Pi.P.2.53 , Arist.EN1131a9, Phld.Ir.p.52 W. ; abuse of one, Pl.Phdr.243a, 243b; action for abusive language, D.21.32, cf. 81; Lys.10.2, etc.; D.57.30

κακήγορος.definition: Dor. evil- speaking, abusive, slanderous, Pi.O.1.53; Pl.Phdr.254e; abusive of one, Ath.5.220a: Comp. Pherecr.96: Sup. Ecphant.5. Adv. Poll.8.81

κακκαβίζω.definition: cackle, of partridges, Arist.HA536b14, Thphr.Fr.181; of doves and partridges coupled, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.180; of owls, hoot, Ar.Lys.761 :—also Hsch. cf

κακκάβιον.definition: Dim. of , Eub.38, Orib.5.33.3 , PLond.5.1657.6 : also Aët.1.130

κακόβιος.definition: living poorly, living a hard life, Hdt.4.95, X.Cyr.7.5.67 , Arist.HA616b31, Str.17.2.1

κακοβλαστέω.definition: sprout ill or with difficulty, Thphr.CP4.7.3

κακοβλαστής.definition: sprouting ill or with difficulty, ib.1.20.6, 4.7.2: Comp. Id.HP4.14.1

κακοβολέω.definition: have unlucky throws , Sch.Ar.Ra.1001 , Suid. s.v

κακοβουλεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be ill-advised, E.Ion877 ; but the form is incorrect and corrupt

κακοβουλία.definition: ill-advisedness, J.BJ2.11.3, D.L.7.93, Quint.Ps.138.20, prob. in POxy.1101.7

κακόγαμος.definition: marrying unlawfully, Eust.1415.47; an ill-starred marriage, Sch.Triclin.S.OT1214, cf. Paul.Al.O.2

κακογένειος.definition: with a poor beard, Suid. s.v

κακογνώμων.definition: gen. ill-judging, wanting in judgement, Sm.1 Ki.25.3, D.C.77.11

κακοδαιμονάω.definition: to be tormented by an evil genius, possessed by an evil spirit, Ar.Pl.372, X.Mem.2.1.5, D.8.16 , Din.1.91, v.l. for sq. in M.Ant.2.8

κακοδαιμονέω.definition: to be unfortunate, unhappy, X.Hier.2.4; Astrol., occupy the region of Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.9, Ptol.Tetr.195, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.130

κακοδαιμόνημα.definition: Astrol., occupation of the region of Vett.Val.74.6, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.119, 8.126, al

κακοδαιμονιστής.definition: worshipper of the member of a 'Satanist' club, Lys.Fr.53.2

κακοδαίμων.definition: gen. possessed by an evil; evil genius, Ar.Eq.112, cf. Arr.Epict.4.4.38

κακοδάκρυτος.definition: producing inferior gum, of trees, Hsch. s.v

κακοδιδασκαλέω.definition: instruct in evil, S.E.M.2.42, cf. Tab.Defix. inIG12.p.1

κακοδοξέω.definition: to be in ill repute, X.Mem.1.7.2, Muson.Fr.9p.47H., Sch.E.Andr.777

κακόδοξος.definition: in ill repute, oflow reputation, Thgn.195, X.Ages.4.1: Comp. Pl.Min.321a; of things, inglorious, E.Andr.778

κακοείμων.definition: gen. ill-clad, Od.18.41, cf. Ps.Luc.Philopatr.21, Hsch. s.v

κακόζηλος.definition: having bad taste: hence in Rhet., using a bad, affected style , D.L.1.38; = Longin.3.4, cf. Demetr.Eloc.186, Hermog.Inv.4.12. Adv. Gal.18.180

κακοηθεύομαι.definition: act maliciously, play a scurvy trick; Medic., to be malignant, Gal.18.464

κακοηθίζομαι.definition: = Arr.Epict.3.16.4, etc; put a bad construction on things, Stob.2.7.2

κακοηχής.definition: ill-sounding, dissonant, Phld.Po.2.42: Comp. Adam.2.42:—also Suid. s.v

κακοθάνατος.definition: dying miserably, Plu.2.22c , cf. Vett.Val.128.19, Sch.E.Hipp.1143

κακόκνημος.definition: Dor. weak- legged, thin-legged, Theoc.4.63, Call.Fr.472

κακολογέω.definition: revile, abuse, Lys.8.5, Isoc.6.98, Hyp.Fr.25, LXXEx.21.16, Ev.Matt.15.4, al.: abs., D.36.61:—Pass., Gorg.Hel.7, PFay.12.15

κακολογία.definition: coarse expression, bad style, Pl.R.401a: but usu. abuse, reviling, Hdt.7.237, X.Cyr.1.2.6, Hyp.Fr.247, Thphr.Char.28, etc

κακολόγος.definition: evil-speaking, slanderous, Pi.P.11.28, Men.256, Arist.Rh.1381b7; of one, Id.EN1125a8

κακομαχέω.definition: fight unfairly, Plu.2.32b, Luc.Demon.49; fight against odds, use desperate expedients, Phlp.in GC16.28

κακομετρία.definition: short measure, POxy. 1447.6; false metre, Sch.Heph.p.106C. , Eust. ad D.P.739

κακόμετρος.definition: in bad metre, unmetrical, Plu.2.747f, etc.; Phld.Po.Herc.1676.8

κακόμητις.definition: = E.Or.1403 ; pl. Astrol., = Doroth. ap. Heph. Astr.3.30

κακομήτωρ.definition: mother of ill, gloss on Hsch.:—but prob. shd. be read in Man.4.307

κακομηχανία.definition: practising of base arts, mischief, Luc.Phal.1.12, Adam.1.5

κακομήχανος.definition: Dor. mischief-plotting, Il.6.344, Od.16.418; B.17.8; Mosch.Fr.3.7; of things, mischievous, baneful, Il.9.257. Adv. Phot.Bibl.p.292 B

κακόμοιρος.definition: ill-fated, AP7.375 , cf. Maiuri Nuova Silloge630

κακόμορος.definition: = foreg., Hsch. s.v. Suid. s.v. Adv. Cat.Cod. Astr.8.129, 142

κακομορφία.definition: ill shape, ugliness, Gloss.; gloss on Sch.E.Hec.240

κακόνοια.definition: ill-will, malice, opp. Lys.22.16, X.An.7.7.45, Cyr.3.1.38, D.21.204, Ph.2.120, al

κακονομέομαι.definition: Pass., to be badly governed, Ocell.4.8

κακόνοος.definition: contr. Att. pl. disaffected, opp. Antipho Soph.109, Ar.Pax496 , 671; X.Cyr.8.2.1; Id.An.2.5.16; Th.6.24; Lys.25.7; oligarchical oath in Arist.Pol.1310a9; Lys.20.20: Sup. Id.7.28, D.23.6. Adv. Sch.E.Or.108; Poll.5.115:…

κακόξενος.definition: Ion. unfortunate in; unfriendly to strangers, inhospitable, E.Alc.558 , AP7.699, Lyc.1286: Comp., Jul.Ep.89b

κακοπάθεια.definition: distress, misery, Hp.VM10, Antipho3.2.11, Isoc.6.55, Arist.Pol.1278b28; Antipho5.18; of plants or trees, Thphr.CP3.7.8; strain, stress, on the parts of a machine, HeroBel.93.1: pl., Hp. l.c.; your present unmerited su…

κακοπαθέω.definition: fut. PLond.1.98r73 : pf. Aen.Tact.26.7:—to be in ill plight, be in distress, Th.1.78, X.Mem.2.1.17, And.2.26, Lys.6.28, D.18.146; PCair.Zen. 93.17 ; by or from a thing, Th.4.29; Id.2.41; Phld.Oec.p.53 J.; of sickness,…

κακόπαθος.definition: troublesome, laborious, Ph.Bel.56.46; Posidon.48 J. , cf. A.D.Synt.187.24

κακοπάρθενος.definition: accursed maiden, Sch.E.Hec.612; Adj. unbecoming a maid, AP7.468

κακοπατρίδης.definition: Aeol. base- born , prob. in Alc.Supp.28.11; cf. sq

κακόπατρις.definition: base-born, Thgn.193; masc. in Alc.37 A. codd

κακοποιέω.definition: do ill, play the knave, A.Fr.111; trans., do mischief to, injure, Id.Mem.3.5.26, cf. Plb.4.6.10; Id.13.4.1:—Pass., Id.27.7.6

κακοποιΐα.definition: evil-doing, Arist.Rh.Al.1432a9, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.249: pl., injuries, Isoc.12.122; opp. Id.1.26

κακοπολιτεία.definition: bad government, Plb.15.21.3, Plu.Pomp.75: pl., Id.Lyc.7, Ph.1.41, 601

κακόποτμος.definition: ill-fated, ill-starred, B.5.138; A.Ag.1136 ; E.Hel.694 ; Arist.HA616b21

κακόπους.definition: gen. with bad feet, X.Mem.3.3.4, Eq.1.2; Arist.HA487b26

κακοπραγέω.definition: fare ill, fail in an enterprise, Th.4.55; to be in ill plight, Id.2.43; Arist.Rh.1386b26, cf. Aphth.Prog.1, al.: in physical sense, Gal.10.789, al

κακοπραγμοσύνη.definition: evil-doing, Democr.297, D.25.101, Plb.4.23.8, al., Phld.Acad.Ind.p.54M

κακοπράγμων.definition: gen. doing evil, mischievous, X.HG5.2.36, Isoc.15.225, 236, Arist.Ath.35.3: Sup. Plb.8.9.3. Adv. Klio 16.163

κακοπρόσωπος.definition: ugly-faced, Posidipp.43, Plu.2.1058a; Xenocr. ap. Stob.4.40.24

κακόπτερος.definition: with bad wings, weak in the wing, opp. Arist.HA617b4, al.; of the Sphinx, as a bird of ill omen, Epigr. ap. Sch.E.Ph.50

κακορραφία.definition: contrivance of ill, mischievousness, Il.15.16; Od.2.236; . . 12.26

κακορρήμων.definition: gen. telling of ill; a poor speaker, D.C.77.11

κακορροθέω.definition: = c. acc., abuse, revile, E.Hipp.340, Alc.707, Ar.Ach.577, Th.896

κακόρρυθμος.definition: in bad rhythm , Phld.Rh.1.162 S.; Id.Po.Herc.1676.8; of the pulse, Gal.19.409

κακοσιτία.definition: Ion. lack of appetite, Archig. ap. Orib.8.23.3, Poll.6.36; Aret.SD2.6

κακοστόματος.definition: foulmouthed, sens. obsc., = Lat. fellator, AP11.155

κακοστομαχία.definition: bad state of the stomach, Gal.14.735

κακοστόμαχος.definition: having a sensitive stomach; Act., bad for the stomach, unwholesome, Heraclid.Tarent. ap. Ath.3.120c, Philistion ap. eund.3.115d, Dsc.1.127, al., Sor.1.94, Gal.6.641: Comp. Diph.Siph.ap Ath.2.56b

κακόστομος.definition: foul-mouthed, E.IA1001; lacking in eloquence, Ptol.Tetr.166

κακοσύνετος.definition: of bad understanding, Eustr.in EN368.31; cf

κακοσυνθεσία.definition: gloss on Hsch.:— also Phot., Suid

κακοσύνθετος.definition: ill-composed, in Rhet., Quint.8.3.59; Luc.Cal.14; Sch.E.Or.674; ill put together, Sch.Ar.V.818. Adv. Sch.E.Hec.801, al

κακόσχημος.definition: badly formed, of a period, Sch.E.Or.307, cf. Hdn.Epim.177

κακοσχήμων.definition: gen. unseemly, only in Adv. Lib.Or.25.15; Sup. Pl.Lg.728b

κακοσχολεύομαι.definition: play mischievous tricks, Porph.Ep.Aneb.26; in mal. part., Hsch. s.v

κακοσχολέω.definition: of children, to be mischievous, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.77; TheanoEp.4.3

κακοτεχνία.definition: base artifice, malpractice; bad art, applied to forensic oratory by Epicur.Fr.51: generally, Plu.2.228b: esp. in Rhet., false artifice, Demetr.Eloc.27,247, Luc.Par.27, Ath.14.631f: pl., Str.7.3.7

κακότεχνος.definition: using evil practices, artful, Il.15.14: esp. in mal. part., lascivious, AP5.128 : Sup., ib.131 ; of songs, Plu.2.706d. Adv. with bad art, Ph.1.195

κακοτροπία.definition: badness of habits, mischievousness, Th.3.83, D.C.54.21, Artem.4.63; in argument, malice, unfairness, Simp.in Cael.156.27

κακότροπος.definition: malignant, D.C.52.2, Vett.Val.74.12; of animals, mischievous, Hippiatr.129

κακοτυχής.definition: unfortunate, used by E. in lyr., Med.1274, Hipp.669: Sup., ib.679; = sq., Id.HF133; Sch.rec.A.Pers.1013, cf. Cat.Cod.Astr.8.142

κακουργέω.definition: do evil, work wickedness, E.Or.823; of discussion, use captious or unfair arguments, Pl.Grg.489b, cf. 483a, Arist.Rh.1404b39

κακούργημα.definition: knavish trick, fraud, Id.Lg.933e, D.18.31, 24.86, etc.; Pl.R.426e; crime, Antipho5.10, etc

κακουχέω.definition: wrong, injure, Telesp.34H.; maltreat, esp. a wife, Mitteis Chr.284.6 , POxy.281.17 , etc.:— Pass., to be afflicted or injured, LXX3 Ki.2.26; D.S.3.23; Plu.2.114e

κακουχία.definition: maltreatment, Pl.R.615b; of a wife; = bad condition, Alex.80; misery, distress, Plb.3.64.8, Vett. Val.127.13: pl., of ascetic practices, Plu.2.117f

κακόφημος.definition: ill-sounding, ominous, Sch.S.Aj.214; evil or ominous words, J.BJ6.5.3; of persons, foul-mouthed, Ptol.Tetr.166. Adv. with evil words, abusively, Man.5.323

κακοφθόρος.definition: destructive, deadly, Nic.Th.795, Al.168: heterocl. gen. ib.465

κακοφραδής.definition: poet. word, bad in counsel, foolish, Il.23.483, cf. A.R.3.936: neut., as Adv., foolishly, Euph.98.2

κακοφραδία.definition: Ion. folly, h.Cer.227: sg., Nic.Th.348, Q.S.12.554

κακοφρονέω.definition: bear ill-will or malice, A.Ag.1174; to be foolish, Sch.E.Or.821

κακοφυής.definition: of bad natural qualities; growing ill, Thphr.HP8.11.8; PTeb. 61.370

κακοφωνία.definition: ill-sound, of a name, Str.13.2.4; cacophony, Demetr.Eloc.255, A.D.Conj.228.20; opp. Phld.Po.Herc.994.23: dist. fr. Gal.7.59

κακόφωνος.definition: ill-sounding, not producing agreeable sounds, Arist.Aud.802b23; with a bad voice, D.T.631.21, Phlp.in de An.533.32; opp. Phld.Po. Herc.994 Fr.11; of words, cacophonous, D.H.Comp.12, cf. 16 , D.T.631.20; = Sch.Ar.Eq.248

κακόχαρτος.definition: rejoicing in evil, Hes.Op.28, 196, cf. Hsch

κακοχρήσμων.definition: Dor. gen. difficult to live with, v.l. for Theoc.4.22, cf. Sch.ad loc

κακοχροέω.definition: to be of a bad complexion, Dsc.1.128

κακόχροια.definition: bad complexion, Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.48, Gal.17.215; of a corpse, Phld.Mort.30: pl., blotches, Dsc.3.1, Gal.6.814

κακόχροος.definition: contr. of bad complexion, Hp.Prorrh.2.42, Aff.20; of bad coloration, Arist.HA616b31; of bad colour, Nic.Fr.85.5; Gal.17.214; of urine, Id.19.598

κακόχυλος.definition: with bad juice or flavour, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.54a: Comp., ib.68f, 3.80c, Diocl. Fr.138; of meat, Sor.1.94

κακόψογος.definition: malignantly blaming, censorious, Thgn.287, cf. Ptol.Tetr.166

κακύνω.definition: damage, in prcv; in moral sense, corrupt, Com.Adesp.138:—usu. in Pass., to be corrupted, D.C.60.2: esp. become bad, E.Hec.251, Pl.Ti.42c; of soldiers, show cowardice, v.l. for X.Cyr.6.3.27

κάκωσις.definition: esp. in Law, ill-usage, of persons by their natural protectors, Lys.13.91, cf. Is.8.32, D.10.40, etc.; Id.58.32, Men.328; Arist.Ath.56.6; Lycurg.147; also misgovernment, of the Rom. actio repetundarum, Plu.Caes.4

καλάθιον.definition: Dim. of Poll.10.125, Sch.Call.Cer.1; part of a surgical machine, in the shape of a Orib.49.4.41:— also Hsch. s.v

καλαθοειδής.definition: basket-shaped, narrow at the base, Cleom.2.2, Gal.18.822, Theo Sm.p.196H., Simp.in Cael.546.31. Adv. Heraclit.All.46

καλαμαῖος.definition: of or in the cornstalks; festival of Demeter and Persephone at Eleusis, IG22.949.9

καλαμάομαι.definition: gather cornstalks, glean, Cratin.420; LXXDe.24.20: metaph., [Alexander] [Antigonus] Plu.2.182a; gather up the stragglers of an army, LXXJd.20.45; ib.Is.3.12

καλαμαύλης.definition: one who plays on a reed-pipe, Ath.4.176d

καλαμεία.definition: reeds, in a collective sense; reed-land, PTeb.457

καλάμη.definition: stalk, esp. the stalk or; stubble, Arist.Mete.341b27, PSI4.380.6 , 1 Ep.Cor.3.12, etc.: metaph., of an old man, thou mayst still, I ween, perceive the stubble of former strength, Od.14.214; Arist.Rh.1410b14; AP11.36 ;…

καλαμητομία.definition: Ep. cutting of stalks, reaping, AP6.36

καλαμηφάγος.definition: devouring reeds, i.e. cutting or trimming pens, AP6.65.3

καλάμινος.definition: of reed, Hdt.5.101; of cane, bamboo, Hdt.3.98

καλάμιον.definition: = sq. I, POxy.1631.14 : without diminutive sense, ib.1742.4; = II.8, Eust.1181.53

καλαμίς.definition: limed twig, acc; case for a writing-reed, pen-case, Poll.10.59, Hsch.; pen, Phld.Po.2.41

καλαμίσκος.definition: Dim. of used as a tube or; branch of a candlestick, LXXEx.25.30

καλαμίτης.definition: perh. the hero of the probe or, of the splints, nickname of Aristomachus, a surgeon who had a statue at Athens, called D.18.129, cf. 19.249

καλαμογραφία.definition: Ep. writing with a reed or pen, Man.4.72

καλαμοκεντρῖτις.definition: land overgrown with prickly rush, POxy.1911.101

καλαμοσφάκτης.definition: one who kills with a pen, Ph.2.536

καλαμοτύπορ.definition: one who catches birds with limed twigs , Hsch

καλαμουργέω.definition: set up poles for vines, PTeb.120.141 , PSI 4.317.6 :—hence PLond.2.163.24

καλαμόφθογγος.definition: played on a reed, of tunes, Ar.Ra.230

καλαμόφυλλος.definition: with leaves like those of reeds; Subst. = Gp.10.44, Hippiatr.129

καλαμών.definition: reed-bed, Posidipp. inPLit.Lond.60.21, Gp.3.6.6, Paus.Dam.p.160 D., Sch.Il.18.576

καλαμωτή.definition: fence or edging of reed, Eust.1533.51; cf. Hsch

κάλημι.definition: Aeol. for Sapph.1.16 , Supp.21.4: 3sg. impf. Alc.Supp.10.5

καλίζομαι.definition: live in huts, in Lacon. aor. 1 Hsch

καλινδέομαι.definition: only in pres. and impf., = , roll about, wallow, of plague stricken persons, Th.2.52; of birds, Arist.HA612a20,b24; Plu.Tim.28; as a form of exercise, Gal.6.220, cf. 324; roam, X.An.5.2.31; Hdt.3.52: metaph., D.19.199…

καλίνδησις.definition: = a throw of the dice, Alciphr.3.42

καλλαμβάνω.definition: aor. part. Pass. Aeol. for IG 12.526.20

καλλιβλέφαρος.definition: with beautiful eyelids: beautiful-; as Subst., , paint for the eyelids and eyelashes, Dsc.1.69, 1 Enoch8.1, Gal.12.211: as Adj., ib.62

καλλίβολος.definition: name of a throw at dice, Poll.7.204

καλλιγάληνος.definition: Dor. beautiful in its calm, Id.Tr.837

καλλιγένεθλος.definition: beautifully formed, prob. in; Act., having a fair offspring, Corinn.23, Procl.H.6.1

καλλιγένεια.definition: bearer of a fair offspring, name by which Demeter was invoked in the Thesmophoria, Ar.Th.299, Alciphr.2.4, cf.IG14.205 ; or her nurse, Ar. ap. Phot.; epith. of the Moon, Hymn.Mag.5.31; of the Earth, Apollod. ap. Phot.…

καλλίγονος.definition: of noble race, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11 ; IG12.1188 :—fem. epith. of Demeter at Pergamon, Ath.Mitt.37.288

καλλιγραφέω.definition: write beautifully, in point of style; paint beautifully, Poll.5.102

καλλιγραφία.definition: beautiful writing, whether of the characters or the style, cf. Plu.2.397c with 145f; as a subject of competition in schools, good handwriting, CIG3088 : in pl., elegances of style, D.L.3.66

καλλιγύναιξ.definition: gen. with beautiful women, poet. word, only in obl. cases, Il.2.683, 3.75, Od.13.412: gen., Sapph.[26]: dat., Pi.P.9.74

καλλίδενδρος.definition: with fine trees, of places, Plb.5.19.2 , Sch. Pi.O.9.27

καλλιέθειρος.definition: with beautiful hair, Orph.H.50.7: pecul. fem. Nonn.D.27.248

καλλιέλαιος.definition: garden olive, opp. Ep.Rom.11.24:—fem. Arch.Pap.2.218 : as Adj., PCair.Zen.125.3 , Gp.9.8; ib.9.10.6

καλλιεπέομαι.definition: say in fine phrases, . . Th.6.83; use fine language, Arist.Rh.1404b16; Pl.Hipparch.225c:—Pass., Id.Ap.17b:—later in Act., Them.Or.20p.285D

καλλιεπής.definition: elegant in diction, Ar.Th.49 , 60, D.H.Comp.18; etym. of Corn.ND14

καλλιεργέω.definition: in Pass., to be worked beautifully, Phlp.in Ph.327.1; of land, to be well-cultivated, Sammelb.5168.27

καλλιεργία.definition: good work, of improvements made by a tenant, Just.Nov.64.1: generally, good cultivation, Sammelb.4481.16 , etc

καλλιερέω.definition: pf. Ph.1.319: plpf; c. acc., sacrifice with good omens, Theoc.5.148; prob. l. in Orac. ap. D.21.53; Plu.Alex.69: abs., X.Eq.Mag.3.1, cf. Pl.Lg.791a:—Med., Ar.Pl.1181:— Pass., Men.319.8; S.E.P.1.149

καλλίζωνος.definition: with beautiful girdles, Il.7.139, 24.698, Od.23.147; B.5.89: in late Prose, Hld.3.2

καλλίκαρπος.definition: rich in fine fruit, of places; of trees, bearing fine fruit, E.Ba.108 , cf. Thphr.CP1.17.10

Καλλικολώνη.definition: Fair-hill, a hill near Troy, on the Simois, Il.20.53, 151:— also Demetr.Sceps. ap. Sch.Il.20.53

καλλίκομος.definition: beautiful-haired, of women, Il.9.449, Od.15.58, Pi.P.9.106; Hes.Op.75, cf. Th.915; Epimenid.19; Sapph.60; Ar.Pax798 , IG12.821; also of trees, with beautiful foliage, IG2.3412

καλλιλογέω.definition: express in elegant diction, embellish, D.H.8.32, Comp.3 :—Med., use specious phrases, Luc.Tox.35

καλλίμηρος.definition: with beautiful thighs, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.45

καλλίναος.definition: beautifully flowing, E.Med.835 , cf. Alc.589 ; A.R.1.1228: Sup., Hsch

καλλίνικος.definition: gloriously triumphant; adorning or ennobling victory, Pi.P.5.106, N.4.16codd.; E.El.865 , Ph.1728 ; Id.IT12, Alex. in Gëtt. Nachr.1922.10; Call.Iamb.1.283; the glory of victory, Pi.N.3.18; so Id.O.9.2; E.Med.45; Id.HF…

καλλιπάρθενος.definition: with beautiful nymphs, . . E.Hel.1; neck of a beauteous maiden, Id.IA1574:—later Inscr.Magn.252

καλλίπεπλος.definition: with beautiful robe, beautifully clad, of women, Pi.P.3.25, E.Tr.338

καλλιπλόκαμος.definition: with beautiful locks, Il.14.326, 18.407; Pi.O.3.1; E.IA1040 ; Id.El.705

καλλίπνοος.definition: contr. beautifully breathing, Telest.2.1; also of smell, Hsch. s.v. prob. in Porph.in Ptol.182

καλλίπολις.definition: fair city, Pl.R.527c: freq. as pr.n.:— hence Hdt.7.154, etc

καλλιπρόβατος.definition: with beautiful sheep, Suid. s.v. EM395.54

καλλίπρῳρος.definition: with beautiful prow, of ships, E.Med.1335: metaph., of men, with beautiful face, beautiful, A.Th.533; Id.Ag.235

καλλίπυγος.definition: with beautiful Cerc.14; epith. of Aphrodite, Ath.12.554c: Comp., ibid

καλλίπυργος.definition: with beautiful towers, E.Ba.1202; of Thebes, Id.Supp.618 ; high-towering, Ar.Nu.1024

καλλιρρημοσύνη.definition: elegance of language, D.H.Th.23; braggart language, Id.DDeor.21.2

καλλιστάφυλος.definition: with fine grapes, gloss on Hsch

καλλιστεύω.definition: to be the finest or most beautiful, Hdt.1.196, al., E.Tr.226 ; of animals, Hdt.4.72, 163: c. gen., Id.6.61, cf. 7.180:—Med., E.Med.947, cf. Ba.409 , Hipp.1009: pf. part. Pass., E.Oen.p.39A.; Procop.Aed.1.1

καλλιτεκνία.definition: possession of beautiful children, IG12.397 , Parth.33.1

καλλίτεκνος.definition: with beautiful children, IG12.397 Eleg.2, IG12.477 ,Inscr.Prien.225 : Comp., Luc.DDeor.16.1: Sup., Plu.Aem.5:—also Hdn.Epim.186

καλλίτεχνος.definition: making beautiful works of art, Str.1.2.33, 16.2.24, Them.Or.4.56b

καλλιτόκεια.definition: pecul. poet. fem. of sq., Opp.C.1.6

καλλιτράπεζος.definition: with beautiful, i.e. well- spread, table, Call.Com.5, Amips.19

καλλίφωνος.definition: with a fine voice, Pl.Lg.817c; expl. of Corn.ND14

καλλιχέλωνος.definition: with a beautiful tortoise on it, Eup.141

καλλίχορος.definition: with fair dancing-grounds, epith. of; of or for beautiful dances, E.Ph.786 ,Fr.453.7 ; Ar.Ra.452 ; a sacred spring near Eleusis, the fount of goodly dances, h.Cer.272, cf.E.Ion1075 , Supp.392, 619

καλλίχροος.definition: beautiful-coloured, prob. l. in Cypr. Fr.4.6

κάλλυνθρον.definition: sweeper, duster made of palm-leaves, LXXLe.23.40, BGU1120.17

καλλυντήριος.definition: of or for beautifying: hence a festival on the 19th Thargelion, when the statue of Athena Polias was fresh adorned, Phot.,EM487.13

καλλωπισμός.definition: adorning oneself, making a display; ornamentation, Hp.Medic.2; for ornament, X.An.1.9.23; Pl.Phd.64d

καλλωπιστεία.definition: beauty of style, poetica Serv. ad Verg.Aen.1.223

καλλωπιστής.definition: one who adorns himself, dandy, opp. Isoc.1.27, cf. Arist.Rh.1401b24, Phld.Vit.Herc.1457.9

καλοβάτης.definition: tight-rope walker, SIG847.5 , Man.5.146; = funambulus, Gloss

καλόγηρυς.definition: with a fine voice, as etym. of Suid. s. h. v

καλοειδής.definition: of beautiful form, Sopat.in Rh.8.56 W

καλοκἀγαθέω.definition: practise noble arts, dub. cj. in Ar.Fr.198.8

καλοκἀγαθία.definition: the character and conduct of a , nobleness, goodness, X.Mem.1.6.14, Arist.EN1124a4, al., Poll.4.10; freq. in Inscrr., SIG 558.15 ; ib.649 ; opp. D.18.93, cf. Isoc.1.6, D.25.24; opp. X.Ages.11.6: pl., Phld.Rh.2.33S

καλοκἄγαθος.definition: an adject. form, perh. only in Poll.4.11 ; orig. denotes a perfect gentleman, Hdt.1.30, Ar.Eq.185, 735, al., Th.4.40, 8.48, X.HG5.3.9, Arist.Pol.1293b39, etc.; X.An.4.1.19; but later in a moral sense, a perfect charac…

καλοσχηματίζομαι.definition: Pass., Astrol., to be grouped in propitious lineation, Cat.Cod.Astr.6.61

καλπάζω.definition: trot, of a horse, A.Fr.145 A, Aq.Je.8.6, Suid

καλύβη.definition: bridal bower, A.R.1.775; sleeping-tent on roof of house, PFlor.335.2

καλύβιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Phld.Acad.Ind.p.54 M., D.H.10.19, Plu.Pomp.73, Alciphr.1.1, D.L.4.19

καλυβοποιέομαι.definition: Med., make oneself a cabin, Str.4.5.2

καλύκειος λίθος.definition: stone found in the head of the fish Hsch

καλύκιον.definition: Dim. of Dsc. ap. Orib.11.1.50, Hsch

καλυκῶπις.definition: like a budding flower in face, i.e. blushing, roseate, h.Cer.8, 420, Ven.284, B.Scol.Oxy.5i 11, Orph.Fr.49ii 23, H.79.2

καλυπτήρ.definition: covering, sheath, Hp.Haem.4; cover, LXXNu.4.13; lid, D.S.18.26: metaph., Secund.Sent.15

καλυπτηρίζω.definition: cover with tiles, Att. fut. IG22.463.71

καλωνυμέομαι.definition: to be in good repute, bear a good name, Heph.Astr.2.32

καλώνυμος.definition: bearing a fair name, IG5.1331 , cf. EM143.22

καμάρα.definition: Ion. anything with an; Medic., hollow near the auditory meatus, Poll.2.86

καμάριον.definition: Dim. of Papers of Amer. Sch.at; Medic., fornix of the brain, Gal.UP8.11

καμαρόω.definition: furnish with a vault, BGU1545.8 :—Pass., to be vaulted, PGrenf.1.21.9 , IG4.203.25

καμάσσω.definition: shake , Hsch.: is prob. f.l. for cf. Id

κάματος.definition: the effect of toil, weariness, Il.4.230, cf. 13.85,711, etc.; 5.811; Od.14.318; 6.2; 9.75, cf. Sapph.Supp.19.4, etc.: in Prose, Aen.Tact.26.8, Parth.1.1, Jul.Or.2.87b

καμήλειος.definition: of a camel: camel's flesh, Porph.Abst.1.14 fin., cf. Gal.8.183; PHolm. 15.18

καμηλέμπορος.definition: one who carries his wares on a camel, of merchants travelling in caravans, Str.17.1.45

καμηλίζω.definition: to be like a camel, Hld.10.27

καμηλοπάρδαλις.definition: camelopard, giraffe, Agatharch.72, LXXDe.14.5, Callix.2, D.C.43.23, Hld.10.27

καμηλών.definition: stable for camels, POxy.507.26 , BGU393.15, etc

καμιναῖος.definition: of or from a furnace, Ezek.Exag.136

καμινευτήρ.definition: = foreg.; the pipe of a smith's bellows, AP6.92 :—fem. Aristarch. ap.Eust.1835.41, Hsch. s.v

καμινευτής.definition: = PPetr.3p.173 (dub; title of priests at Ostia, IG14.914

καμινεύω.definition: heat in a furnace, Arist.Mir.833b25, Thphr.Lap.69, etc.; Str.5.2.6

καμινίτης.definition: baked in an oven, Philistion ap.Ath.3.115e

καμινοκαύστης.definition: one who heats a furnace or; one who burns gypsum in a kiln, BGU952.8

κάμινος.definition: oven, furnace, or kiln, for smelting, baking, burning earthenware and bricks, Hom.Epigr.14, Hdt.1.179, 4.164, A.Fr.281, Critias2.13 D., PPetr.3p.141 , etc.: pl., of Hephaestus' forge, Anacreont.27 A 2; flue for warmin…

καμμύω.definition: Ep. for v.l. in Batr.191: also in later Gr., LXXIs.6.10, al., cf. Ph.1.645, HeroAut.22.1, PMag.Lond.121.855 , Paul.Aeg.3.22.29: pf. A.D.Synt.323.22: cited from Alex.319 by Phryn., but censured as un-Attic

καμπτήρ.definition: bend, angle, X.Cyr.7.1.6; turning-point in the which was the goal in the single race , Arist.Rh.1409a32, BCH23.567 , Babr.29.4: pl., as works of art, Plin.HN36.25: metaph., the 'last lap' of life, Herod.10.3; of the c…

κάμπτρα.definition: case, chest , IG5 .1390.11 , BGU781.12 , Gloss.:—Dim. Gp.10.21.10, Gloss.; cf

καμπυλόομαι.definition: Pass., become curved, Antyll. ap. Aët.7.74

καμπυλόπρυμνος.definition: with rounded stern, Sch.D Il.2.392, Hsch. s.v

κανάσσω.definition: only in aor. inf. and part. pour with a gurgling sound, Hsch.; Poll.10.85: elsewh. only in compds. cf

καναχή.definition: Dor. sharp sound; esp. ring or clang of metal, . . Il.16.105, cf. 794; loud rang their tramp, Od.6.82; gnashing of teeth, Il.19.365, Hes.Sc.164: pl., ib.160; B.13.15; S.Ant.130 ; sound of flutes, Pi.P.10.39 , B.2.12, …

καναχήπους.definition: with sounding feet, of the horse, Certamen100, Opp.C.2.431; Dor. acc. sg. masc. Alcm.23.48

κανηφορέω.definition: carry a basket, Ph.2.55, al.; esp. carry the sacred basket in procession, Ar.Lys.646, al., IG2.1204, al., 3.921; Arist.Ath.18.2; also DurrbachChoix d' Inscriptions de Délos115 ; Plu.2.772a; CIG2298 , cf. 3602

κανηφόρος.definition: carrying a basket: at Athens, title of maidens who carried baskets in procession at festivals, Ar.Ach.242 , al. , Hermipp.26, IG22.896.9 ; represented in works of art, Cic.Verr.4.3.5, Plin.HN36.25; elsewh., as title o…

κανθάρεως.definition: or name of a kind of vine, Thphr.CP2.15.5: Hsch

κανθαρώλεθρος.definition: death-to-beetles, name of a district in Thrace, Arist.Mir.842a6, Str.7Fr.30, Plu.2.473f

καννάβινος.definition: like hemp, AP11.325 ; hempen, Apollod.Poliorc.159.5; Hippiatr.24

κάνναβις.definition: gen. Hdt.4.74, Sor.2.46, Gal.6.549; acc. Moschio ap.Ath.5.206f, Hdt.l.c., Paus.6.26.6:-hemp, Cannabis sativa, S.Fr.243, Hdt.l.c., Dsc.3.148, etc. : in pl., hemp-seed, Ephipp.13.6; burnt and used to medicate vapour bat…

κανόνιον.definition: small bar or rod, Ph.Bel.74.11; tabulation, table, Ptol.Harm.2.15, Gaud.Harm.22, Vett.Val.321sq

κανονίς.definition: acc. to Suid., =; frame with parallel cross-ledges, Arist.Ath.64.2; door-frame, IG22.1672.155

κανονισμός.definition: perh. the frieze of a building, in pl., Man.1.299, 4.151

κανονογραφία.definition: construction of astronomical tables, Ptol.Alm.2.9, Vett.Val.336.12:—also Ptol.Alm.3.1, TheoninPtol. Alm.p.109H., Vett.Val.353.14

καταδακτυλίζω.definition: feel with the finger, sens. obsc., Phryn.PSp.83 B., Sch.Ar.Pax548

καταδαμάζω.definition: subdue, aor. 1 Act. LXXJd.14.18: aor. inf. Med. Th.7.81: aor. Pass., D.C.50.10,78.39

καταδαπανάω.definition: squander, Arist.Pol.1316b23; consume, of an army, X.An.2.2.11; Sotad.15.16:—Pass., LXXWi.5.13; Eun.Hist.p.269D

καταδατέομαι.definition: fut. :—Med., divide; divided, allotted it, Tab.Heracl.2.28

καταδείκνυμι.definition: Ion. aor. discover and make; invent and teach, introduce, Ar.Ra.1079 ; Antiph.123.1, cf. Diod.Com.2.4; Pl.R.407d, cf. 406c; D.25.11; Com.Adesp.106.2: c.inf., show how to do, Hdt.1.171; Aeschin.2.87; D.S.1.45: both con…

καταδειλιάω.definition: show cowardice, D.61.28; spoil by cowardice, X.An.7.6.22

καταδειπνέω.definition: eat at a meal, Plu.2.355c; Ael.VH1.24

καταδερματόω.definition: in Pass., to be covered with hide, Hsch. s.v

καταδεσμεύω.definition: bind up, LXXSi.30.7; bind on, Gp.12.21

κατάδεσμος.definition: tie, band, bathing-drawers; = II, Pl.R.364c, cf. Plot.4.4.40 , PMag.Par.1.2176 ; Artem.1.77

καταδέχομαι.definition: Arc. SIG306.58 (iv; receive back, take home again, esp. from banishment, And.3.3, Lys.6.13, D.26.6, etc.: aor. Pass. in pass. sense, Luc.Bis Acc.31, D.C.78.39: fut. ib.40.40

καταδηϊόω.definition: contr. ravage, waste, in Pass., D.H.11.42

καταδηλέομαι.definition: injure, violate, Men.Prot.p.108 D.: Elean forms Schwyzer 413.8, 6; ib.418.19

καταδημαγωγέω.definition: conquer by the arist of a demagogue, Plu.2.482d, cf.Arr.Fr.150 J.:—Pass., Plu.Per.9; to be won by such arts, Id.Cleom.13, etc

καταδιαιρέω.definition: distribute, D.H.4.19, cf. CPR22.25 :—Med., distribute among themselves, LXXJo.3.2, Plb.2.45.1, D.S.3.29

καταδιαιτάω.definition: decide as arbitrator against one, give judgement against, opp. D.49.19, cf. 21.84; ib.85; give judgement in default against one, Id.21.92, cf. 40.17, Luc.Pr.Im.15: metaph., condemn, c. gen., Alciphr.1.31:—Med., to be …

καταδιαφθείρω.definition: squander, Eup.44; in Pass., to be consumed, Luc.Tim.44

καταδίδωμι.definition: intr., of a channel, open into, Hdt.4.85, cf. Plu.Fab.6

καταδίκη.definition: judgement given against one, sentence; damages or fine, Th.5.49, 50, D.47.52, PHal.1.52 ; IG 12.267.16 , cf. Tab.Heracl.1.156

κατάδικος.definition: having judgement given against one, found guilty, condemned, SIG484.1 : c. gen., to banishment, D.S.13.63; Id.27.1; mulcted in, GDI2516.7 : abs., J.AJ5.1.14, Arr.Epict.4.11.24, App.BC1.2, CIG2759b

καταδιφρεύω.definition: throw down from a chariot, Eust.183.38

καταδολεσχέω.definition: chatter at, weary by chattering, LXXLa.3.20; Plu.2.22a; Jul.Ep.32: pf. Plu.2.503b: abs., PSI5.495.3:— Pass., pf. part. Suid. s.v

καταδοξάζω.definition: form a wrong opinion, Epicur.Nat.2.9, Herc.1413.4; D.H.6.10

καταδουλεύομαι.definition: reduce to slavery, Sm.Le.27.17, f.l. in Eus. Mynd.Fr.10

καταδουλίζω.definition: = foreg., IG9.119 :— but usu. Med., GDI1701.7, al. : aor. IG9.42

καταδουλόω.definition: reduce to slavery, enslave; more freq. in Med., make a slave to oneself, enslave, Hdt.7.51, cf. Pl.R.351b; X.Mem.2.1.13, cf. GDI4982 , PEleph. 3.3 , etc.; Philem.95.8; Eus.Mynd.Fr.10; LXX1 Ma.8.18; ib.Ex.1.14

καταδούλωσις.definition: enslavement, Th.3.10, 7.66, Pl.Lg.776d, GDI 1869.7 , Mémoires de la mission arch. de Perse 20.85

καταδράσσομαι.definition: lay hold of, Dsc.Ther.Praef.; grasp, apprehend, Procl.in Prm.p.534 S.; Id.in Ti.3.107D.; Id.in Alc.p.153 C., cf. Olymp.in Alc.p.194C

καταδρύπτω.definition: tear in pieces, rend, AP5.42 ; ib.7.487 , cf. M.Ant.6.20:—Med., Hes.Sc.243

καταδυναστεύω.definition: oppress, LXXEx.1.13,al; get control, abs., of mutineers, Ps.-Ptol.Centil.56

κατᾴδω.definition: uncontr. sing to: hence; trans., charm, appease by singing, D.H.4.29, Plu.2.745e, Luc.JTr.39, Philops.31: c. dat., sing a spell or incantation to . . , . . Hdt.7.191:—Pass., to be induced by charms to do a thing, c. i…

καταδωροδοκέω.definition: betray in return for bribes, Ar.V.1036, Lys.27.3:—Med., Ar.Ra.361, Arist.Pol.1271a3

καταέννυμι.definition: or Ep. Verb, not found in the form because of the digamma, only in impf., aor. Act., and pf. Pass.:— clothe, cover, Il.23.135; . . Opp.H.2.673:—Pass., Od.13.351, 19.431, h.Merc.228, h.Ven.285; h.Ap.225

καταζεύγνυμι.definition: and yoke together; in Pass., to be straitened, confined, Hdt.8.22; S.Ant.947

καταζευγοτροφέω.definition: squander money on teams of horses, Is.5.43

καταζητέω.definition: search out, Iamb.VP29.158 ; hold inquiry into, Just.Nov.123.18.1, cf. Cod.Just.1.3.41.26

καταζοφόω.definition: in Pass., to be darkened, Sch.E.Hec.912

καταζῶ.definition: live one's life out, live on, E.Ion56, cf. Pl.Smp.192b, Arist.EN1100b16, Plu.2.194a; Phld.Rh.2.162S., Plu.Cic.4

καταζώννυμι.definition: gird fast:—Med., gird for oneself, E.Ba.698; Plu.Pyrrh.27:— Pass., D.H.2.70

κατάημι.definition: Ep. aor. part. = , Hsch.: fut. Id

καταθαλαττόω.definition: throw into the sea, Tz.ad Lyc.712

καταθαμβέομαι.definition: Pass., to be astonished at, c. acc., Plu.Num.15, Fab.26

καταθαρσέω.definition: later Att. to be confident; c. gen., behave boldly against, D.S.15.34; Str.12.8.6

καταθαρσύνω.definition: embolden, encourage against, Plu.Luc.29:—Pass., in form = foreg., Ph.1.41, Luc.DMort.21.2, D.L.2.127: c.gen., title of work by Polystr., cf. Them.Or.34p.464D

καταθεάομαι.definition: look down upon, watch from above, X.An.6.5.30; ib.1.8.14: abs., Id.Cyr.3.2.1: generally, contemplate, Plu.2.426d: metaph., with the mind, X.Cyr.8.2.18

καταθεμελιόω.definition: in Pass., to be founded, based, Lyd.Mens.4.51

καταθερμαίνω.definition: strengthd. for dub.l. in Philagr. ap. Orib.5.21.1

κατάθεσις.definition: layering of branches for; paying down, payment, Ph.2.224, Poll.4.47, 5.103, dub. in CIG2826.17

καταθέω.definition: make inroads, ib.5.2.43: c. acc., overrun, ravage, Th.7.27, X.Cyr.5.4.15; Polyaen.1.23.1

καταθήγω.definition: sharpen, whet, AP6.303 ; = Hsch.: Dor. aor. inf. = Id

καταθηλύνω.definition: make womanish, Luc.Peregr.19, DMeretr.5.3; softened, f.l. in Hp.Aër.15

καταθλάω.definition: aor. 1 crush in pieces, LXXPs.41.11: metaph., ib.Is.63.3

καταθλίβω.definition: press down, Thphr.Ign.23; Sor.1.76; Plu.2.133d; Id.Aem.14

καταθοινάω.definition: feast upon, Hsch.:—aor. Med., Aesop.14, Diogenian.7.52:—aor. Pass. in med. sense, Pancrat. ap. Ath.7.283b

καταθορυβέω.definition: shout down, Pl.Prt.319c:—Act. in Numen. ap. Eus.PE14.6: also c. acc. cogn., ibid

κατάθραυστος.definition: broken in pieces, f.l. in Dsc.5.87

καταθραύω.definition: break in pieces, shatter, Pl.Plt.265d, Ti.56e , Plu.2.949c; Gal.18.471

καταθρηνέω.definition: bewail, E.El.1326 , prob. in Phld.Mort.24: c. acc., D.S.17.118; Plu.2.1103a; App.Pun.81

καταθρύπτω.definition: break in pieces, Nic.Al.61; Artem. ap. Ath.14.663e; D.S.1.83, cf. Dieuch. ap. Orib.Syn.5.33

καταθρῴσκω.definition: aor. 2 leap down, Il.4.79: c. acc., leap down the wall, Hdt.6.134; Id.3.86: c. gen., Nonn.D.23.220

καταιβάσιος.definition: descending, epith. of the; of Apollo, as invoked by those who prayed for a return to their country, Sch.E.Ph.1408, Zen.4.29

καταιβάτης.definition: a name of Zeus as descending; of Hermes, who led souls down to the nether world, Sch.Ar.Pax649

καταιβάτις.definition: steep, downward path, A.R.2.353, 3.160; Lyc.91; Act., that brings down, that brings down the moon by spells, Sosiph.1

καταιγίζω.definition: rush down like a storm; Pass., to be visited by storms, of places, Str.7.4.3, cf. 9.3.15: metaph., Hld.5.24; also, of the sea, Gal.6.709

καταιγίς.definition: squall descending from above, hurricane, Democr.14, Arist.Mu.395a5, AP7.273 , Corn.ND9, Erot. s.v. Gal.18.178, D.C.74.12, Lib.Or.59.138: metaph., of gusts of passion , Phld.Herc.1251.6; of battles, Tz.H.1.984

καταιγισμός.definition: = foreg., in pl., gusts of physical passion, Epicur.Fr.413

καταιδέομαι.definition: fut. aor. Pass. in act; later in Act., put to shame, Hld.4.18, Them.Or.15.191b, f.l. in Plu.2.801f, cf. Hsch., Phot

καταιθαλόω.definition: burn to ashes, . . A.Fr.160; E.Supp.640; Id.Ion215 ; Ar.Av.1242, cf. 1248; Lyc.1376: metaph., of love, Ar.Av.1261:—Pass., E.Tr.60; all burnt and sooty, Luc.DDeor.5.4, cf. Artem.2.10; Hp.Ep.27

καταινέω.definition: poet. aor.1 Pi. :—agree to a; agree, promise to do, c. aor. inf., Pi.P.4.222: c. fut. inf., S.OC1633, cf. 1637; also agree that he should be king, Hdt.1.98; AP9.98

καταιονάω.definition: pour upon or over, foment, of ailing parts, Hp.Mul.1.68, Plu.2.74d: metaph., D.C.38.19:—Pass., Luc.Lex.5

καταιόνησις.definition: = foreg., D.Chr.17.6, M.Ant.5.9, Poll.4.180, Gal.12.675; Ath.1.24d

καταίρω.definition: take down, only in Aeol. form for; intr., come down, swoop, of birds, Ar.Av.1288; Paus.10.15.5; Plu.Rom.9; of bees, Id.2.41f; of persons, X.Eq.Mag.6.5; E.Ba.1294; Pl.Hp.Ma.281a; Plu.Phil.14

καταισιμόω.definition: consume utterly, Eub.15.6 ; to drink it off, Epin.1.10

καταιτιάομαι.definition: accuse, arraign, Hdt.6.14; c. acc. rei, lay something to one's charge, impute, Th.3.42; D.21.118

καταιχμάζω.definition: strike down, c. gen., Nonn.D.21.6, al

κατακαγχάζω.definition: laugh aloud at, AP5.215.6 , cf. Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

κατακαίνω.definition: = kill, in early writers in aor. 2 X.Cyr.4.6.5 , An.3.2.12; 3sg. subj. Anon. in PSI9.1091.4; is required by the metre in S.Ant.1340: pf. part. shd. be read in X.An.7.6.36: pres. in later Prose, Parth.7.2, Arr.Ind.11.1…

κατακαλέω.definition: call down, Plu.Oth.18; but usu. summon; call upon, invoke, App.Pun.81; v.l. Isoc.10.61, cf. Plu.Them.13

κατακαλύπτω.definition: cover up, Il.1.460, cf. Hdt.2.47 ; . . Il.6.464; 16.325; 17.594; A.Pers.917 , cf. Hes.Op.121, E.Tr.1315 , etc.:—Med., having covered his head, Od.8.92; so alone, Hdt.6.67; even one veiled would perceive, Pl.Men.76b; I…

κατάκαρπος.definition: fruitful, Aristodem. ap. Ath.11.495f, LXXHo.14.7. Adv. abundantly, ib.Za.2.4

κατακαρπόω.definition: offer burnt-sacrifices, esp. of fruits, Suid

κατακάρφω.definition: fut. parch up, Hsch.:—Pass., wither, fall into the sere, A.Ag.80

κατάκαυμα.definition: anything burnt: pl., burnt parts; fiery inflammation, Hp.Coac.154, LXXLe.13.24, 25; burns, in pl., Thphr.Ign.57, Dsc.5.123, Crito ap.Gal.13.800, Gp.12.17.11

κατακαυχάομαι.definition: boast against one, exult over him, Ep.Rom.11.18, Eust.ad D.P.Prooem.p.67 B.; Ep.Jac.3.14: metaph., ib.2.13; to glory in it, LXXZa.10.12

κατακαχρύω.definition: fut. Hsch., Phot.: aor. inf. Paus.Gr.Fr.227:—prop. grind roasted corn: metaph., grind, crush, ll. cc

κατάκειμαι.definition: Ep. 3pl. Il.24.527: Ion. plpf; to be deposited, of deeds in a registry, POxy.1040.32 , etc

κατακελευσμός.definition: calling to one, encouraging, name of a part of the Str.9.3.10, Poll.4.84

κατακενόω.definition: strengthd. for LXXGe.42.35; J.BJ1.30.6, cf. Androm. ap. Gal.13.886

κατακεντέω.definition: pierce through, Pl.Ti.76b; prick; shoot down, Zos.5.21

κατακεντρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be furnished with spikes, D.S.18.71

κατακεράννυμι.definition: mix, temper, in Pass., Arist.Pr.949a38, Sor.1.53, Plu.2.132d:—Act., dilute, weaken, Dsc.5.11; cf. also Poll.10.149

κατακερδαίνω.definition: make gain of a thing wrongly, X.Oec.4.7

κατακερματίζω.definition: chop up, cut into pieces, freq. metaph., Pl.Men.79c; Gal.Thras.24; fritter it away, Demetr.Eloc.76; Plu.2.1142b; Str.4.4.2; Gal.1.246:—Pass., to be cut up, Pl.R.395b; . . Id.Prm.144b; cut up into questions and answers…

κατακερτομέω.definition: rail violently, Hdt.1.129; at a person, Id.2.135, Ph.2.440; Nic.Dam.3 J., Polyaen.1.34.2, Longus2.20

κατακηλέω.definition: charm, cast a spell over, S.Tr.1002 :—Pass., Pl.Cra.403e, Plu.Num.20, Ath.4.174b, Dam.Isid.48

κατακηρόω.definition: cover with wax, Hdt.1.140, v.l. in X.Eq.10.7 :—Pass., Hdt.4.71

κατακηρύσσω.definition: Att. proclaim or command by; Pass. also, to be summoned by crier, Poll.8.61

κατακινέω.definition: strengthd. for in Pass., f.l. in Sch.Theoc.5.116

κατακίρνημι.definition: = in Pass., Longin.15.9, AP9.362.12, Iamb.in Nic.p.119P.:—also

κατακισηρίζω.definition: rub smooth with pumice-stone, pf. part. Pass., of an effeminate youth, Ctes.Fr.20

κατάκλεισις.definition: shutting up, closing, Gal.19.445; completion, Nicom.ap.Theol.Ar.43

κατάκλειστος.definition: shut up, of women, Call.Fr.118, cf. LXX2 Ma.3.19, Luc.Tim.15, Hsch.; D.L.6.94; Str.13.1.54; precious, S.E.P.1.143

κατακλείω.definition: old Att. Th. : a rare; c. acc. pers., shut in, enclose, e. g. a mummy in its case, Hdt.2.86: freq. of blockading, Th.1.109; X.Cyr.4.1.18; Id.An.3.4.26; D.H.6.74, 11.26; Ev.Luc.3.20, cf. OGI669.17 : metaph., i.e. not t…

κατακληροδοτέω.definition: seize and parcel out, v.l. in LXX1 Ma.3.36, De.1.38, Act.Ap.13.19

κατακληρονομέω.definition: obtain as one's assured possession, LXXSi.4.16; leave as an inheritance, ib.De.21.16

κατακληρουχέω.definition: receive as one's portion, esp. of a; assign as a portion, D.S.1.54, cf. PLond.2.383.2 ; portion out to colonists, Plu.Ant.55

κατακληρόω.definition: = foreg. 2, D.S.13.2 codd., PSI4.344 :—Med., receive as one's portion, Plu.Pomp.41; draw the lot, LXX1 Ki.14.42; but also ibid

κατάκλησις.definition: summoning by name, Ph.2.388; summoning of the whole body of citizens, incl. rural population, opp. Ammon.Diff.p.47 V

κατακλινής.definition: sloping, Leonid. ap. Stob.4.52.28; D.H.5.38; hanging down, Thphr.CP2.9.11

κατάκλισις.definition: making one to lie down, seating; lying at table, sitting at meat, Arist.Pol.1336b9,21; Pl.Smp.175e; Plu.2.679f, cf. Porph.Abst.2.61

κατάκλιτος.definition: perh. flowing down, of light summer garments, LXXIs.3.23; cf. Hsch

κατακλύζω.definition: metaph., deluge, overwhelm, . . Archil.9.3; . . E.Tr.995; . . Cratin.186; make life overflow with plenty, X.Oec.2.8; deluge with sufferings, E.Or.343 ; . . . . Pl.R.473c:—Pass., of a city, A.Th.1084 ; Pl.R.492c; Plu.D…

κατακλυσμός.definition: metaph., political deluge, D.18.214; Medic . . affusion, douche, Cael. Aur.TP4.1.1

κατακνίζω.definition: chop up, mince, Ath.9.376d; metaph., pick to pieces, Isoc.12.17; Luc.Hes.5

κατακοιμίζω.definition: = II (for which it is a; sleep through, sleep out one's watch, Hdt.9.93. Ael.NA1.15, al.; X.Mem.2.1.30

κατακοιμιστής.definition: one who puts to bed, chamberlain, D.S.11.69, Ph.2.571, Plu.2.173e, Jul.ad Ath.272d, prob. in Ephor.191.131J

κατακοινωνέω.definition: make one a partaker, give one a share, D.32.25; share the public property among themselves, Aeschin.3.66

κατακολουθέω.definition: follow after, LXXJe.17.16, cf. Longus3.15 codd.: c. gen., Dioxipp.p.2 ; comply with, Epicur.Fr.388; obey, LXXDa.9.10, 1 Ma.6.23; Plu.Lys.25; follow a historical or philosophical authority, Phld.Rh.2.146S.; Plb.2.56.2,…

κατακόλουθος.definition: following, of persons, c. dat., Vett.Val.220.4; of things, Id.125.31

κατακολπίζω.definition: run into a bay, Th.8.92, cf. Str.8.3.33

κατακόλπισις.definition: putting into a bay, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

κατακομίζω.definition: bring down, esp.from the inland to the; bring into harbour, D.50.55; Id.56.27; ib.20; bring home, Aeschin.2.71

κατακοντίζω.definition: Att. fut. used also by Hdt.9.17:—shoot down, Id. l.c., Th.8.108, D.18.151, LXXJu.1.15: pf. inf. Pass. Phld.Piet.34; Luc.Tox.59

κατακόπτω.definition: cut down, fell, of trees, in Pass; cut in pieces, cut up, Hdt.1.48,73, 2.42, Ar.Av.1688 , etc.; Pl.Euthd.301c; cut in pieces, Hdt.8.92

κατακορακόω.definition: fasten up, close a sarcophagus, BSA17.225 , Jahresh.23 Beibl. 101

κατακορμίζω.definition: cut wood into logs or pieces, Paus. Gr.Fr.224:—also Hsch

κατακοτταβίζω.definition: squirt or throw wine over any one, Ar.Fr.152

κατακρατέω.definition: prevail over, c. gen. pers; abs., prevail, gain the mastery, gain the victory, A.Pers.101 , cf. Hdt.7.168, Th.6.55, Pl.Lg.840e; Hdt.7.129; of an opinion, D.C.57.15; of planetary influence, predominate, Procl.Par.Ptol.…

κατακρέμαμαι.definition: Pass., hang down, be suspended, Hdt.4.72, Cratin.164; from a thing, Plu.2.672a

κατακρεμάννυμι.definition: hang up, Od.8.67; Aen.Tact.11.6: in med. sense, . . having hung the bow on herself, h.Hom.27.16: Ep.Subj., Nic.Fr.74.42:—Pass., hang down, be suspended, Hp.Fract.21; D.S.18.26

κατακρεμασμός.definition: hanging down: relaxation of the uvula, Apollon. ap. Gal.12.981

κατακρεουργέω.definition: Ion. hew in pieces, as a butcher does meat, Hdt.7.181 , Xanth.12

κατακρήμναμαι.definition: Pass., = Hp.Morb.2.10, Ar.Nu.377: impf. h.Bacch.39, prob. in Dsc.4.46, J.AJ3.7.5

κατακρημνίζω.definition: fut. Carm.Pop.46.33; generally, throw headlong down, X.HG2.1.31; Plb.3.116.12; D.S.4.31:—Pass., X.Cyr.1.4.7

κατακρημνιστής.definition: one who throws headlong down, Gloss

κατάκρημνος.definition: steep and rugged, Batr.154, cf. Gp.18.18.2

κατακριδεύω.definition: chatter like a swarm of locusts, Hsch., Phot

κατάκριμα.definition: condemnation, judgement; punishment, fine, damage, CPR1.16 , PAmh.2.114.8 , Ep.Rom.5.16, 8.1

κατακρίνω.definition: c. acc. pers., condemn, v.l. in Antipho4.4.2: c. acc. et inf., Hdt.6.85, cf. 9.93, Theoc.23.23 ; Ev.Matt.20.18, cf. J.BJ5.13.1; IG5.1390.161 : c. acc. rei, deem guilty of a thing, Arist.Rh.Al.1423b29; J.AJ3.14.4:—Pass…

κατακρίσιμος.definition: of a case, ready to be judged, Sammelb. 5230.18

κατάκρισις.definition: condemnation, 2 Ep.Cor.3.9, 7.3; judgement, a false estimate, Gal.5.76

κατάκριτος.definition: condemned, sentenced, D.S.33.2, cf. Plu.2.188b; to death, Luc.Am.52, cf. 23, 36; Ph.2.411

κατακροάομαι.definition: listen attentively to, Eup.245; J.BJ4.1.5, Anon. in Gött.Nachr.1922.33

κάτακρος.definition: strengthd. for Sch.DIl.15.536. Adv. Anon.Prog.inRh.1.627 W

κατακροταλίζω.definition: make a loud rattling noise, Call.Dian.247

κατακρουνίζω.definition: pour down over, Archestr.Fr.13.8; of a douche or shower-bath, Philum.Ven.5.3, Gal.10.935:—Pass., to have water poured over one, D.L.6.41

κατακρούω.definition: knock, Gp.10.61; make narrow incisions or 'stabbings', Hp.Ulc.24, 25, Medic.7

κατακτάομαι.definition: fut. LXX2 Ch.28.10:—get for; Pass., possessed by . . , Phld.Vit.Herc.1457.10: aor., D.S.16.56

κατακυβεύω.definition: pf. D.C.45.28:—gamble away; Pass., also, to be beaten in play, Eust.1396.54

κατακυκλόω.definition: encompass, encircle, in Pass., J.BJ3.8.6 , Gal.18.787

κατακυλίνδω.definition: or , roll down, D.H.11.26, LXXJe.28.25:—Med., Arr.Tact.11.6:—Pass., to be rolled down or thrown off, Hdt.1.84, 5.16; X.Cyr.5.3.1:—pres. J.BJ4.1.10; impf. D.C.56.14

κατακυριεύω.definition: gain or exercise complete dominion; gain dominion over, gain possession of, ib.Ps.9.26 , 1 Ep.Pet.5.3; D.S.14.64

κατακυρόω.definition: confirm, ratify, Arist.Ath.47.2; confirm a contract with a tax-farmer, J.AJ12.4.4:—Pass., to be ratified, Thphr.Fr.97.1; to be fulfilled, S.Ant.936 ; condemned to death, E.Or.1013

κατακωλύω.definition: hinder from doing, c. acc. et inf., Simon.41, cf. Ar.Ach.1088; detain, keep back, X.Oec.12.1, D.53.5; X.An.5.2.16; . . Pherecr.153.7:—Pass., c. gen. rei, D.33.13

καταλαβεύς.definition: holder, nail, in pl., Hsch., Phot

καταλαγνεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be very lewd, Hsch

καταλαγχάνω.definition: hold possession of, dub. l. in Ael.NA9.35

καταλαζονεύομαι.definition: boast, brag largely; exaggerate invidiously, Isoc.15.5, 31

καταλαλέω.definition: pf. A.D.Synt.323.7:—talk, babble; talk down, rail at, IG9.338.6 ; Plb.3.90.6; Id.18.45.1; D.S.11.44; 1 Ep.Pet.2.12; LXXHo.7.13; ib.Ps.49.20:—Pass., Plb.27.13.2; to be outdone in speech, Phld.Rh.1.343S

καταλαμβάνω.definition: fut. Pl.Prt.311a (in pass.sense; of death, fatigue, disaster, etc., . . Il.5.82; . . . . Od.17.326: c. dupl. acc., 1.192; Heraclit.28; befall, overtake, E.Hipp.1161: freq.in Hdt., 2.66; ibid., cf. 3.42; may be expecte…

καταλγύνω.definition: grieve very much, in Pass., Hsch

καταλειτουργέω.definition: Att. spend one’s substance in bearing the public burdens, D.36.39:-Pass., prob. in Is.Fr.130 S. ; BCH44.91

καταλεπτύνω.definition: make very thin, in Pass., Hp.Aër.7; Arist.PA668a22, cf. Gal.18.18, 25

καταλεύω.definition: stone to death, Hdt.1.167, al., Ar.Ach.285; condemn to work in mines, Hsch

καταλέχομαι.definition: pres. only in Cypr. imper. , = Hsch. ; Ep. only in Med. and Pass. fut. and aor.:—lie down, go to bed: aor. 1 Il.9.690, Od.10.555: non- thematic aor. Pass. Il.9.662, etc.; part. Od.22.196; inf. 15.394: fut. Hes.Op.523

καταλέω.definition: aor. 1 grind, Od.20.109; Hecat.323 J., cf. Hdt.4.172, Hp.VM3, Ph.Bel.88.46, Str.6.1.8; LXXEx.32.20:—Pass., Ph.1.257

καταληπτέος.definition: to be seized or; one must cover with a plaster, Philum. ap. Orib.Syn.8.3, Philum.Ven.3.5

καταληπτήρ.definition: strap for holding fast, Hsch; clamp, BCH29.468

καταληρέω.definition: lose by idle talking, Eub.53; overpower with talk, Jul.Ep.32: abs., Ach.Tat.7.11

καταλιμπάνω.definition: = Hp.Mul.1.78, Th.8.17, Antiph.35, PPetr.3pp.4,12 , LXXGe.39.16, Ocell.4.13, etc

καταλλαγή.definition: exchange, esp. of money; money-changer's profit, agio, D.50.30, Diph.66.14, Euphro3.4

καταλλακτήριος.definition: reconciliatory, Ph.1.673; fem. as epith. of Aphrodite, Milet.7.19

καταλλάκτης.definition: money-changer, EM137.24; reconciler, mediator, J.AJ3.15.2, D.C.Fr.72.1

κατάλληλος.definition: set over against one another; appropriate, Arr.Epict.1.9.9, cf. Zos.4.53; M.Ant.5.8. Adv. prob. f.l. for Arist.Metaph.1041a33, cf. Stoic.3.42; Arr.Epict.1.22.9

καταλοάω.definition: crush in pieces, make an end of, c. acc., X.Cyr.7.1.31, Aeschin.2.140:—Pass., Eub.15.5; Luc.Icar.15; cf

καταλογή.definition: I.3) enrolment, enlistment; I.2b) regard, respect, Plb.22.12.10 codd. , cf. SIG739.9 ; honoris causa, with gen., IG7.413.37 ; 'saving your reverence', prob. for Hsch.; on my recommendation, used in letters of introduc…

καταλογίζομαι.definition: count up, reckon, X.An.5.6.16; count, reckon among, X.Mem.2.2.1:—Pass., LXXIs.14.10, Wi.5.5

κατάλογος.definition: enrolment, register, catalogue; at Athens, register of citizens liable for service, Ar.Eq.1369; those on the list for service, Th.6.43, al.; X.Mem.3.4.1; Id.HG2.4.9; the superannuated, opp. D.13.4; of trierarchs, Id.1…

καταλούομαι.definition: Med., spend in bathing, [prob. cj. for Ar.Nu.838

καταλοχίζω.definition: distribute into Ael.Tact.2.4, Arr.Tact.5.2: generally, distribute, D.S.18.70; Plu.Lyc.16; Id.Sull.18; . . . Lib.Ep.36.1 :—Pass., Plu.Cic.15

καταλοχισμός.definition: register, enrolment, LXX1 Ch.4.33; register of grants of land to military settlers, PPetr.3p.230 , cf. POxy.45 , etc

καταλυκουργίζω.definition: press the laws of Lycurgus against, Alciphr.2.1

καταλυμαίνομαι.definition: Dep., ruin utterly, destroy, X.Oec.2.13,6.5; Plb.5.9.3

καταλυμακόομαι.definition: Pass., to be silted up, Tab.Heracl.1.56

καταλύσιμος.definition: to be dissolved or done away, S.El.1247

κατάλυσις.definition: dissolution, putting down, esp. of; dismissal, disbanding of a body of men, X.Cyr.6.1.13; breaking up of a ship's crew, D.50.11; till dismissal, of soldiers at a review, X.Eq.Mag.3.12

καταλυτέος.definition: neut., one must put down, D.S.14.65; one must rest, Suid. s.v

καταμαγγανεύω.definition: subdue by sorceries, gloss on Hsch

καταμαθηματικεύω.definition: reduce to mathematical terms, in Med., Phlp.in de An.481.34

καταμαίνομαι.definition: aor. Pass. do mad acts against, Ph.2.542, cf. J.BJ7.8.1

καταμαλακίζω.definition: in Pass., to be or become soft or effeminate, X.Oec.11.12, Arist.MM1202b37, 1203b7

καταμαλάσσω.definition: Att. soften, Luc.Anach.24: metaph., appease, Id.JTr.24, Ach.Tat.6.19; Hld.7.21

καταμανθάνω.definition: learn, acquire knowledge of, Pl.Tht.198d, etc.; how to obey, v.l. in X.Oec.13.7

καταμαντεύομαι.definition: foretell against or about one; divine, surmise, Arist.Rh.1368a31; Plb.2. 22.7, etc.: c. gen., Hp.Art.9; Ath.14.634d; Hierocl.in CA10p.437M.; . . Nicostr. ap.Stob.4.22.102, cf. Gal.15.907; Onos.36.2

καταμαραίνω.definition: aor. Ph.1.266:—cause to wither, Thphr.Ign.10, Ph.l.c.; make lean, Luc.Tim.17:—Pass., die away, of dropsical swellings, Hp.Prorrh.2.6; Arist.Resp.479a14, cf. Thphr.HP5.9.3, etc.; Arist.Mete.368a7; of persons, . . Plu.2…

καταμαργάω.definition: Ion. to be stark mad, rave, Hdt.8.125

καταμαρτυρέω.definition: bear witness against; Pass., of evidence, to be given against one, Is.5.25, cf. 6.15: abs., D.29.55

καταματτεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be tickled, Hp.Int.6, 27 :—also Gal.19.109; Hp.Int.12

καταμάχομαι.definition: pf. Plu.Flam.3:—subdue by fighting, conquer, l.c.; Paus.6.11.2: metaph., overcome, D.S.3.47

καταμεγαλαυχέομαι.definition: strengthd. for in aor., Hsch. exalt oneself against, Aq., Thd., Sm.Ps.40.10

καταμεθύσκω.definition: aor. causal, make drunk, Hdt.1.106, Pl.Grg.471b, etc.; Archyt. ap. Stob.3.1.114:—Pass., to be made quite drunk, D.S.4.84: abs., get drunk, Plb.5.39.2

καταμείβω.definition: in Pass., to be divided between, f.l. in EM358.44

καταμείγνυμι.definition: or mix in, combine, Ar.Lys.580; . . Id.Nu.230; D.30.10; Id.25.63; Plu.2.148a; ib.648c; Id.Lyc.27:—Pass., Hp.Aër.8; Arist.Spir.485b10; i.e. were mingled with the citizens, X.An.7.2.3; Plu.Cat.Ma.20

καταμελαίνω.definition: make black, darken, in Pass., Agath.5.3

καταμελετάω.definition: train fully, exercise; study carefully, for the purpose of composing, Id.Clit.410b; Phld.Rh.1.236S.; Them.Or.26.312b

καταμελέω.definition: give no heed to, c. gen., Hp.Art.14, cf. X.Oec.4.7, J.AJ18.6.9 ; neglect, BGU195.19 : folld. by relat. clause, Eup.352: abs., pay no heed, S.Aj.45, 912 , Pl.Ti.44c, D.S.29.3 , etc.: c. acc., ruin by neglect, X.HG6.2.3…

καταμέμφομαι.definition: fut. Phld.Oec.p.74J.: aor. Pass. in act. sense, Pi N.11.30; also in pass. sense, Sammelb.5357.11 :—find fault with; esp. with a sense of distrust in oneself, Pi.l.c.; Isoc.15.61, cf. 5.110; Th.8.106, cf. D.22.27; . . …

καταμένω.definition: fut. Men.Epit.197:—stay, Thgn.1373; remain fixed, continue in a state, X.Cyr.2.1.18; Gal.6.328; Id.2.27; Nymphod.21: abs., X.Cyr.3.1.30

καταμέρισις.definition: division into parts, Epicur.Ep.2p.48U.; distribution, Metrod.Herc.831.10

καταμέστιος.definition: poet. for sq., quite full, Nic.Al.45

καταμεστόω.definition: fill quite full of a thing, Pherecr.145.28

καταμετρέω.definition: measure exactly, be the measure of, Arist.Ph.237b28 ; aliquot parts, Id.Metaph.1023b15:—Pass., Id.Cat.4b33: esp. in Metric, of feet or rhythms, D.H.Comp.17, cf. Dem.39

καταμηλόω.definition: put in the probe, so as to sound wounds; plunge them into dyestuff, Poll.7.169

καταμήνιος.definition: monthly, of wages, IG12.339.30, al; hired by the month, BGU1521 , POxy.2155.8

καταμηνύω.definition: point out, make known; inform against, Lys.13.49, cf. D.24.60; also D.H.4.43:—Pass., ib.62, cf. Cod.Just.10.11.8.4

καταμιαίνω.definition: defile, Pi.P.4.100; Pl.Lg.937d; Luc.Cat.27:—Pass., wear squalid garments as a sign of grief, Hdt.6.58

καταμισθοφορέω.definition: spend in paying etc., Ar.Eq.1352, v. Sch.; in paying mercenaries, Aeschin.2.131; Theopomp. Hist.90; D.H.Dem.20: c. dat., Id.4.23

καταμονομαχέω.definition: conquer in single combat, Plu.Thes.11, Ael.VH10.22

καταμπέχω.definition: and encompass, i.e. bury him, E.Hel.853; full of green herbs, i.e. either fed on grass or stuffed with herbs, Antiph.1; cover, Plu.Crass.11

καταμυκτηρίζω.definition: mock with upturned nose, gloss on Paus.Gr.Fr.209:—Pass., Hsch. s.v

καταμυττωτεύω.definition: make mincemeat of, in pf. Pass., Ar.Pax247

καταμύω.definition: Ep. aor. inf. v.l. in Batr.191; aor. etc., also in later Gr., v. the eyes, X.Cyn.5.11; Hp.Epid.7.83; LXX ; Ph.1.645, cf. 2.414; M.Ant.4.29: more freq. alone, close the eyes, Str.6.1.14; Philostr.VA6.11: hence, drop as…

καταμφιέννυμι.definition: clothe completely, cover all round, J.AJ8.5.2

καταμφικαλύπτω.definition: strengthd. for put all round, Od.14.349

καταμωκάομαι.definition: mock at, c. gen., Plu.Demetr.13, Epict.Ench.22: c. acc., Anon. ap. Suid.: abs., LXX2 Ch.30.10, Hld.7.25, Sch.A.R.3.791

καταμωλύνομαι.definition: Pass., = of uicers, Hp.Prorrh.1.170, f.l. in Id.Epid.2.2.6

καταμωλωπίζω.definition: cover with weals or stripes, Suid

καταναγκάζω.definition: force back, esp. of dislocated or; overpower by force, constrain, E.Ba.643; torture, Luc.Nec.4

κατανάγκασις.definition: reduction of dislocated limbs, Hp.Art.48, al

κατανάγκη.definition: means of constraint: spell; kind of vetch, Ornithopus compressus, used in making philtres, Dsc.4.131, Plin.HN27.57, PMag.Osl.1.370

κατανάθεμα.definition: curse, Apoc.22.3; and curse, Ev.Matt.26.74, both vv.ll. for

καταναισιμόω.definition: use quite up, in Pass., Hp.Art.11, Gland.3

καταναλίσκω.definition: impf. Isoc.1.18: plpf; consume, Arist.GA763a13, Plu.2.160b; devour fuel, of fire, Arist.Juv.469b29; later, eat, Agatharch.109; Apollod.1.5.3:—Pass., Arist.GA771a28,725b31, cf. Hp.VM11; Andronic.Rhod.p.578 M

καταναρκάομαι.definition: Ion. Pass., grow quite; Act., to be slothful towards, press heavily upon . . , 2 Ep.Cor.11.9, 12.13

καταναυμαχέω.definition: conquer in a sea-fight, beat at sea, And.3.5, cf. D.20.68, X.HG7.1.10, Din.1.75, TAM2.265 :— Pass., Isoc.12.105, cf. Luc.Hist.Conscr.38

κατανδρίζομαι.definition: fight manfully against, expld. by Hsch

κατανεανιεύομαι.definition: prevail over by youthful vigour, or exult over, Hsch

κατανεκρόω.definition: kill, prob. in Tab.Defix.Aud.16Fr.x 13; deaden, Lyd.Mens.4.67

κατανέμω.definition: distribute, allot, freq. of pasture land; distribute, divide into portions, distributed or apportioned them in ten groups among the tribes, Hdt.5.69, cf. Decr. ap. D.59.104: without Prep., X.Cyr.7.5.13; Pl.Criti.113e;…

κατανέω.definition: aor. heap, pile up, Hdt.6.97; spin out, in pf. Pass., Hsch. s.v

κατανθίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be decked with bright colours, D.S.18.26; Callistr.Stat.7; Hierocl.in CA17p.458M

κατανθρακόω.definition: fut. burn to cinders; elsewh. only in Pass., S.El.58; . . E.IA1602; I have it burnt out, Id.Cyc.663

κατανθρωπίζω.definition: treat in a friendly manner, BGU1141.5

κατανιάω.definition: strengthd. for Hsch. s.v. Id. s.v

κατανικάω.definition: strengthd. for S.Fr.84, cf. J.AJ3.2.2, PFlor.338.11 ; Philum.Ven.4.3

κατανίσσομαι.definition: go or come down from, A.R.2.976; go through, c. acc., Hermesian.7.65

κατανίσταμαι.definition: aor. pf. up against, Plb.1.46.10, 38.12.7: abs., Id.38.13.1; LXXNu.16.3

καταντάω.definition: come down to, arrive; in a speech or narrative, come to, arrive at a point, Plb.4.1.8; Id.10.37.3; D.S.1.79, cf. J AJ3.10.4, etc.; have recourse to, Epicur.Ep.3p.63U.; Phld.Lib.p.62 O

κατάντημα.definition: end, goal, LXXPs.18.7, Sch. Ar.Ra.1026; Sch.E.Hec.744; result, PSI6.698.5

καταντιβολέω.definition: entreat earnestly, Ar.Fr.625: c. inf., J.BJ1.6.4, al

καταντλέω.definition: pour water or liquid down one's throat; bathe, Gal.8.366; J.AJ8.4.1:—Pass., Id.BJ4.9.10

κατάντλησις.definition: = foreg., Hp.Medic.3, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.23.1, Gal.10.237

κατανύσσω.definition: stab, gouge, Phleg.36.4J.:—elsewh. in Pass., with fut. LXXSi.20.21: aor. ; to be sorely pricked, metaph., Act.Ap.2.37, cf. LXXGe.34.7: hence, to be bewildered, stunned, LXXIs.47.5, cf. Ps.4.5, al.; keep silence, ib.Le…

κατανυστάζω.definition: aor. Poll.2.67:—doze, fall; trans., lull asleep, dub. in Ael.NA14.20

κατανωτίζομαι.definition: carry on one's back, Plu.2.924d; turn one's back upon: hence, ignore, disdain, reject, BGU1296.9 , PFay.11.21 , Phld.Mort.35; of critics, Simp.in Ph.1036.17, al., Dam.Isid.150

καταξαίνω.definition: fut. LXXJd.8.7:—card, comb well; tear in pieces, rend in shreds, E.Ion1267; . . Lyc.300; LXX l.c.; Plu.Agis2; so pound him to red rags, Ar.Ach.320:—Pass., . . crushed to atoms, S.Aj.728; E.Ph.1145; Id.Supp.503; Id.HF2…

καταξενόομαι.definition: Pass., to be received as a guest, hospitably treated, A.Ch.706

καταξηραίνω.definition: dry up, Arist.GA772a12; LXXJo.2.10:— Pass., Pl.Ti.76a, Arist.Mete.340b1

κατάξηρος.definition: very dry, parched, Hp.Prorrh.1.3, cf. Arist.de An.422b5, Thphr.CP6.18.3, etc.; Alciphr.3.35: metaph., LXXNu.11.6; Alciphr.1.22; of persons, stale, Plu.2.8c. Adv. Antyll. ap. Orib.9.23.6

καταξιοπιστέομαι.definition: demand implicit belief to the prejudice of, Plb.12.17.1

καταξύω.definition: scrape down, Hp.VC19, Sor.2.12, Gal.10.132; scratch, mark, Luc.Nigr.27; inscribe, Hymn.Is.11

καταπάγιον.definition: fixed payment, IG12.572 . Adv. constantly, Isoc.15.156

καταπαίζω.definition: fut. , jest, mock at, c; deceive, LXXJe.9.5

καταπαλαίω.definition: throw in wrestling, Ar.Ach.710: metaph., overthrow, E.IA1013; Pl.R.362d; S.E.M.8.475:—Pass., Luc.Cont.8

καταπάλλομαι.definition: Pass., dart down, . . Il.19.351 ; PMag.Berol.2.95: aor. 1, leapt down from, Nonn.D.18.13. Hsch.; of a waterfall, AP9.326 cod. : nisi leg. v

καταπαλταφεσία.definition: discharging of catapults, artillery practice, IG 22.1006.65, 12.647.25

καταπάλτης.definition: engine of war for hurling; bolt, shot, Hp.Epid.5.95, 7.121, Hsch.:—hence , of or belonging to catapults, IG22.1487.102; Plb.11.11.3, cf. Str.17.3.15, Bito62.4; = Plb.9.41.5; artillery, D.S.14.42

καταπαννυχίζω.definition: pass the night in revelry, Alciphr.1.39

καταπάομαι.definition: gain possession of, in aor. 1 Hsch

καταπασσαλεύω.definition: Att. nail down: hence, bewitch, SIG 1261.17

καταπάσσω.definition: c. acc. rei, sprinkle, strew over, Hp.Fist.3; Arist.HA627b20; Ar.Nu.177:—Med., on his own head, J.BJ2.21.3 ; v.l. in LXXJb.1.20; Luc.Asin.7

καταπατέω.definition: trample under foot, Th.7.84, etc; metaph., Il.4.157; Pl.Lg.714a; Id.Grg.484a; Ep.Hebr.10.29; Lib.Ep.14.1

καταπάτησις.definition: trampling on, ib.4 Ki.13.7; perambulation, inspection, CPHerm.7 ii6

κατάπαυσις.definition: stopping: metaph., putting down; rest, calm, LXXIs.66.1, al.; place of rest, ib.Ps.94.11, al.; Thphr.Vent.18: metaph., allaying, Phld. Mus.p.86 K

καταπαυστήριον.definition: means of putting to rest, gloss on Sch.S.Tr.575

καταπεδάω.definition: fetter, hamper, Il.19.94; Od.11.292 , cf. Mosch.2.4

κατάπειρα.definition: attack, of disease, Philum.Ven.1.4, Orib.Fr.76, Paul.Aeg.3.78, 5.3

καταπειράζω.definition: fut. Lys.30.34:— make an attempt; c. gen., make trial of, Plb.4.11.6, 4.13.5, cf.PAmh.2.134.3 :—also in Med., Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.40.5

καταπειράομαι.definition: Pass., to be much tried; Med., v.l. for in Ph.2.567

καταπειρασμός.definition: attack, of disease, Dsc.Ther.3, cf. Philum.Ven.4.11: in pl., skirmishes, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

καταπειρατηρία.definition: Ion. sounding- line, Hdt.2.5, 28; catapirātes in Lucil.Fr.1191 Marx; anchor-cable, prob. in CIL8.27790

καταπείρω.definition: insert, Sor.2.62; Hld.10.32:—Pass., Gal.Nat.Fac.1.14; Paul. Aeg.6.32; of persons, Phalar.Ep.147.4. · , dub. in Hsch.)

καταπελεκάω.definition: hew with an axe, in Pass., Sch.Il.16.642

καταπελματόομαι.definition: Pass., to be cobbled, clouted, of shoes, LXXJo.9.5

καταπέμπω.definition: send down, Hes.Th.515; esp. from; send from head-quarters, dispatch, D.12.13; as general, Plu.Flam.15; Luc.DDeor.20.6; Hdn.2.12.3

καταπέρδομαι.definition: only in aor. 2 Act. wind at, in sign of contempt, Epicr.11.28 , Ar.Pax547; Id.V.618; Id.Pl.618

καταπερίειμι.definition: surpass, have the advantage of, Plb.5.67.2

καταπηδάω.definition: leap down, X.Cyr.7.1.38, cf. LXXGe.24.64, BGU1201.12 , Plu.Caes.49; Charito5.3; Aen.Tact.22.19

καταπημαίνω.definition: hurt, damage, in aor. 1 opt. Hsch., Phot

καταπιαίνω.definition: fatten, in Pass., Pl.Lg.807a, cf. Ael.VH9.13, PFlor.130.1

καταπίμελος.definition: very fat or rich, of persons or lands, Dsc.1.24, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.4, Gal.19.451; Dsc.2.76

καταπίμπλημι.definition: fill quite full, dub. l. in Lync.1.16; c. acc. et gen., fill full of, Plu.2.715a; Ph.1.411, cf. 2.558:—Pass., Pl.R.496d: also c. dat., . . Antiph.183.4:—Med., their own tents, Plu.Brut.47

καταπίμπρημι.definition: fut. D.C.39.9: pf. Id.59.16:— burn to ashes, AP11.131 , Ph.1.516, Plu.Cam.22, Polyaen.8.65, Hdn.8.1.4, Jul.Or.2.62d:—Pass., Plb.14.4.10; Luc.Par.57

καταπίνω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.693, later; abs., swallow, Hp.Aph.4.35, cf. Gal.Nat.Fac.3.6

καταπιστεύω.definition: trust, Plb.2.3.3; entrust, Zos.1.36, 3.2; Id.1.5; c. inf., Sammelb. 5273.4 :—Pass., to be entrusted, POxy.136.8 : also in pf. part., devoted, Phalar.Ep.93.1

καταπιστόομαι.definition: Med., become security, for one to another, Plu.Cleom.21

καταπίστωσις.definition: assurance, pledge of faith, of lovers, Arist.Fr.97, cf. Plu.2.258b

κατάπλασις.definition: plastering or poulticing, Hp.VC13, cj. in Sor.1.73

κατάπλασμα.definition: plaster, poultice, Hp.Art.40 , Ar.Fr.320.12, Arist.Pr.863a6, Thphr.HP9.11.4, Od.59, PLit.Lond. 170 , etc

καταπλάσσω.definition: Medic., plaster or poultice, Hp.VC13, al.; also, apply as a plaster or poultice, in Pass., Dsc.4.87, 88: metaph., c. gen., Ph.1.455

καταπλίσσομαι.definition: Pass., to be tripped up, will be tripped up, beaten by our chorus, dub. in Ar.Fr.198.3, cf. Hsch. s.v

καταπλύνω.definition: wash out, remove by washing, Arist.Mete.357b5:—Pass., Thphr.CP3.24.3: metaph., the affair is washed out, has become worthless, Aeschin.3.178, cf. Poll.7.38

κατάπλωσις.definition: Ion. for home-coming by sea, Herod.1.68

καταπνέω.definition: Ep. blow or breathe upon or over; inspire, . . A.Ag.105 ; Ael.NA12.2,7: c. acc. pers., E.Rh.387:—Pass., Ph.1.411

κατάπνιξις.definition: choking, smothering, opp. ib.966b36, cf. Thphr.HP5.9.4, Sud.9

καταποικίλλω.definition: deck with various colours or in divers; metaph., of style, Isoc.13.16, Phld. Rh.1.167S.; also of historians, Agath.Praef.p.136D

καταπολεμέω.definition: war down, i.e. exhaust by war, reduce; simply, make war against, Phld.Piet.54: abs., carry on warfare, Plu.Caes.26

καταπολεύω.definition: revolve, . . Sch.Arat.147; of the constellation move downwards in an orbit, opp. PMag.Par.1.702

καταπολιτεύομαι.definition: subdue or reduce by policy, D.19.315, Plu.Pomp.51, Galb.20, etc

καταπομπός.definition: one who conveys or delivers, c. gen., POxy.1415.5 , etc

καταπονέω.definition: handle roughly, crush, damage, Thphr.HP8.7.5; maltreat, oppress, esp. in Pass., Arist.Fr.575, BGU1188.17 , cf. Act.Ap.7.24, Diog.Oen.1

κατάπονος.definition: tired, wearied, Plu.Sull.29; laboured, of poetry or works of art, Id.Tim.36; wearisome, LXX3 Ma.4.14; Phld.D. 3.13

καταποντίζω.definition: throw into the sea, plunge or drown therein, Lys.14.27, D.23.169, Plu.2.403c, etc.: metaph., Axiop.6 ; Lib.Or.49.10:—Pass., v.l. in Plb.2.60.8; D.S.18.20; Ev.Matt.18.6; Plu.Tim.13; sink, Ev.Matt.14.30; of a ship, PPet…

καταποντιστής.definition: one who throws into the sea, of pirates, Isoc.12.226, D.23.166, 167, cf. Jul.Or.6.201b: metaph., Paus.8.52.3, cf. Lib.Or.63.17

καταποντόω.definition: = Hdt.1.165, 4.154, Xenarch.2.5, etc.; Hdt.3.30; Polem.Hist.54; Philostr.VA1.13:—Pass., Antipho5.28, Pl.Grg.511e, Ph.1.264, 394, Plu.Cat.Mi.11

καταπορεύομαι.definition: come back from banishment, Plb.4.17.8; return home, LXX2 Ma.11.30, 3 Ma.4.11

καταπορνεύω.definition: prostitute, Hdt.1.94; violate, treat as prostitutes, Plu.2.821d, Ael.VH9.8:—Pass., prob. in POxy.1241 iii 11

κατάποτον.definition: pill, bolus, v.l. for in Hp.Acut.70, Mul.2.133, cj. for in Thphr.HP9.20.2: in pl., things swallowed, Aret.CA2.2:—Dim. little pill, Hp. ll. cc., Thphr.HP9.8.3, Ruf. ap.Orib.7.26.125, Archig.ib.8.2.30, POxy.2144.4 , etc

καταπραγματεύω.definition: Act. and Med., c. gen., sine expl., Suid

καταπράσσω.definition: Att. accomplish, execute; construct, build, IG12.478.2

καταπραΰνω.definition: fut. Hsch.: Ep. and Ion. opp. Pl.Ti.67a: usu. metaph., soften down, appease, Pl.Euthd.288b, A.R.1.265, Q.S.14.328; of an orator, Isoc.4.13, cf. Arist.Rh.1380b30; Plb.5.52.14; Plu.Them.31:—Pass., to be pacified, of ani…

καταπρεσβεύω.definition: undertake an embassy against, Str.17.1.11: abs., Plb.22.11.8

καταπρηνής.definition: down-turned, opp. in Hom. always of the hand as used in striking or grasping, . . with the flat of his hand, Il.16.792, cf. Od.13.164; Il.15.114; Od.19.467; Hp.Fract.40

καταπρηνίζω.definition: throw headlong down, . . Nic.Th.824, cf. Nonn.D.4.395

καταπροδίδωμι.definition: betray utterly, leave in the lurch, Hdt.7.157, 8.94, Ar.V.1044, Th.1.86, 7.48, etc.; Hdt.9.73; Lys.20.6:—Pass., Th.3.111

καταπροΐεμαι.definition: Med., throw away, abandon, Plb.1.77.3, etc.; Id.3.81.4, cf. PRev.Laws 27.11 , PTeb.27.61 ; Phld.Mort.5; Plu.Arist.4; Procop.Arc.1 : aor. Poll.8.143

καταπροΐξομαι.definition: Att. in early writers; c. gen. pers., he shall not escape me unpunished, Archil.92; . . Ar.Nu.1240; . . Id.V.1396

καταπρονομεύω.definition: carry off as booty, LXXNu.21.1, Jd.2.14

καταπροτείνομαι.definition: hold out as a pretence, Gal.5.92

καταπροτερέω.definition: get the better of, D.S.17.33; seize a favourable opportunity, Men.Prot.p.102 D.:—Pass., to be beaten, yield, Plb.1.47.9, 16.19.1

καταπτερόω.definition: furnish with wings, E.Melanipp.Sap.Prol.15, cf. Apollod.1.6.3

καταπτύω.definition: spit upon or at, esp. as a mark of abhorrence or contempt, c. gen., D.18.200, cf. Aeschin.3.73, Luc.Cat.12, etc.; Aeschin.2.23; Luc.Icar.30: abs., Ar.Ra.1179. [On the quantity, v

κατάπτωσις.definition: fall, Hp.Art.42; Medic., collapse, Gal.10.837; of epileptic seizures, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.64, cf. Vett.Val.38.13 : hence of a spell which induces a trance, PMag.Par.1.850

καταπτωχεύω.definition: reduce to beggary, beggar, Plu.Cat.Mi.25:—Pass., to be or become beggared, Id.Cic.10; beggared fortunes, D.H.9.51

καταπυγίζω.definition: to be or act like a Phot

κατάπυγος.definition: = , Hsch., Phot., prob. in Gerhard Phoinix p.7 : Comp. Sophr.63: Sup. Epigr.Gr.1131

καταπυγοσύνη.definition: unnatural lust, Cratin.53, Ar.Nu.1023 , Fr.130, Luc.Gall.32

καταπύγων.definition: in Att., the middle finger , Poll.2.184

καταπυκάζω.definition: cover over, Hsch. s.v. : metaph., Eust.1379.12

καταπυκνόω.definition: stud thickly, Plb.8.5.6; force into a small compass, compress, condense, Damox.2.62; spent four talents in a lump, ib.4; to illustrate this is cited the dogma of Epicur.,Sent.9, cf. Plu.2.510f:—Pass., Porph.Plot.14; a…

καταπύκνωσις.definition: in Music, close packing of the intervals in a scale, Aristox.Harm.p.7 M., Nicom.Harm.11

καταπυκτεύω.definition: conquer in boxing, Sch.A.R.2.98 , cj. in Pl. Com.124

καταπυρπολέω.definition: waste with fire, Ar.Th.243 , Plb.5.19.8, Palaeph.52 , Phalar.Ep.104

κατάρα.definition: Ion. curse, to lay curses upon one, Hdt.1.165; . . . . ib.82; in consequence of . . , Id.4.30; E.Hec.945 , cf. El.1324 , A.Th.725 ; opp. Pl.Alc.2.143b , cf. SIG1241 , etc.; opp. Ep.Jac.3.10; Plb.23.10.7; D.S.1.45, Plu…

κατάρατος.definition: Ion. Herod.5.44, but Schwyzer702.11 :—accursed, abominable, E.Med.112 : freq. in Com., Ar.Ra.178, cf. Pax33; Id.Lys.530, etc.: Comp. D.18.212: Sup. S.OT1345

κατάρβυλος.definition: reaching down to the shoes, S.Fr.622:—also Hsch

καταργέω.definition: leave unemployed or idle, E.Ph.753; cause to be idle, hinder in one's work, LXX2 Es.4.21, POxy.38.17 :— Pass., LXX2 Es.6.8; to be rendered or lie idle, PFlor.176.7 , etc

κατάργησις.definition: making null, abolishing, cj. in Sm.Ps.45.9, La.1.7

κατάργυρος.definition: covered with silver, silvered, Callix.2, Socr. Rhod.1, J.BJ5.5.3, Plu.2.828e

καταριθμέω.definition: count or reckon among; recount in detail, Pl.Smp.215a:—Med., recount, enumerate, Id.Phlb.27b, Grg.451e, Isoc.1.11; Aeschin.3.54: pf. Pass. in med. sense, having summed up . . , Arist.Top.101a31:—Pass., Phld.Ir.p.78 W.…

καταρίθμησις.definition: computation, J.Ap.1.21; enumeration, list, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.30.29, M.Ant.4.45, Gal.6.95

καταρκέω.definition: to be fully sufficient, Hdt.1.32; E.Rh.447; Jul.Or.1.29c: impers., it is enough, S.Fr.86

καταρνέομαι.definition: deny strongly, persist in denying, S.Ant.442, cf. PFlor.181.5
