καταρόω.definition: plough up, Ar.Av.582: fut. Jusj. ap. Poll.8.106: 2sg. aor. Hsch

καταρραθυμέω.definition: to be remiss or idle, X.Mem.3.5.13; trans., neglect, Cod.Just.1.2.24.16: also c. gen., Just.Nov.22.45.3

καταρραίνω.definition: besprinkle, Hp.Art.63; sprinkle, Gp.2.32.1 :— Pass., S.E.P.1.55

καταρράπτω.definition: stitch on or over; stitch tight, Hp.Acut.21; sew up, Thphr.HP9.5.3; Plu.Ant.81; in Surgery, Gal.14.783:—Pass., Aen.Tact.31.4; Agatharch.7; Sor.1.68

καταρραχίζω.definition: strengthd. for Anon. in Rh.3.577 W

καταρρήγνυμι.definition: and fut. E.HF864; tear in pieces, rend, . . D.21.63; D.S.19.34; Luc.Pisc.36:—Med., they rent their coats, Hdt.8.99, cf. X.Cyr.3.1.13, etc

καταρρητορεύω.definition: overcome by rhetoric:—Pass., to be so; = Lat. peroro, Gloss

καταρριζόω.definition: make rooted, plant firmly, Pl.Ti.73b; Plu.2.805f; AP9.708 :—Pass., take root, Pl.Ti.76c, 77c, etc.; planted, terminated, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.22.10

καταρρικνόομαι.definition: to be shrivelled, in pf. part. Pass., S.Ichn.295; also glossed by Suid

καταρρινάω.definition: or file down, make thin, Antyll. ap. Stob.4.37.16: metaph., polished, elegant, Ar.Ra.901; of men, i. e. having had all superfluous flesh worked off, A.Supp.747

καταρριπτάζω.definition: in Pass., to be blown away, scattered, Hsch

κατάρροπος.definition: inclining downwards; sloping, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.14.6

καταρροφέω.definition: = foreg., Id.Loc.Hom.17, X.Cyr.1.3.9, Arist.Pr.876a27, Herm.Iamb.4; some of . . , Orib.8.6.16:—Pass., Ruf.Sat.Gon.18:—later Alex.Trall.11.2, Sm.Jb.39.30

καταρρυθμίζω.definition: bring into rhythm, Hld.3.3; passages over-rhythmical, Longin.41.2: metaph., Philostr.VA7.18:—Pass., Ath.5.179a

κατάρρυθμος.definition: very rhythmical, Longin.41.1; prob. f. l. for in Paul.Aeg.2.11

καταρρυπαίνω.definition: fut. Isoc.12.63:—defile, sully, l. c., cf. Pl.Lg.919e, 937d; Arist.Ath.6.3, cf. Lib.Or.64.41; Plu.2.456c; Chor.Milt.64

καταρρωδέω.definition: Ion. for fear, dread, Hdt.1.34,80, al.; Id.9.8; Id.7.178: abs., Id.8.75, 103; . . Id.9.45

καταρτάω.definition: hang up, suspend, Plu.Rom.16; fasten, adjust, a well-adjusted or convenient thing, Hdt.3.80; became normal, recovered sense, to talk no connected sense, Id.Acut.16:—later in Act., Herod.1.62

καταρτίζω.definition: adjust, put in order, restore; furnish, equip, Plb.1.47.6, al., cf. PTeb.6.7 , D.S.13.70, etc.:—Pass., Plb.5.2.11; abs., in battle array, Hdt.9.66; instructed, Ev.Luc.6.40; prepare, make ready, Ph.Bel.78.24:—Med., LXX…

καταρτισμός.definition: restoration, reconciliation; Settling of a limb, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.1.1 , Sor.1.73

καταρτιστήρ.definition: one who restores order, mediator, Hdt.4.161, 5.28, Them.Or.4.61c

καταρτύω.definition: prepare, dress, of food, Luc.Hist.Conscr.44; train, discipline, Plu.2.38d: c. inf., to procure his coming, S.OC71:— Pass., Sol.27.11; . . S.Ant.478; Pl.Lg.808d; Id.Men.88b; Junc. ap. Stob.4.50.9

καταρχαιρεσιάζω.definition: beat in an election, esp. by unfair means, Plu.CG11:—metaph. in Pass., to be corrupted as by office, Longin.44.9

κατασαμινθεύω.definition: throw into a bath, PMasp.9 ii 29

κατάσαρκος.definition: fleshy, plump, Agatharch.Fr.Hist.7 J., Sor.2.57, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.12.8, Alciphr.Fr.5.3; gloss on Hdn.Epim.130

κατασάττω.definition: stamp down, Thphr.CP5.6.2: pf. part. Pass. glossed by Hsch

κατασεισμός.definition: = foreg., Sor.1.60 , Archig. ap. Gal.12.657, Aët.6.87

κατασημαίνομαι.definition: Med., cause to be sealed up; cause to be noted down, ib.756c:—Pass., ib.756e, cf. Arist.Ath.49.2

κατασήπω.definition: cause or allow to rot, X.Cyr.8.2.21:—Pass; metaph., cause or allow to linger, Gal.10.264:—Pass., pine away, ib.263; Arr.Epict.4.10.20

κατασθμαίνω.definition: pant, struggle against, c. gen., A.Th.393

κατασιγάζω.definition: put to silence, Arist.HA614a20, Ael.VH14.9; Hdn.1.9.3; Ael.NA16.23:—Pass., Posidon.36 J.; not now perused, Ath.1.3a

κατασιδηρόω.definition: plate with iron, D.S.13.54, cf. Bito53.7, Str.15.3.11

κατασίνομαι.definition: injure, damage, Hsch.: aor. 1 part., prob. l. in Malch.p.407 D

κατασιτέομαι.definition: eat up, feed on, c. acc., Hdt.1.216, 3.38, Str.15.2.14, D.S.3.36

κατασιωπάω.definition: keep silence, Isoc.8.38, Arist.Rh.1413b7; c. acc. rei, keep silent, pass over, D.S.32.10:—Pass., Isoc.4.27

κατασκεδάννυμι.definition: spread a report against one, Pl.Ap.18c:—Pass., Id.Min.320d; Lys.10.23; Hp.Medic.7

κατασκελετεύω.definition: reduce to a skeleton, Plu.2.7d; Sch.Ar.Ra.153:—Pass., to be wasted away, 'desiccated', Isoc.15.268, cf. Ph.1.198, al., Onos.1.5 , D.L.8.41: metaph., Longin.2.1

κατασκέλλομαι.definition: Pass., become a skeleton, wither away, A.Pr.481: mostly in pf. Act. Thphr.CP6.14.11, Luc.Gall.29, Gal.UP8.7, etc.; Alciphr.3.19, cf. Luc.Bis Acc.34: plpf., Babr.46.8; to behard or frozen, Thphr. l.c.: metaph., austere…

κατασκευάζω.definition: fut. Att. SIG1097.9; without dat., furnish, equip fully, X.An.1.9.19; Id.Cyr.3.3.3; OGI54.12 :—Med., having got his asses ready, etc.:—Pass., Th.4.75, cf. 8.24; cultivated farms, Anaxag.4; of persons, to be under trea…

κατασκεύασμα.definition: that which is prepared or; arrangement, contrivance, D.23.13; Arist.Pol.1271a33; ib.1319b27; Phld.Rh.1.183 S.; Lat.ex composito, D.C.52.7

κατασκευασμός.definition: contrinance, D.24.16; Lat.ex composito, D.C.38.9, al

κατασκευαστέος.definition: to be prepared or made; neut., one must prepare, make, etc., Pl.Lg.964d, X.HG3.4.15, etc.; Philum. ap. Aët.9.23

κατασκευαστής.definition: contriner, Hsch. and Suid. s.v; one who makes provision, commissariat officer, quartermaster, Just.Nov.30.7.1

κατασκευάστρια.definition: fem. of she who prepares, Sch.Lyc.578

κατασκευόω.definition: Dor. = aor. IG 14.241 : pf. Test.Epict.4.13:—Med., GDI1874.26

κατασκηνάω.definition: = sq., aor. X.An.3.4.32, HG4.5.2, etc.: —Med., Pl.R.614e

κατασκηνόω.definition: take up one's quarters, encamp, . . X.Cyr.4.5.39, Hell.Oxy.16.2, etc.; . . LXX1 Ch.23.25; X.Cyr.6.2.2: generally, rest, LXXPs.15.9; settle, of birds, Ev.Matt.13.32: metaph., Porph.Abst.4.9

κατασκήνωμα.definition: covering, veil, A.Ch.985; gloss on Sch.Opp.H.2.524, cf. 3.5

κατασκήνωσις.definition: encamping, taking up one's; of birds, restingplace, nest, Ev.Matt.8.20

κατασκήπτω.definition: fut. E.Hipp.1418:—rush down or fall; c.acc., fall upon, dub.l. in E.Med.94 :—Pass., struck by lightning, Hsch.s.v

κατασκιάζω.definition: fut. Att. S.OC406:—overshadow, cover over, Hes.Th.716; Archil.29; Pl.Ti.74d; spread awnings, E.Ion1142; bury one, S.l.c.; . . IG7.580

κατασκιρόομαι.definition: Pass., become hard or dry through age; pf.inf. , = Apollod.Hist.Fr.107 J

κατασκιρτάω.definition: leap upon, Plu.2.790c; leap about, Ael.NA5.6

κατασκληρόομαι.definition: pf. part. Pass. gloss on Id

κατασκοπέω.definition: fut. aor. closely, spy out, reconnoitre, . . E.Hel.1607; reconnoitre, Aen. Tact.23.10; . . X.Cyr.7.1.39, cf. Th.6.50, al.; Plu.Sol.9; keep a look-out, of ships, Plb.3.95.6:—Med., X.Mem.2.1.22; Arist.MM1213a5; inspect,…

κατασκοπή.definition: viewing closely, spying, S.Ph.45; E.Ba.838; X.Cyr.6.2.9, cf. HG1.4.11, Arist.Ath. Fr.4, Plb.3.95.8; Aeschin.2.28; X.An.7.4.13; Plu.Fab.12; Th.6.34; to inspect the money, ib.46

κατασκοπία.definition: fem. of epith. of Aphrodite at Troezen, Paus.2.32.3

κατάσκοπος.definition: one who reconnoitres, scout, spy; examiner, inspector, Th.4.27, cf.8.41; Fouilles de l'Institut Français d'Arch. Orientale du Caire4.p.74: metaph., Secund.Sent.7

κατασμικρολογέω.definition: speak disparagingly of, accuse as niggardly, Hp.Ep.17

κατασμικρύνω.definition: lessen, abridge; = belittle, Hierocl.p.59 A., cf. Max.Tyr.22.2, Ath.8.359a, Simp.in Epict.p.102 D

κατασμύχω.definition: burn with a slow fire, burn up, Il.9.653: metaph., of love, Theoc.3.17:—in Pass., of a disappointed rival, waste away, Id.8.90, cf. Phalar.Ep.144.4; Hld.7.21

κατασμώχομαι.definition: Med., rub in pieces, bruise, Nic.Th.860, Al.332

κατασοβαρεύομαι.definition: regard haughtily, J.BJ3.1.1, D.L.1.81, Men.Prot.p.321 D

κατασοφίζομαι.definition: outwit by sophisms or fallacies, c; evade by quibbling, CIG 4224d10

κατασοφισμός.definition: outwitting, trickery, Alex.Aphr.in SE48.10, Eust.1695.36, Sch.Hermog.in Rh.4.215 W

κατασπάζομαι.definition: embrace, kiss, Plu.Cor.9; do homage to a king, J.AJ7.10.5

κατασπαράσσω.definition: Att. tear in pieces, Ar.Eq.729; Plb.23.14.8, D.S.29.21; Luc.Asin.22

κατάσπασις.definition: drawing down, Arist.Mete.369b20; dub.in Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.108

κατάσπασμα.definition: in pl., vibrations of the reed-; part, fragment, J.BJ5.12.1 , cf. Hsch. and Suid. s.v

κατασπαταλάω.definition: live wantonly, wanton, LXXPr.29.21, Am.6.4, Luc.Epigr.50

κατασπειράω.definition: in pf. part. Pass., dub.l. in Epicur.Ep.2p.45U.; fort

κατασπείρω.definition: fut. LXX :—sow, plant; beget, E.HF469, Phint. ap. Stob.4.23.61a; him that begat me, Diph.93

κατασπένδω.definition: fut. E.Or.1187:—pour as a drink-; c. acc., wet, Trag.Adesp.548

κατασπέρχω.definition: urge on, with a spear, Ar.Ach.1188; Opp.H.4.91; drove [them] on, D.C.41.46; of circumstances, urgent, pressing, Th.4.126:—Pass., to be driven on, J.BJ4.2.4

κατασπεύδω.definition: urge, hasten on, Aeschin.3.67, cf; agitate, dismay, LXXDa.4.16

κατασπιλάζω.definition: spot, stain, Hsch; = Anon. ap. EM495.42

κατασπορά.definition: sowing, PTeb.341.5 , POxy.2121.42 , Sch.Pl.Lg.853d, Phot. s.v

κατασπουδάζομαι.definition: as Pass., to be troubled, LXXJb.23.15, Aq.2 Ki.4.1, al; to be oppressed, Vett. Val.254.16

κατάσσω.definition: later for impf. Aesop.7:—Pass., Apollod.Poliorc.189.6, App.Pun.129, Artem.1.66, PHolm.6.40. by nature, Hdn.Gr.2.109.]

καταστάζω.definition: c. acc. rei, let fall in drops upon, shed over, E.Hec.760; Id.HF934; also of a garment, S.Fr.373.3: c. acc. only, let fall in drops , A.Fr.327

κατασταθμεύω.definition: put into a stable or stall, Str.4.5.2:—Pass., to be oppressed by having soldiers quartered upon one, Id.16.1.16

κατασταμνίζω.definition: draw off wine into a smaller vessel , rack off, bottle, wine in bottle, Thphr.CP2.18.4; bottles of wine, Nicostr.Com.11:—Act., Com. ap. Poll.7.162

καταστασιάζω.definition: overpower by forming a counter-party; = LXXEx.38.22, J.BJ Prooem.7, BGU 836.5

κατάστασις.definition: trans., settlement, establishment, institution, A.Ag.23, cf. Ar.Th.958; D.18.188; mode of establishing democracy, Pl.R.557a; constitution of a wardship, Arist.Ath.56.6: also c. gen. agentis, their ordinance, decree, E…

καταστάτης.definition: establisher, restorer; in dual, , as official title, Schwyzer 418.13

καταστατόν.definition: kind of cake, gloss on Sch.rec. Theoc.9.21

καταστεγάζω.definition: cover over, Hdt.4.71, cf. Pl.Criti.115e; Arist.HA603a5; roof over, IG22.463.52:— Pass., Gp.13.14.7

καταστεγνόομαι.definition: Pass., to be closely covered, Moschio ap.Ath.5.207d, v.l. in Gp.13.14.7

κατάστεγος.definition: covered in, roofed, Hdt.2.148; Pl.Euthd.273a; Arist.HA616a25, cf. Men.Sam.76, Ph.Bel.80.32, Plb.9.41.9; Lib.Or.9.8

καταστείχω.definition: aor. 2 = AP9.298 ; return from exile, IG22.1113.12

καταστέλλω.definition: fut. E.Ba.933 (for Aeol. forms v; let down, lower, D.H.8.44; shut them, Plu.2.979c; press down, Gal.15.792

καταστενοχωρέω.definition: drive into a narrow space, Zos.5.16

καταστένω.definition: sigh over, lament, c. acc., S.OC1440, E.Tr.317 , HF1141; ib.1045 ; Id.IA470; S.El.874

καταστερέω.definition: = sq., in Pass., Nech. ap. Vett.Val.59.28

καταστερισμός.definition: placing among the stars: title of treatise on constellations by Hipparchus, Suid.; also of an extant work wrongly attributed to Eratosthenes; cf. Plin.Epp.5.17.1, Ps.-Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.833.2

καταστερόω.definition: f.l. for I, Palaeph.51:—Pass., prob. in Phld.D.3.9, cf. Sch.E.Or.1631

καταστέφω.definition: deck with garlands, crown, wreath, E.Heracl.124; Id.Ph.1632; here are my tresses for you to crown, Id.IA1478 ; encircle thee, Id.Heracl.226; and are vv.ll. in S.OC467, cf. D.C.51.5; Epic. in Arch.Pap.7p.7:—Pass., Aesc…

καταστηλιτεύω.definition: post up, publish a name, etc., Luc.DMeretr.4.2, cf. Hsch. s.v. Ph.Fr.54H., cf. Poll.8.73

καταστηρίζω.definition: establish, Nonn.D.38.424; prove; intr., . . settle in a spot, of disease, Hp.Aff.15, cf. 11

καταστίζω.definition: cover with marks, Hdn.Gr.1.10; brand, D.S.34/5.2.27: freq. in pf. Pass., to be marked or spotted, spotted, Arist.HA559a24, cf. Dsc.5.143; Ael.NA12.24; D.C.43.23; are marked upon them, Ael.NA10.13: metaph., to be spott…

κατάστικτος.definition: spotted, speckled, brindled, S.Fr.11; E.Ba.697; Arist.HA593a13; of garments, IG22.1514.11,al.; Arr.Ind.5, cf. Men.1019; tattooed, Str.7.5.4: metaph., dotted, Id.2.5.33; Id.17.3.1; studded, Jul.Or.5.171a

καταστίλβω.definition: send beaming forth, h.Mart.10; irradiate, AP12.254

καταστοιχειόομαι.definition: Pass., to be reduced to its elements, Epicur.Ep.1p.3U

καταστολή.definition: equipment, dress, 1 Ep.Ti.2.9; putting down, checking, D.S.15.94; reduction, subjugation, Wilcken Chr.12.15

καταστομίζω.definition: v.l. for put to silence, Plu.Arist.4

καταστόμιον.definition: mouth of a pipe or tube, HeroSpir.1.25

καταστοχάζομαι.definition: aim at, Alex. Trall.Febr.6: hence, hit, guess, infer, Plb.12.13.4; D.S.19.39; Ath.9.391b, Procl.in Alc.p.46 C., Phlp.in Ph.640.3: abs., Heph.Astr.3.4:—Act. is f.l. in Suid. s.v. and dub. cj. for :—Pass., Phld.Rh.1.362…

καταστοχαστής.definition: one who guesses, cj. for in Suid. s.v

καταστοχέω.definition: hit the mark, i. e. succeed in bribing him, PTeb.58.35

καταστράπτω.definition: hurl down lightning, flash lightning; trans., strike with lightning, dazzle, Id.Tim.28; Them.Or.27.337d; Hld.1.21; make it gleam with arms, Id.9.14

καταστρατεύω.definition: take the field against, make war upon; Med., overrun in war, ChioEp.2

καταστρατηγέω.definition: overcome by generalship or stratagem; counteract by stratagem, Zos.3.24

καταστρατοπεδεία.definition: pitching a camp: living in camps, Phylarch.41 J. , Ael.VH9.3

καταστρατοπεδεύω.definition: encamp, X.Cyr.7.2.8; intr., take up quarters, Plb.1.30.15, 1.18.2, 3.77.1: abs., Ph.Bel.103.48:—Med., X.An.3.4.18, Arr.An.5.9.1

καταστρέφω.definition: pf. Plb.23.11.2:—Pass; upset, overturn, Ar.Eq.274; D.L.5.82; ruin, undo, Plb.23.11.2; AP11.163 :—Pass., Hdn.8.4.8

καταστροφεύς.definition: one who ruins or spoils his; subverter, Lyd.Mag.3.69

καταστροφή.definition: overturning, A.Eu.490 (lyr; subjugation, reduction, Hdt.1.6, 92, etc.; Id.6.27; Id.4.167; Th.1.15: pl., Phld.Rh.1.255 S

καταστρώννυμι.definition: also LXXJb.12.23; spread over, cover, . . Ael.VH9.8:—Pass., was strewed with . . , D.S.14.114; Str.14.2.26

καταστυγνάζω.definition: pf. to be of sad countenance, Apollon.Lex.s.v. Sch.E.Or.1317:—Pass., pf. part., Sch.E.Med.1009

κατάστυγνος.definition: of sad countenance, Ath.13.585d, Vett.Val.2.5, Sch.E.Alc.800

καταστύφελος.definition: very hard or rugged, h.Merc.124, Hes.Th.806

καταστωμύλλομαι.definition: in pass. sense, things blabbed out, EM524.31

κατασυγκρίνω.definition: reduce the pores to a proper state, Steph.in Gal.1.337 D

κατασυλλογίζομαι.definition: Pass., have a conclusion drawn against one, Arist.APr.66a25

κατασυμβαίνω.definition: dub. l. in Iamb.in Nic.p.12 P

κατασφάζω.definition: later Luc.Sacr.12 : fut. LXXEz.16.40:—slaughter, murder, Hdt.6.23, 8.127, LXX l.c., al., Ev.Luc.19.27, D.C.40.48: freq. in aor. Pass. A.Eu.102, S.OT730, X.An.4.1.17, etc

κατασφαλίζομαι.definition: fortify, Men.Prot.p.15 D; confirm, Lyd.Mag.3.12; Just.Nov.102 Praef.; assure oneself of, Steph.in Hp.1.76 D

κατασφηκόω.definition: nail fast, fasten, in Pass., Tryph.88, cf. Hsch

κατασφηνόομαι.definition: Pass., to be wedged, bound tight, Hp.Nat.Puer.24

κατασφραγίζω.definition: Ion. and Ep. seal up, LXXJb.9.7, 37.7: mostly pf. part. Pass. sealed up, made fast, secured, Emp.115.2, cf. A.Supp.947, E.Fr.762, Pl.Erx.400a, etc.: impf. Pass. Tryph.68: fut. Hermes 64.64 : aor. LXXWi.2.5, Hsch.:—Med…

κατασχάζω.definition: slit, cut open, Thphr.HP2.7.6; Id.CP1.17.10, al.; open a vein, let blood, Gal.19.139:—also scarify, Hp.Int.22, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.29.2

κατασχασμός.definition: = Gal.11.321, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.15, Orib.7.18 tit

κατάσχεσις.definition: holding back, restraining; possession, LXXLe.25.25, Za.11.14, al., Act.Ap.7.5

κατασχετέος.definition: to be held fast, Sch.Ar.Ach.258; abs., one must hold back, delay, Sch.E.Ph.1279

κατασχηματίζω.definition: dress up or invest with a certain form or appearance, Isoc.11.24; Plu.Rom.26:—Pass., to be conformed, modelled, Id.Lyc.27

κατασχημονέω.definition: act indecently, Phot. s.v. act indecently towards, App.Sam.7, Sch.Ar.Ra.153

κατασχίζω.definition: fut. X.An.7.1.16:—cleave asunder, split, slit, Ar.V.239, cj. in Hp.Mochl.36 ; burst them open, X. l.c., D.21.79; tear, Phld.Ir.p.39 W.: —Med., Ar.Ra.405 :—Pass., of nerves or veins, branch, Gal.2.390, 8.65; of leaves,…

κατασχολέομαι.definition: to be engaged, of sciences, Perict. ap.Stob.3.1.121; Placit.1 Prooem., cf. Archyt. ap. Iamb.Comm.Math.8, Apollon.Mir.7, Theol.Ar.18; to be concerned, worried about, PRein.18.18 , Phld.Rh.2.139 S

καταταινιόω.definition: bind with a Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

καταταρταρόω.definition: hurl down to Tartarus, Orph.Fr.57, Corn.ND7, S.E.P.3.210; Lyd.Mens.4.159:—Pass., Apollod.1.1.3, Sch.E.Med.1296:—hence Procl.in Ti.1.188 D., Lyd. l. c

κατατάσσω.definition: Att. pf. Plb.8.9.5; appoint, to do a thing, D.25.13; Pl.Lg.945a; POxy.1415.18 ; . . appoint one to go to a place, Plb.3.33.12

καταταχέω.definition: accelerate, PTeb.19.13 :—Pass; outstrip, overtake, Plb.8.3.3; escape by superior speed, Id.1.47.8; c. part., anticipate in doing, Id.3.16.5, 4.68.5:—Pass., D.S.14.72

κατατέμνω.definition: Ion. fut. Ar.Ach.301: aor; c. dupl. acc., cut him up into strips, Ar.Ach.301; having cut it up into cubes, Alex.187.4; Ephipp.22; Pl.R.610b; Tab.Heracl. l.c.: —Pass., may I be cut up into straps, Ar.Eq.768

κατατετραίνω.definition: found as pres. only in the form Gal.11.402: aor. 1 Plu.2.689c:—bore through, perforate, ll.cc.: usu. in pf. Pass., cavities bored through it, Pl.Ti.70c, cf. Str.15.1.36; Plu.2.699a

κατατιλάω.definition: make dirt over, Ar.Av.1054, Ra.366:—Pass., Id.Av.1117; Artem.2.26

κατατίλλω.definition: aor. 1 pull to pieces, Hp.Nat.Mul.32: metaph., Hsch. s.v

κατατλάω.definition: strengthd. for in med. form Hsch

κατατοιχογραφέω.definition: write upon a wall, write up libels against a person, Str.14.5.14; v.l

κατατολμάω.definition: behave boldly towards; strengthd. for abs., Id.1.47.10, UPZ42.20 ; desperate, reckless persons, Phld.Sto.Herc.339.12: c.inf., Plb.2.13.5, LXX2 Ma.3.24, Gal.14.644: c. acc., Hld.7.24

κατατοξεύω.definition: strike down with arrows, shoot dead, Hdt.3.36, Th.3.34, etc.; Ar.Nu.944:—Pass., X.HG4.7.6, Phld.Piet.34: metaph., Eun.Hist.p.263 D

κατατραγῳδέω.definition: describe tragically, exaggerate, Ach.Tat.6.4: also c. gen., uttered in tragic phrase against, Id.8.9

κατατρέχω.definition: aor. 1 inf. only in Hsch.: aor. 2; of seamen or passengers by sea, run to land, disembark, X.HG5.1.12; Plb.3.91.2: metaph., come to a haven in . . , f.l. in Pi.N.4.23

κατατριακοντουτίζω.definition: Com. word in Ar.Eq.1391, alluding to the personified upon the stage as courtesans, with an obscene pun upon

κατατρίβω.definition: fut. X.Cyr.8.4.36: pf; of clothes, wear out, Thgn.55, cf. Ar.Fr.345, Pl.Phd.87c, Metrod.Fr.55: hence metaph., Pl.Phd.91d, cf. 87d; i.e. constant frequenters of the tribune, Isoc.Ep.8.7; Arist.Ph.253b15: metaph., to ha…

κατατριδομέω.definition: perh. lay three layers of stones, IG12.11.18

κατατροπόω.definition: put to flight, Aesop.291b:—also i in Med., Id.21

κατατροχάζω.definition: cause to run smoothly: hence, promote; = II.2, Nech.in Cat.Cod.Astr.7.141

κατατροχίζω.definition: upset from a chariot, Sch. A.R.1.752; break on the wheel, condemned by Phryn.PSp.114 B

κατατρυφάω.definition: make merry, be insolent, Luc.JTr.53; =; c. gen., delight in, LXXPs.36.4; ib.11

κατατρύω.definition: = foreg., in Med., Nic.Al.593:— Pass., pf. inf. prob.l.in X.Cyr.5.4.6

κατατρώγω.definition: fut. Cratin.143: aor. 2 Ar.Ach.809:—eat up, esp. fruits and vegetables, ll.cc., Thphr.HP9.11.9, LXXPr.24.23 , Theoc.5.115, Luc.Apol.5: c. gen., Plu.Art.3, etc.: aor. 1 part. Timo66.6:—Pass., Arist.Pr.925a31

κατατυγχάνω.definition: hit one's mark, reach the object of; abs., to be lucky or successful, opp. D.18.178; as to the situation of the city, one must hope to be successful, Arist.Pol.1330a37

κατατύπτω.definition: pound, crush, Sch.E.Hipp.977:—Med., beat one's breast, Sapph.62: c. acc., beat one's breast for, . . Supp.Epigr.4.190

κατατυραννέω.definition: to be tyrant over, c. gen., Sm.Nu.16.13

κατατωθάζω.definition: jeer, scoff at, Hld.6.2, cf. Lib.Descr.5.6

καταυαίνω.definition: fut. Archil.61:—wither up, l.c.:—later Lyc.397, Luc.Am.12

καταυγάστειρα.definition: as if fem. of illuminator, of the Moon, Orph.H.9.6

καταυθαδίζω.definition: act or speak obstinately against, Suid.:—Med., Men.Prot.p.102 D.:—also defy, Just.Nov.12.1

καταύλησις.definition: flute-playing, Thphr.HP4.11.5, Apollon.Mir.49; treatment by music, Sor.2.29

καταυλίζομαι.definition: aor. Hippon.63 , S.Ph.30, E.Rh.518, X.An.7.5.15; later Plu.Pyrrh.27, etc.:—to be under shelter of a hall, house, tent, ll.cc

καταυχένιος.definition: on or over the neck, AP5.72

καταφαίνω.definition: Dor. aor. 1 declare, make known; Pass., fut. dub. in E.Fr.781.65 :— become visible, appear, h.Ap.431, Hdt.7.51, Th.5.6, E.l.c., Plu.Luc.27:—also intr. in Act., Orph.A.370,762

καταφανής.definition: clearly seen, in sight; manifest, evident, Hdt.2.120, cf. Isoc.11.4, Pl.Grg.453c, X.Cyr.1.6.14, etc.; Hp.Off.3: Comp., Pl.Lg.812a: Sup., Id.Tht.186e, etc.: freq. c. part., Hp.VM1; And.1.116, cf. Aeschin.2.39, Isoc.2.1…

καταφαντάζομαι.definition: to be like, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44 codd

καταφαρμακεύω.definition: dose with drugs, Alex.Trall.9.3; anoint with drugs or charms, Luc.Am.39: hence

καταφαρμάσσω.definition: bewitch with drugs, Hdt.2.181: metaph., Plu.Dio14

καταφάσκω.definition: = Phld.Piet.123, Ph.1.104; Gal.10.37,al.; answer in the affirmative, Id.7.526:—Pass., A.D.Synt.245.12

καταφέρεια.definition: proneness, to pleasure, Ath.7.352c: abs., lechery, Eust.827.31

καταφερής.definition: inclined, prone, esp. to sensual pleasures, prob. in Phld.Ir.p.31 W.; Plu.Alex.23, Ath.13.589d: abs., lecherous, D.L.4.40, Sor.1.38 , Phot. s.v. freq. written

καταφεύγω.definition: fut. D.8.41:—flee for refuge; escape from . . , Hdt.6.75: abs., Alex.124.17

κατάφημι.definition: assent, S.OT506 (lyr., is gen; promulgate, f.l. in J.BJ3.8.4

καταφημίζω.definition: assign or dedicate to a god, Plb.5.10.8; Plu.Eum.13, cf. Jul.Or.4.156c

καταφθάνω.definition: fall upon unawares; c. inf., bring forth a child first, BGU665 ii 14 : also c. acc., pay in advance, POxy.1482.10

καταφθατόομαι.definition: take first possession of, A.Eu.398; cf. Hsch

καταφθείρω.definition: fut. Plu.2.24od:—destroy, bring to; corrupt, Plu.l.c

καταφθίνω.definition: sed v. infr.], waste away, decay, Pi.I.8.51, Hdt.2.123; S.Ph.266, E.Alc.622: in later Att. Prose, Thphr.HP9.16.5: aor. part. Plu.2.117c: pf. part. ib.621f, Arr.Epict.4.11.25: trans. is f.l. in Theoc.25.122

καταφίημι.definition: let slip down, f.l. in Pl.La.184a; Arist.Pr.960b32

καταφιλέω.definition: kiss, caress, X.Cyr.6.4.10; ib.7.5.32, cf. Men.Epit.56, Arr.Epict.4.10.20; X.Mem.2.6.33, cf. Arist.Fr.553, LXXRu.1.9, Ev.Matt.26.49; dist. from Ph.1.478; esp. of an amorous kiss. Luc.Am.13

καταφιλοσοφέω.definition: overcome in philosophizing; prove philosophically, . . Arr.Epict.4.1.167

καταφλάω.definition: press, crush, Hsch.:—Pass., dub. l. in Str.4.1.7

καταφλεξίπολις.definition: inflamer of cities, of a courtesan, AP5.1

καταφλυαρέω.definition: keep on chattering, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.20, 25: c. gen., Str.12.3.21, cf. D.L.5.20, Corp.Herm.1.29

καταφοβέω.definition: strike with fear, Th.7.21, Luc.DMeretr.13.5, D.C.39.36:—Pass., c. fut. Med., to be greatly afraid of, Ar.Ra.1109 : abs., Th.6.33

κατάφοβος.definition: fearful, afraid of, =; Act., terrifying, PSI6.684.17

καταφονεύω.definition: slaughter, Hdt.1.106, 165, al., E.Ba.1178 :— Pass., Id.Or.536

καταφορέω.definition: = of a river, carry down, Hdt.5.101, cf. 3.106 : metaph., . . . . you have poured forth a wonderful stream of calculation of the difference . . , Pl.R.587e; . . he went on inveighing much against . . , Plu.2.548c

καταφορτίζω.definition: load heavily, J.AJ7.9.3 : metaph., weigh down, Hipparch. ap. Stob.4.44.81; weary, burden, Jul.Or.2.69b; of financial burdens, Just.Nov.148 Praef

καταφράζω.definition: declare, Pi.O.10.55:—Med., with aor. Pass. and Med., consider, think upon, weigh, Hes.Op.248; having observed . . , Hdt.4.76; Sol.13.38; D.P.884

κατάφρακτος.definition: covered, shut up, S.Ant.958 ; decked vessels, Th.1.10 codd., cf. Plb.1.20.13; IG12.41 ; cavalry clad in full armour, mailed, Plb.30.25.9, cf. Arr.Tact.4.1, 19.4; Plu.Crass.21; coat of mail, PMagd.13.6 : metaph., encas…

καταφράσσω.definition: fortify, protect, in Pass., LXX1 Ma.6.38; J.BJ7.8.5; Plu.Alex.16; Id.Crass.24: metaph., Id.Alex.33

καταφρονέω.definition: look down upon, think slightly of; abs., to be disdainful, deal contemptuously, Th.2.11, Amphis1.3, Arist.Rh.1378b15; contempt, D.H.5.44

καταφρόνημα.definition: contempt, not only spirit, but a spirit of disdain, Th.2.62, cf.J.AJ19.1.16,al., D.C.51.9

καταφρόνησις.definition: contempt, disdain, Th.1.122, Pl.R.558b, Arist.Rh.1378b14, D.S.1.93, etc.; disregard, neglect, PMasp.94.13 , etc.; D.H.Orat.Vett.2; title of work by Polystratus: also without any bad sense, opp. Th.2.62

καταφρονητής.definition: despiser, Arr.Epict.4.7.33; Plu.Brut.12; J.BJ2.8.3: abs., LXXHb.1.5, Ze.3.4, Vett.Val.47.33

καταφροντίζω.definition: used in a Com. phrase; attend to, Plb.28.13.10

καταφρυάττομαι.definition: snort at, prop. of a horse: metaph., behave insolently, M.Ant.7.3; Id.9.41; Suid

καταφρύγω.definition: burn away, burn to ashes, of lightning; parch, consume, of disease, Alex.Trall.Febr.4:—Pass., to be dried up, Ruf. ap. Aët.5.95: fut. Hsch.:—also Id., Olymp.in Mete.299.11

καταφυγή.definition: place of refuge, Hdt.7.46; c. gen. obj., refuge from . . , E.Or.448 ; Th.4.98; E.Or.567 , cf. Antipho1.4; Pl.Lg.699b, etc.; Hyp.Eux.10; Men.581

καταφύγιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Democr.180, Sch. Hermog.in Rh.4.172 W

καταφυλλοροέω.definition: shed the leaves: metaph., lose its splendour, Pi.O.12.15

καταφυτεύω.definition: plant, ib.Ex.15.17,al; transplant, acclimatize, SIG22.13 , cf. Posidon.68 J., Str.15.3.11

κατάφυτος.definition: full of plants or trees, Plb.18.20.1: c. dat., planted with . . , D.S.2.37; Str.12.2.1; Luc.Nec.11

καταφύω.definition: aor. 1 implant, insert; Med., overrun a country, Suid., Phot

καταφωράω.definition: catch in a theft: generally, detect, Th.8.87, Luc.Gall.28; Th.1.82; discover its existence, X.Cyr.8.7.17: aor. Pass., J.AJ16.10.1

κατάφωρος.definition: detected, Onos.39.2, J.AJ20.11.1; evident, manifest, D.H.Rh.9.5; Plu.Cat.Mi.54

καταχαίρω.definition: fut. LXXPr.1.26:—exult over; rejoice much, Alciphr.2.4, IG14.2410.11, Supp.Epigr.2.844

καταχαλκεύω.definition: work or mould in bronze, Plu.2.559d; that [the coin] might not be worked up, Id.Lys.17

καταχαράσσω.definition: scratch all over, Men. Prot.p.89 D.:—Pass., Sch.D.T.p.139 H

καταχαρίζομαι.definition: corruptly make one a present of a; surrender a thing corruptly, Lys.27.14; Aeschin.3.53; give judgement by private interest, Pl.Ap.35c, cf. Din.1.105, J.AJ4.8.14; D.26.20; Arist.Pol.1271a3; Ael.VH14.5, cf. 11.9; Plu.P…

καταχασμάομαι.definition: = foreg., Hsch. s.v; Pass., split, burst open, Thphr.CP4.12.11

καταχέζω.definition: fut. Ar.Fr.152: aor. Id.Nu.174, Alc.Com.4:—befoul, ll.cc

καταχειρίζομαι.definition: make away with, D.C.77.6; take in hand, Ptol.Tetr.206

καταχειροτονέω.definition: vote by show of hands against, vote in condemnation of or so as to commit for trial, D.21.2, Din.2.20, etc.: c.inf., D.21.175, cf. 51.8; a vote of condemnation having been passed against him, and that for sacrilege, I…

καταχειροτονία.definition: condemnation, esp. by show of hands, D.21.6, cf. Aeschin.3.52, Arist.Ath.59.2 , Harp., EM481.46

καταχθέω.definition: weigh down, afflict, J.AJ18.6.7: pf.part. Pass. = Phot

καταχθόνιος.definition: also A.R.4.1413:—subterranean, i.e. Pluto, Il.9.457 ; of Pluto, Demeter, Persephone, and the Erinyes, IG3.1423; Hierocl.in CA1 p.419 M.; = Lat. Di Manes, AP7.333; = Lat. Di Manes, freq. in sepulchral Inscrr., IG14.166…

καταχιονίζω.definition: cover with snow, in Pass., Hsch. s.v

καταχλαινόω.definition: clothe with a Anon. ap. Suid

καταχλευάζω.definition: scoff, jeer, D.H.Comp.25, Poll.6.199: c.gen., J.BJ2.18.7:—Pass., f.l. in Ph.2.598

καταχλοάζομαι.definition: to be covered with green weed, of rocks, Sch.Opp.H.1.131

καταχορδεύω.definition: mince up as for a sausage, Hdt.6.75; Them.Or.21.261d

καταχόρευσις.definition: song, finale of the representing Apollo's dance of triumph, Poll.4.84

καταχορεύω.definition: dance in triumph over, Ael.NA1.30: metaph., insult, Anon. ap. Suid

καταχορηγέω.definition: lavish as Lys.19.42: generally, spend or contribute lavishly, D.H.3.72; Plu.Lys.9; squander upon, Id.Eum.13; Id.2.348f; Id.Cat.Ma.3

καταχραίνω.definition: befoul, B.5.44, cf. Eustr.in EN316.34:—also in Med., sprinkle, with milk, AP7.657

καταχράομαι.definition: Delph. SIG672.32; do what one likes with a person or thing, Aeschin.1.122

καταχρηματίζω.definition: deal with, SIG1023.73 , GDI 3624a32 : dispose of property, POxy.506.42 , etc

καταχρηματισμός.definition: deed, instrument dealing with property, ib.237iv7 , PFlor.381.11

κατάχρησις.definition: excessive use or consumption; analogical application of a word , Arist. ap. Cic.Orat.27.94, Demetr.Lac. Herc.1014.49, D.H.Comp.3 , Quint.8.6.34, Sch.D.T.p.459 H., etc.: pl., Suid. s.v. Gal.6.136

κατάχριστος.definition: for use as ointments, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.24.10, cf. Dsc.5.106; Tab.Defix.Aud.8

καταχρίω.definition: anoint, smear, coat, Arist.HA625b31; IG11.203 A54 ; ib.199 A102 ; LXXEx.2.3; Luc.Anach.9; Ael.VH2.15:—Med., Artem.4.41:—Pass., Dsc.2.70; M.Ant.3.3; Ph.2.158; = oblita, Gloss

καταχρυσόω.definition: cover with gold-leaf, gild, Hdt.2.129; metaph., make golden , Plu.Per.12; plastered him with gold , Ar.Ec.826

καταχρώννυμι.definition: Poll.7.169, Suid.: impf. Anon. ap. Suid. :—colour, Poll.2.35, cf. Alex.Aphr.in SE9.3:—Pass., metaph., . . E.Hec.911

κατάχυμα.definition: bath-water, Ammon.Diff.p.78 V.; = perfusio and = tucca, Gloss.: but in pl., = Them.Or.23.293c

κατάχυσις.definition: pouring on or over, Hp.Aph.5.21; affusion, besprinkling, Id.Art.27; Gp.13.14.11. II. vase for pouring, later Gr. for Att. Moer.p.296 P., cf. Hsch. s.v. III. mistransl. of Hebr. mûṣaq ’straitness’, as if mûṣaq ’smeltin…

κατάχυσμα.definition: that which is poured over, sauce; handfuls of nuts, figs, etc., showered over a bride, Theopomp.Com.14; also on a new slave, by way of welcome, Ar.Pl.768 , D.45.74; cf

καταχυσμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., sauce for pouring over a dish, Pherecr.108.11, Poll.6.68

καταχωνεύω.definition: melt down, D.22.76, Din.1.69, Str.9.1.20, etc.; Plu.2.82of; poured molten gold down his throat, App.Mith.21

καταχώννυμι.definition: silt up, dam up, D.S.24.1; metaph., . . with fresh streams they will choke up the channel of our original argument, Pl. l.c.; Id.Grg.512c; Plu.2.512e:—Pass., to be buried in obscurity, Pl.Cra.414c; Vett.Val.301.9

καταχωρίζω.definition: Att. fut. OGI 229.75; enter in a register or record, LXXEs.2.23; IG7.413.31 ; PAmh.2.35.36 , etc.:—Pass., POxy.515.3 , etc.; SIG18.6 , cf. Supp.Epigr.3.378C13 ; LXX1 Ch.27.24; Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39 xvii 27

καταχωρισμός.definition: registration, deposit in a registry, PAmh.2.35.37 , POxy.514.4 , etc.: setting in order, Andronic.Rhod.p.576 M

καταψεκάζω.definition: Att. wet by continual dropping, A.Ag.561; Plu.Alex.35:—hence Gp.5.39.2

καταψελλίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be made to lisp, Philostr.Im.1.25

καταψεύδομαι.definition: say falsely, pretend, . . E.Ba.334; feign, invent, D.18.11; c. gen., make a pretence of, Luc.Asin.7; give a false account of, Arist.Pr.950b6; J.BJ Prooem.1

καταψευδομαρτυρέω.definition: bear false witness against, X.Ap.24:—Med., D.29.6:—Pass., to be borne down by false evidence, Pl.Grg.472a, Is.5.9, D.21.136

καταψηφίζομαι.definition: fut. Lys.12.90:—vote against or; Pass. , to be condemned, D.21.151; to death or exile, Pl.R.558a, cf. Plt.299a

καταψήφισις.definition: voting against, condemnation, Antipho1.3, D.C.36.38 :— also Poll.8.149

καταψήχω.definition: rub down, pound in a mortar, Nic.Th.898; wear away, consume, cj. in Simon.176:—Pass., crumble away, S.Tr.698, cf. Pl.Ti.84a

καταψιθυρίζω.definition: whisper against; abs., in a low, conversational tone, Hieronym. ap. Phld.Rh.1.199S

κατάψυχρος.definition: very cold, Hp.Art.67, S.E.P.1.125, etc.; Dsc.2.76; Gp.1.12.33; of character, Vett.Val.11.32, al

κατέαγμα.definition: later form of BGU647.12 , PAmh.2.93.19 , Gloss

κατεγγυάω.definition: as law-term, make responsible, compel to give security, or D.32.29, 59.40, cf. Pl.Lg.871e, PTeb.490 , etc.; make him give security to the amount of 20 talents, Plb.5.15.9; Plu.Tim.37:—Pass., to be held to bail, D.59.4…

κατεγγύησις.definition: = taking of pledges, sequestration, PTeb.148 , PRyl.119.13

κατεγκονέω.definition: to be in great haste, Hsch

κατεγχλιδάω.definition: look haughtily down upon, Macho ap.Ath.13.577e

κατεικάζω.definition: guess, surmise, Hdt.6.112; Hp.Ep.17; suspect, Hdt.9.109

κατείλησις.definition: crowding, compression; wrapping, Aret.CA2.9, cf. Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.18.1; is f.l. in Archig. ap. Gal.13.168

κατείργω.definition: Ion. , Cypr. aor. 2; hinder, prevent, E.Med.1258 : c. acc. et inf., . . Id.Supp.308: abs., delay, Id.Alc.256 ; limit, Plu.Pomp.53

κατειρωνεύομαι.definition: use irony towards, banter; treat in a spirit of raillery, Id.Comp.Dem.Cic.1

κατελαύνω.definition: drive down, Longus2.10; push down, Ar.Fr.205

κατελέγχω.definition: convict of falsehood, belie; betray, of dogs, Poll.5.42

κατελεέω.definition: strengthd. for have compassion upon, or Pl.R.415c, And.2.15, Lys.6.3; Plb.2.6.2: abs., Arist.HA631a19

κατελπίζω.definition: hope or expect confidently, Hdt.8.136, cf. Plb.2.31.8; D.S.15.33, cf. Phld.Oec.p.73 J.: c. gen., base one's hopes upon, J.AJ5.1.20:—Pass., Phld.Lib.p.27 O

κατεμφορέομαι.definition: Med., take one's fill of, Eun.Hist.p.256 D

κατεναντιόω.definition: pf.part. Pass. in opposition to, Phld.Po.Herc.1676.3

κατεναρίζω.definition: strengthd. for kill outright: aor. Pass. A.Ch.347 : pf. part. Pass. S.Aj.26

κατενισχύω.definition: become firmly established, v.l. in LXX1 Ch.29.30

κατεντυγχάνω.definition: seek an interview with, PGen.31.4; plead against, accuse, Suid. and Phot. s.v

κατεξανάστασις.definition: rebellion against, resistance to, Longin.7.3; Iamb.VP16.69

κατεξανίσταμαι.definition: aor. 2 Act. rise up; rise, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.139

κατεξουσία.definition: sovereignty, dominion, IG14.1047.5 : c.gen., power over, PMag.Par.1.1949; also CIG4710

κατεξουσιάζω.definition: exercise authority over, Ev.Matt.20.25, Ev.Marc.10.42; Jul.Gal.100c

κατεπαγγέλλομαι.definition: Med. with pf. Pass., make promises or engagements, with one, D.32.11; Aeschin.3.223; promise, c.acc., J.AJ8.14.4; devote it to . . , Plu.2.807b: c. pres. inf., Aeschin.1.117, cf. Ph.2.316: c. fut. inf., Aeschin.1.173;…

κατεπαίρομαι.definition: Pass., to be arrogant towards, c. gen., Sm.Ps.60.3, Just.Nov.129 Praef

κατεπείγω.definition: press hard, his creditors were pressing him hard, D.33.6, cf. Th.1.61; the ebbing water urges him on, Pl.Tht.172e; Id.Ep.338e: c. acc. et inf., . . Id.Lg.781e; D.24.18; X.Mem.2.1.2; PFlor.161.5 ; alone, the urgent sym…

κατεπεμβαίνω.definition: overflow to its injury; plant one's foot firmly upon, Corp.Herm.18.16

κατεπιδείκνυμαι.definition: Med., show off before another, M.Ant.11.13

κατεπίθεσις.definition: strengthd. for Eun.VSp.477 B., Phot. and Suid. s.v

κατεπίκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie, rest upon, IG14.1888, CIG4152 d

κατεπιορκέω.definition: commit perjury against; Med., effect by perjury, D.54.40

κατεπιτηδεύω.definition: finish too elaborately, of style, D.H.Th.42

κατεπιχειρέω.definition: lay hands upon, attempt, AB154, cf. Eustr.in EN51.21

κατεποικοδομέω.definition: build over or upon, in Pass., CIG3281

κατεργάζομαι.definition: fut. later 3sg. PTeb.10.2; earn, gain by labour, acquire, Hdt.3.65; E.Heracl.1046; Aeschin.3.229; D.45.66; Pl.Grg.473d: in pass. sense, Hdt.7.102

κατεργασία.definition: working up, freq. of food, by digestion or by chewing, Arist.PA675b5, Pr.931a32, etc.; stewing, boiling, Mnesith. ap. Ath.2.59b: generally, production, Hp.Praec.9; Epicur.Ep.1p.9 U. ; Phld.Oec.pp.51,55 J.; working or …

κατερείκω.definition: bruise, grind, Demon22: metaph., crush, subdue, Ar.V.649:—Med . . rend one's garments, in token of sorrow, Sapph.62, cf. Hdt.3.66, A.Pers.538

κατερειπόω.definition: = sq., in pf. part. Pass., D.S.32.14, Hld.9.5, Porph.Plot.12, Gloss

κατερεύγομαι.definition: aor. 2 belch over or upon, Ar.V.1151

κατερέφω.definition: cover over, roof, Plu.Caes.9; Id.Ant.49:—Med., roof over for oneself or what is one's own, Ar.V.1294; A.R.2.1073

κατευδοκέω.definition: to be well content with, Plb.21.33.2

κατευθύνω.definition: poet. impf. IGRom.4.507b; guide, direct, Id.Lg.809a; ib.847a; Arist.HA610a28; Id.Fr.11; Aristeas18; Plu.Cam.42; Id.2.20d; ib.780b; Gal.17.362

κατευναστής.definition: = foreg., Plu.Alex.40, Oth.17; generally, servant, ib.945d

κατευοδόω.definition: = LXXJd.18.5 cod.A:—also in Pass; bring prosperity, LXXPs.67.20

κατευπαθέω.definition: waste in dissipation, in Pass., Phryn.PSp.80B

κατευστοχέω.definition: strengthd. for to be quite successful, D.S.2.5: abs., Plu.Aem.19

κατευτυχέω.definition: to be quite successful, prosper, Arist.EE1229a.19 , Phld.Rh.1.132 S.; Plu.Sert.18:—also in Pass., D.S.20.46

κατευφημέω.definition: applaud, extol, LXX3 Ma.7.13, Plu.Sert.4, Cic.9, Epigr.Gr.430.12 : abs., Plu.2.487b; OGI234.18 :—Pass., D.H.3.18:—also Hsch. s.v

κατευχή.definition: prayer, vow, A.Ch.477 , Plu.Dio24 ; OGI309.7 , cf. SIG589.7

κατεύχομαι.definition: fut. E.IA1186:—pray earnestly, c; c.acc. et inf., A.Ch.139, Eu.922 , S.OC1575 ; pray to one, A.Ch.88, E.Andr.1105; Ath.13.573e; c. inf., entreat a person to . . , Theoc.2.71

κατευωχέομαι.definition: feast and make merry on; later in Act., feast, entertain, J.AJ11.6.1:—Pass., ib.6.1.3, al

κατεφίσταμαι.definition: rise up against, in aor. Act., Act.Ap.18.12

κατηβολή.definition: = III, Hp. ap. Gal.19.11c, Pl.Hp. Mi.372e , Hsch., Phot

κατηγορέω.definition: speak against, esp. before judges, accuse; bring as a charge against a person, accuse him of it, S.OT514, cf. E.Or.28, etc.; X.Mem.1.3.4; D.18.294; Hyp.Eux.23; And.1.110, Th.8.85: c. inf., Pl.Grg.482c: c. dupl. gen., …

κατηγόρημα.definition: accusation, charge, Gorg.Pal.22; in Logic, predicate, Arist.Int.20b32, Metaph.1053b19, etc.; Epicur.Fr.18

κατηγορησείω.definition: Desiderat., to be anxious to accuse, Agath.4.2

κατηγορία.definition: Ion. accusation, Hdt.6.50; in Logic, predication, Arist.Metaph.1007a35, etc.: pl., Id.APo.84a1; esp. affirmative predication, opp. Id.APr.52a15; Stoic.2.93

κατήγορος.definition: accuser, Hdt.3.71, S.Tr.814, And.4.16, Lys.7.11, Pl.Ap.18a , Apoc.12.10, etc.; public prosecutor, PFlor.6.6 ; betrayer, A.Th.439; X.Oec.20.15; . . what the respiration reveals, Hp.de Arte12

κατηλογέω.definition: make of small account, neglect, c. acc., Hdt.1.84,144, 3.121: c. gen., Parth.23.1, J.AJ12.4.6.—The form does not occur

κατήφεια.definition: Ion. and Ep. dejection , Il.3.51; 16.498, 17.556; Th.7.75; opp. Ep.Jac.4.9; Plu.Them.9; Id.Cor.20, cf. D.H.3.19, Corn.ND28, Charito6.8; Ph.2.204; Rhian.1.8

κατηφής.definition: with downcast eyes, downcast; metaph., dim, obscure, AP9.658 ; Poll.5.110; of colour, Philostr.VS2.1.8, cf. Him.Ecl.12.7

κατηφιάω.definition: = AP14.3, Ph.2.519 , Plu.2.119c; Ep. part. A.R.1.461, etc.; Ep. iterat. MAMA1.319

κατιθύνω.definition: Ion. and Ep. for Hdt.2.96, cf. Hp.Art.71, Luc.Trag.56, Aristaenet.1.15; Mosch.2.121; AP6.188 ; APl.4.226

κατιλλαίνω.definition: look askance at, Hsch. :—Act. is prob. in Arist.Phgn.813a21

κατίλλω.definition: = dub. sens. in Hp.Epid.3.5 .678, Erot.); = Phot. s.v

κατιλλώπτω.definition: look askance at, leer at, Philem.124; look scornfully, Poll.2.52, Hsch

κατιόομαι.definition: Pass., become rusty, tarnished, LXXSi.12.11 , Str.16.2.42, Ep.Jac.5.3, Dsc.4.82, Arr.Epict.4.6.14: metaph., D.C.71.36

κατισχναίνω.definition: cause to pine or waste away; reduce a swelling, Hp.Prog.23; Call.Epigr.47.3; weaken, Thphr.Od.47

κατισχνόομαι.definition: = J.AJ2.5.5, Gal.UP1.21, Aët.4.34:—Act., Hsch., Phot., Sch.Nic.Al.592

κατισχύω.definition: fut. Ev.Matt.16.18:—overpower, prevail; abs., have the upper hand, prevail, LXXEx.17.11, al.; to be superior in . . , Plb.11.13.3; Ev.Luc.23.23

κατοδύρομαι.definition: deplore, Pl.Ax.367d; D.S.13.58; X.Eph.5.1, cf. Parth.26.4:—Pass., to be mourned, Arch.Pap.1.220

κατοικέω.definition: settle in, colonize, Hdt.7.164; abs., settle, dwell, . . S.OC362; Ar.Av.153; E.Hel.1651, Pl.Lg.666e, etc.; Th.3.34; Isoc.1.36; Apoc.3.10; esp. of non-citizens, SIG352.4 . cf. 633.67 :—pf. and plpf. Pass., to have been…

κατοίκησις.definition: settling in a place; dwelling, abode, Pl.Ti.71b, Criti.115c, LXXGe.10.30, etc.; Ev.Marc.5.3; inhabited district, Ath.12.523e

κατοικία.definition: habitation, Hecat.119 J; settlement, colony, Str.5.4.11; esp. of military colonies in Egypt, PTeb.61.227 , etc.; also, = Lat. colonia, Str.6.2.5, Plu.Ant.16,App.BC5.19; foundation of colonies, Plu.Pomp.47

κατοικίδιος.definition: living in or about a house, domestic, Theopomp.Hist.258; Nic.Dam.56 J.; Gp.l.c., 2.35.5; Longus3.6; stay-at-home historians, Luc.Hist.Conscr.37; Ph.2.378, D.S.3.53; domestic means or methods of extension, Hp.Art.78; h…

κατοικίζω.definition: Cret. Schwyzer 175.2; c.acc.loci, colonize, people a place, A.Pr.725; Hdt.5.76, cf. E.Andr.295 , Th.6.76, etc.; Pl.Ep.357a; Ath.12.523e:—Pass., to be settled, Th.1.12, cf. 2.17; to be founded, established, Isoc.9.19; …

κατοίκισις.definition: settlement, Pl.R.453b, Lg.969c: pl., Th.6.77, App.BC5.19

κατοικισμός.definition: = foreg., in pl., Pl.Lg.683a, Arist.Mete.351b22; for habitation, J.AJ4.7.4

κατοικιστής.definition: founder of a city, Sm.Je.50.7, Hsch

κατοικοδομέω.definition: build upon or in a place; squander in building, Plu.Publ.15 )

κατοικτείρω.definition: intr., feel, show compassion, ask in compassion, Arist.Rh.1393b28; feel compassion at the thought that . . , Hdt.7.46

κατοικτίζω.definition: Att. fut. A.Supp.903: = foreg., c; causal, excite pity, . . S.OC1282

κατοίομαι.definition: to be conceited of oneself, LXXHb.2.5, Ph.Fr.99 H

κατοίχομαι.definition: have gone, the departed, dead, D.43.67, 60.8, Arist.VV1250b21, PGnom.17, Aret.SA2.4: sg., Nic.Fr.108, BMus.Inscr.1032.19 , 1032a

κατοκλάζω.definition: = Opp.C.3.473:—Med., Str.3.4.15; flag, grow inattentive, Anon.in Rh.233.17

κατοκνέω.definition: shrink from, c. inf., . . S.El.956; Hp.Mochl.20; Th.2.18; . . Isoc.1.19: c. acc., App.Mith.110: abs., shrink back, A.Pr.67, Th.2.94, Isoc.6.75, D.29.1, etc.; to be sluggish, Phld.Mus.p.30 K

κατοκωχή.definition: = possession, Anon. ap; being possessed, inspiration, Pl.Ion536c; Id.Phdr.245a, cf. Ph.1.174, al., Dam.Isid.32:—the forms are late and incorrect; cf

κατοκώχιμος.definition: held in possession, held as a; capable of being possessed by a feeling or passion, Arist.Pol.1342a8; Id.EN1179b9; possessed, Id.HA572a32; inclined, Id.Pol.1269b30: abs., frantic, Luc.JTr.30

κατολιγωρέω.definition: neglect utterly, Lys.9.16; abs., to be negligent, Diogenian.2.75, cf. PSI4.426.3 ; with contempt, Arist.Rh.Al.1421a15

κατολισθάνω.definition: later Gal.7.36, Agath.1.1: Ep. aor. 2 A.R.1.390: aor. 1 Alciphr.3.64: pf. Orib.50.42.3:—slip, sink down, Str.4.6.6; of hernia, Gal.l.c.; of a building, collapse, Agath.1.10: metaph., Luc.Abd.28, Alciphr. l.c.; Ael.Fr.…

κατόλλυμι.definition: in pf. Act., perish utterly, . . A.Pers.670

κατολοφύρομαι.definition: aor. 1 Diog.Oen.1:—bewail, c.acc., E.IT644 , X.Cyr.7.3.16; Diog.Oen. l.c.; D.H.5.12: abs., E.Or.339

κατομβρέομαι.definition: Pass., to be rained on, Plb.34.1.16, Str.16.1.5: metaph., AP7.389

κατομβρία.definition: heavy rain, Lyd.Ost.30, al.: pl., ib.58

κάτομβρος.definition: rainy, Arist.Vent.973b9; wet with rain, drenched, Thphr.CP3.12.1, 3.22.3: metaph., AP5.144

κατόμνυμι.definition: aor. E.Hel.835:—confirm by oath; c.acc., call to witness, swear by, E.Or.1517 , etc.; Ar.Ec.158: c. dupl. acc., E.Hel.l.c.: c.gen., Anon. ap. Suid

κατονομάζω.definition: name, Str.7.3.2, al.; ib.13.1.48; Pass., to be betrothed, c. dat., Plb.5.43.1, Hsch. s.v. to be devoted to the gods. D.H.1.16, Phalar.Ep.84.1

κατονομαξία.definition: Dor. for expression of numbers, Archim.Aren.1.7 :—also ib.3.1

κατοπτάω.definition: roast or bake thoroughly, Archestr.Fr.13.6, Phld.D. 1.19, Str.15.2.2, 16.4.13:—Pass., to be well baked, Arist.Aud.802b2, 803a29; to be overheated, of the blood, Gal.7.246

κατοπτήριος.definition: = Str.9.3.15; height which commands a view, Delph.3.136

κατόπτης.definition: = I, h.Merc.372, Hdt.3.17; one who visits or explores, Vett. Val.330.15; one who contemplates, Ph. Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10

κατοπτρίζω.definition: show as in a mirror or by reflexion; Med., look into a mirror, behold oneself in it, Zeno Stoic.1.66, S.E.P.1.48, Ath.15.687c, etc

κατοργιάζω.definition: initiate in orgies, prepare for them, Plu.Sol.12:— Pass., Id.2.766b, Fr.6.2, Luc.Trag.125

κατορθόω.definition: set upright, erect, E.Hipp.1445; metaph., keep straight, set right, . . S.El.416; Id.OC1487; make them prosper, D.18.290

κατόρθωμα.definition: that which is done rightly, virtuous action, in pl., opp. Chrysipp.Stoic.2.295, al., cf. IG5.268.15 , etc.; = Stoic.3.134

κατόρθωσις.definition: setting straight, of a fractured; setting up, LXXPs.96.2

κατορρωδέω.definition: Ion. , fear, dread, c. acc., Plb.14.1.5, Luc.Dem.Enc.3: abs., to be afraid, . . Plb.10.3.5, cf. Onos.11.3

κατουλόω.definition: cause to cicatrize, D.S.32.10, Dsc.5.74:—Pass., cicatrize, heal over, AP9.311 , Thessal. ap.Gal.10.250

κατοφρυόομαι.definition: to be furnished with eyebrows, in pf. part., Philostr.VA3.8: metaph., stern, severe words, Luc.Am.53

κατοχεύω.definition: have a female animal covered, LXXLe.19.19; pf. part. Pass. fertilized, Mitteis Chr.151.26

κατοψοφαγέω.definition: spend or waste in eating, Aeschin.1.95; eat greedily, Ph.2.479, Ath.5.186c

κάτω.definition: with Verbs implying Motion, downwards, Il.17.136; Od.23.91; Hdt.8.53; Ar.Pl.238; A.Pr.74; S.Ant.527 , cf. E.Fr.384; esp. of the nether world, A.Pers.839, S.Ant.197, etc.; Pl.R.500b, 584e; they suffered from diarrhoea,…

κατωμιστής.definition: throwing the rider over the shoulders, Hsch

κατωφέρεια.definition: propensity, Sch.D Il.24.30, cf. Sch. A.Ch.600; downward tendency, Eustr.in EN60.3

κατωφερής.definition: metaph., prone to vice, lewd, v.l. for in Apollod.Ath. ap. Ath.7.281f, cf. Vett. Val.18.3, EM451.2; Hsch. s.v

καυλίζομαι.definition: Pass., have a shaft, of a spear, Ar.Fr.404

καυλίσκος.definition: Dim. of I.1, Dsc.4.114; branch of a candlestick, J.BJ7.5.5

καυλοκοπία.definition: cutting of stalks, prob. in PCair.Preis.38.16

καυματίζω.definition: burn, scorch up, Apoc.16.8:—Pass., to be burnt up, Ev.Matt.13.6; become heated, suffer from heat, Plu.2.100b, 691f, Arr.Epict.1.6.26, Sor.1.108, M.Ant.7.64

καυστήρ.definition: cauterizing apparatus, Hp.Haem.6 ; in form Hippiatr.26, Gal.14.782; on the accent, v. Hdn.Gr.2.922

καυτήριον.definition: branding iron, E.Fr.815 , LXX4; burnt mark, brand, Str.5.1.9, BGU469.7

καυχάομαι.definition: Dor. Theoc.5.77; 2sg. in late Gr., as Ep.Rom.2.17, 23, etc.: fut. Hdt.7.39, Eup.134, Epicr.6: aor. Arist.Pol.1311b4; Sapph.Supp.4.2: pf. 2 Ep.Cor.7.14:—Act., EM527.1:— speak loud, be loud-tongued, Pi.O.9.38, cf. Eup.l…

καυχηματίας.definition: boaster, braggart, Ptol.Tetr.159, EM121.7; boastful, Sch.Il.13.373

καύχησις.definition: boasting, Epicur.Fr.93, LXX1 Ch.29.13, al., Phld.Vit.p.27 J., Ph.1.534, Ep.Rom.15.17

καχάζω.definition: Dor. fut. Theoc.5.142:—also in nasalized form S.Aj.198 , Babr.99.8, AP5.229 , 6.74 ; cf. aloud, S.Ichn.348, Ar.Ec.849, Anacreont.31.29, Luc.DMeretr.6.3; at one, Eub.8, Luc.Am.23; Theoc. l. c.; jeer, mock, S.Aj.l.c

καχεκτεύομαι.definition: to be in a miserable plight, BGU1141.31

καχεξία.definition: bad habit of body, opp; of the mind, bad disposition, disaffection, Diph.24, Nicol.Com.1.12, Plb.5.87.3, Hierocl.in CA7p.430M.: play on both meanings in Str.14.5.14

καχήμερος.definition: passing an unhappy day, AP9.508 ; v.l

καχλάζω.definition: also , usu. pres. and impf., plash or bubble, of the sound of liquids, Pi.O.7.2, cf. Philostr.VA3.25; of the sea, A.Th.761 , cf. 115 ; Theoc.6.12 , cf. Arr.An.5.20.8; ofrain, Lyc.80; of boiling water, Zos. Alch.p.109 …

καχυπονόητος.definition: = sq., cited in error by Poll.2.57 from Pl.Phdr.240e; v

καχύποπτος.definition: suspecting evil, suspicious, Ar.Fr.794, Pl.R.409c, Arist.Rh.1389b21

κεγχρίας.definition: like grains of millet. an; serpent with millet-like protuberances on the skin, Philum.Ven.22.1:—also Dsc.Ther.32; cf. III. III. in Poll.1.248, and are f.ll. for

κεγχρίνης.definition: is another species in Philum.Ven.26.1, Nic.Th.463, Lyc.912, Paul.Aeg.5.18

κεγχρίδιον.definition: Dim. of grain of seed like millet, Hsch

κέγχρινος.definition: made of millet, Dsc.5.3, cf.Gal.6.519; millet-pottage, Hsch

κεγχροειδής.definition: like grains of millet, interpol.in Hp.Prog.6; granulated work on silver cups, Ath.11.475b. Adv. Steph.in Hp.1.114 D

κεδαίω.definition: later Ep. for , in Pass., Arat.159, 410, A.R.2.626, Nic.Th.425; A.R.4.500; Hsch

κεδρία.definition: Ion. oil of Hdt.2.87, D.S.1.91, Dsc.1.77, Erot.s.v. cf

κέδρινος.definition: made from Hp.Mul.1.78, Arist.HA583a23; Dsc.5.36; orange-coloured dye, PHolm. 21.30

κειμήλιον.definition: anything stored up as; relic, PGrenf.2.111.1

κελαινεφής.definition: sync. for black with; generally, dark-coloured, 11.36, cf. Il.4.140; black, rich soil, Pi.P.4.52; Id.Fr.142

κελαινιάω.definition: to be black, in Ep.3pl. Opp.H.4.67; part. Nonn.D.38.18

κελαινόβρωτος.definition: black and bloody with gnawing, A.Pr.1025

κελαινόομαι.definition: Pass., grow black or dark, A.Ch.413

κελαινόρρινος.definition: with black skin or hide, Opp.H.5.18, Nonn.D.15.158: pl. S.Fr.29

κελαινόχρως.definition: black-coloured, AP9.251 , prob. l. in A.Supp.785 : also Man.4.261

κελαινώπας.definition: black-faced: hence, gloomy, S.Aj.955 :—fem. Pi.P.1.7:—also Hdn. Gr.1.188

κελάρυξις.definition: rushing sound, as of water, Hsch

κελεύθειος.definition: belonging to the road, Id.: epith. of Athena at Sparta, Paus.3.12.4

κέλευσις.definition: command, Plu.2.32c , Plot.4.8.2: freq. in Inscrr. and Pap., OGI589 , cf. 455.3 , BGU286.9 , etc.; IGRom.4.214 ; CIG5187b3

κέλευσμα.definition: or , order, command, A.Eu.235, S.Ant.1219 , etc.; call, summons, A.Ch.751 : in Prose, word of command in battle, Hdt.4.141, 7.16, cf. E.Hec.929 ; 1 Ep.Thess.4.16; also, the call of the , which gave the time to the row…

κελευστής.definition: boatswain, who gives the time to the rowers, E.Hel.1576, Ar.Ach.554, Th.2.84, X.HG5.1.8, Pl.Alc.1.125c, Phld. Rh.1.361 S., D.S.20.50, Arr.Fr.151 J

κελεύστωρ.definition: one who commands, more general than Phryn.PSp.81 B

κέλλα.definition: = Lat. cella, room, chamber, POxy.1128.15 , etc

κελλάριον.definition: Hdn.Gr.2.13], cupboard for glasses, POxy.741.12 , PLond.2.191.9 ; store-chamber, POxy.1851

κενεαγγίη.definition: Ion. for lowering or evacuant treatment, ibid., al., Aph.1.2, Coac.54; evacuation by bleeding, Aret.CD2.3

κενεμβατέω.definition: step on emptiness, Plu.Flam.10; step into; Medic., of a lancet, catheter, etc., reach a cavity, Orib.44.11.3, Gal.14.786, Paul.Aeg.6.59

κενεμβάτησις.definition: piercing of a cavity, Sor.2.62; 'emptiness' of the pulse, Gal.8.509, 931

κενεόφρων.definition: gen. empty-minded, Thgn.233; Simon.75, Pi.N.11.29:—also A.Pr.762

κενοδοξέω.definition: hold a vain opinion, Plb.12.26c.4; to be vain-glorious, Hld.9.19; f.l. for J.AJ16.11.1

κενοδοξία.definition: liability to vain imagination; vanity, conceit, Plb.3.81.9, LXXWi.14.14, D.S.17.107, Ph.2.47, Ep.Phil.2.3, Plu.2.57d, Porph.Marc.15; esp. of false prudery, Gal.6.415

κενόδοξος.definition: vain-glorious, conceited, Plb.27.7.12, Ph.1.672, Ep.Gal.5.26, Arr.Epict.3.24.43, Jul.Or.6.180d; Vett.Val.271.2

κενοδρομέω.definition: Astrol., to be without attendant planets, 'void of course', Ptol.Tetr.114, Man.2.486:—hence Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.107, Porph.in Ptol.189

κενολογία.definition: empty, idle talk, Plu.2.1069d; chicanery, PMasp.126.50 : v.l. for in Max.Tyr.23.1

κενοπονέω.definition: toil in vain, v.l. in Ph.1.658

κενοσπουδέω.definition: to be zealous about frivolities, J.AJ16.4.3, Artem.4.11

κενοσπουδία.definition: zealous pursuit of frivolities, D.H.6.70, D.L.6.26; M.Ant.7.3

κενόσπουδος.definition: zealous about frivolities, Hipparch.1.3.11, Plu.2.560b, 1061c; 'more haste, less speed', Heliod. ap.Orib.47.14.3; D.L.9.67; matters of mere curiosity, Cic. Att.9.1.1. Adv. Plu.2.234e

κενοτάφιον.definition: empty tomb, cenotaph, X.An.6.4.9; image, = Heb. těraphim, LXX1 Ki.19.13

κενοφωνία.definition: vain talking, Dsc.Praef.2: in pl., 1 Ep.Ti.6.20, 2 Ep.Ti.2.16, Porph.Chr.58; Just.Nov.146.1.2

Κενταυρίδης.definition: sprung from Centaurs, a Thessalian horse, Id.Ind.5

Κενταυρομαχία.definition: battle of Centaurs, D.S.17.115, Plu.Thes.29, Comp.Thes.Rom.1

κεντηναρία.definition: office of such a value, IG14.1480

κεντητήριον.definition: pricker, awl, Luc.Cat.20; gloss on Gal.19.134; gloss on Suid

κεντρίζω.definition: = X.Eq.11.6: metaph., Id.Smp.8.24; Plu.2.84c; stimulate, Sor.2.54:—Pass., X.Cyr.8.7.12; Ph.2.386

κεντρίνης.definition: spiny shark, Arist.Fr.310; kind of or fig-insect, Thphr.HP2.8.2, Plin.HN17.255

κέντριον.definition: a surgical instrument, called modern spelling of Gal.13.407; = Suid., cf. EM503.39

κεντρίσκος.definition: a kind of fish, Thphr.Fr.171.9; Schneid

κεντρίτης.definition: prickly reed, PTeb.152; fem. place where a horse is tapped for dropsy, Hippiatr.38

κεντρομυρσίνη.definition: = butchers' broom, Ruscus aculeatus, Thphr.HP3.17.4, Gp.10.3.7

κεντροτύπος.definition: Act., striking with a goad; proparox., = EM503.47, cf. Hsch

κεντροφόρος.definition: with a sting, Id. s.v; Subst., = I, Opp.H.4.244

κέντρων.definition: one that bears the marks of the; piece of patch-work, rag, Bito55.4, Heras ap.Gal.13.1044, Sch.Ar.Nu.449; perh.pen-wiper, POxy.326 : hence, copy of verses made up of scraps from other authors, Eust.1099.51, 1308 fin

κέντρωσις.definition: goading, piercing, Sch.Pi.P.1.54; Astron., situation at cardinal point, Ptol.Tetr.79, 99

κεραμεία.definition: the potter's craft, Pl.Prt.324e: prov., of those who undertake the most difficult tasks without learning the elements of the art, Id.Grg.514e, cf.La.187b, Dicaearch. Hist.51; of the same make, Eratosth. ap. Ath.11.482b

κεραμεύς.definition: Att. name of an Attic deme, Ar.Ra.1093 , Pl.Prt.315d, etc

κεραμεύω.definition: to be a potter, Phryn.Com.15, Pl.R.467a; c. acc., make earthenware cups, Epig.4; he tinkers the state, of the demagogue Cephalos, whose father was a potter, Ar.Ec.253; make a pot of the potter, Pl.Euthd.301d; i.e. dis…

κεραμήϊος.definition: Ep. for Nic.Th.80, cf. II:—fem. Marc.Sid.60

κεραμιδόω.definition: make a roof as of shields to protect the soldiers , Apollon.Lex. s.v. Hsch. s.v. to be roofed or coped with tiles, . . Arist.Ph.246a28

κεραμίς.definition: Diph.84, Ion. and later; = PLond.3.1177.158 , PIand.12.3

κεραμῖτις.definition: of or for pottery, potter's earth, Hp.Morb.1.17, 3.1, Plu.2.827e, Gal.2.137; a gem of the colour of potsherds, Plin.HN37.152 .169, cf. 8.190)

κεραμόω.definition: roof with tiles, IG12.373.246, 22.1668.58, al., 8.270:—Pass., SIG 996.18 , cf. Simp.in Ph.1055.17; of soldiers in the Roman testudo, Onos.20.1

κεραμύλλιον.definition: Dim. of jar, IG11.161 C101 , PCair.Zen.12.35 , Inscr.Délos 442B179 , Aq.Is.63.3

κεραμών.definition: store for pottery or tiles, Hdn.Gr.1.32, 40

κερατίζω.definition: butt with horns: metaph., LXXEz.32.2, cf. Ph.1.57: c.acc., gore, LXXEx.21.28

κερατίνης.definition: the fallacy called the Horns: D.L.7.187; Com.Adesp.294: acc.sg. Luc.Symp.23; cf

κεράτινος.definition: made of horn, X.An.6.1.4, Pl. Com.50, etc.; Epicr.8; = Plu.2.983e, cf. Arist.Fr.489; LXXPs.97.6; also alone, ib.Jd.3.27, 2 Ki.2.28

κερατισμός.definition: loss on exchange of solidi for PMasp.58 ii 11 , Lyd.Mag.3.70

κερατῖτις.definition: horned, horned poppy, Glaucium flavum, Thphr.HP9.12.3, Dsc.4.65, Plin. HN20.205

κερατογλύφος.definition: working in horn, Sch.D Il.4.110, EM505.11

κερατοειδής.definition: like horn, external coat of; applied to a part of the coat, opp. Ruf.Onom.27, cf. Gal.UP10.3

κερατών.definition: made of horns , of an altar on Delos, IG22.1641.2 , 11.161A101 , Inscr.Délos 442 A188 , Plu.Thes.21

κεραύνιον.definition: truffle, Tuber aestivum, Thphr.HP1.6.5; critical mark to indicate corrupt passages, Isid.Etym.1.21.21, Sch.Il.ip.xliii Dind.; but D.L.3.66

κεραύνιος.definition: thunder-smitten, of Semele, S.Ant.1139 , E.Ba.6; Id.Supp.496; the 'thunder-splitten peaks', name of several mountain ridges, Str.6.3.5, etc

κεραυνόβλητος.definition: struck by lightning, Ephor.17 J., Sch.S.Ant.1139, Hsch. s.v. Suid. s.v

κεραυνοβολέω.definition: hurl the thunderbolt, AP12.122; trans., strike therewith, Eratosth.Cat.6

κεραυνοβόλος.definition: hurling the thunder, IG5.37; proparox. Pass., thunder- stricken, of Semele, E.Ba.598 , cf. D.S.1.13, etc

κεραυνοκλόνος.definition: causing the din of the thunderbolt, PMag.Par.1.599

κεραυνοσκοπεῖον.definition: machine for making thunder on the stage, Poll.4.127,130

κεραυνοσκοπία.definition: divination by thunder and lightning, D.S.5.40

κεραυνοφόρος.definition: wielding the thunderbolt, Plu.Alc.16, cf. 2.335a; Legio XII Fulminata, D.C.55.23: as Subst., title of a priest at Seleucia in Pieria, OGl1245.47

κεραύνωσις.definition: striking with thunder, Str.16.2.7, Plu.2.996c ; Scymn.398

κερβολέω.definition: = Hsch.; perh. to be read in B.1.34

κερδαίνω.definition: fut. A.Pr.876, Lys.8.20, etc.; Ion; in bad sense, reap disadvantage from a thing, E.Hec.518; X.Ap.9

κερδαλεόφρων.definition: gen. greedy of gain, Il.1.149, 4.339; crafty, Opp.C.2.29

κερκῖτις.definition: a kind of olive , prob. in Colum.5.8.3

κερκούριον.definition: Dim. of only as pr. n. of a AP5.43

κερμάτιον.definition: Dim. of Philippid.23, Plu.Cim.10, Arr.Epict.3.2.8, AP11.346 , Phld.Vit.p.27 J. ; Men.Her.7; cash, PHib.1.45.8 , al

κερνοφόρος.definition: priest or priestess who bears it, Nic.Al.217; Ps.-Plu.Fluv.13.3; Poll.4.103, Ath.14.629d

κεροβάτης.definition: horn-footed, hoofed, Ar.Ra.230 : acc. to some Gramm., he that goes with horns, i.e. the horned god; acc. to Sch., he that walks the mountain-peaks

κεροπλάστης.definition: arranging the hair in horns or queues , hairdresser, Archil.57, Poll.2.31, Hsch

κερουτιάω.definition: prop. of horned animals, toss the horns: metaph., of persons, toss the head, give oneself airs, Ar.Eq.1344:—hence hauteur, Phot

κερτόμιος.definition: mocking, taunting, Od.24.240; Il.5.419; simply 1.539, cf. Od.9.474; S.Ant.956 ; ib.962 . cf

κέρχνος.definition: = Hsch. s.v. cf. Anaxandr.41.27, Gal.18.574; rough excrescence

κεστρεύς.definition: mullet, = Hp.Int.30, Ar.Fr.156, Pl.Com.29, Arist.HA591a22, Antig.Mir.93, Hices.and Dorio ap.Ath.7.307d, Alciphr.1.7; as nickname of a starveling , Euphro2; prov. of those too honest to make gains, Ath.7.307c, cf. Lib.…

κεστροφύλαξ.definition: officer in charge of II, ib.1094, al.:—hence ib.735, 736

κευθμών.definition: hiding place, hole; of the nether world, Hes.Th.158; the deep black vault of T., A.Pr.222; E.Hec.1; Id.Hipp.732 .—Rare in Prose, as Str.11.2.10

κεφαλαία.definition: inveterate headache, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.13.1, Aret.SD1.2, Gal.10.513; prob. in Thphr.HP9.11.2

κεφάλαιος.definition: of the head: metaph; mostly Subst. = head, parts about the head, esp. of fish, Callias Com.3: in pl., Amphis35, Sotad. Com.1.5; also Ar.Nu.981; of an infant, Leonid. ap. Aët.6.1

κεφαλαίωσις.definition: comprehension of several notions in a general term, Sch.S.OC916

κεφαλαλγέω.definition: suffer from headache, Hp.Aph.5.64, Sor.2.29, Dsc.1.30, Arr.Epict.3.22.73, Gal.6.589, BCH48.517

κεφαλαλγής.definition: suffering from headache, Plu.2.147f; Act., causing headache, X.An.2.3.15, Thphr.HP8.4.6, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.54a, Ph.1.390, 2.99, Plu.2.133c, Gal.17.818, etc

κεφαλαλγία.definition: headache, in pl., Hp.Aph.3.13, Arist.Pr.860a37, Str.16.2.41, IG42.126.27

κεφαλαργία.definition: later form for Luc.Jud.Voc.4:— hence PMag.Par.1.136; give one a headache, Hsch. s.v

κεφαληγερέτης.definition: Dor. head- collector, Comic epith. of Pericles, formed after the Homeric from the peaked shape of his skull, Cratin.240

κεφαλίδιον.definition: Dim. of Poll.2.42; as an article of food, POxy.1656.22

κεφαλίνη.definition: root of the tongue, supposed to be the seat of taste, hence also called Poll.2.107

κεφάλιον.definition: Dim. of as an ornament, IG22.1466.13, cf. Dsc.4.148, Sor.1.119, al., Plu.2.641b; of a person, Sammelb.5807.12

κεφαλίς.definition: Dim. of little head; capital of a column, Ph.2.147, Chor.p.118 B. , PLond. 3.755v6 , Gp.14.6.6 : pl., = Eust.903.6

κεφαλισμός.definition: multiplication table of single numbers from one to ten, Arist.Top.163b25 , cf. Suid

κεφαλοβαρής.definition: with a head at the root, of bulbous plants, Arist.Long.467a34, Thphr.HP1.6.8

κεφαλόβρωτος.definition: eaten away at the top, Arch.Pap.6.101

κεφαλοειδής.definition: shaped like a head, Hp.Int.6; Dsc.2.110; Apollod.Poliorc.220.20; Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.36

κεφαλόθλαστος.definition: bruised in the head: contusions of the head, Thphr.HP9.20.4

κεφαλόπους.definition: in pl., lamb's or goat's trotters, Cass.Fel.40

κεφαλοτομέω.definition: cut off the head, less Att. than Thphr. ap.AB104, cf. Phryn.320

κηδεία.definition: care for the dead, funeral, A.R.2.836; connexion by marriage, alliance, E.Supp.134; X.Mem.2.6.36; Plb.1.9.2; . . Arist.Pol.1262a11; ib.1280b36; ib.1307a39

κηδεμονεύω.definition: to be a guardian, Just.Nov.94.2:—Pass., to be a ward, ib.18.9

κηδεμονία.definition: care, solicitude, Pl.R.463d, Phld.Mort.25, Ph.2.179, D.C.43.17, POxy.1070.21 ; the general charge of her affairs, IG3.632, cf. CIG3187 ; BGU372i12

κηδέστρια.definition: female attendant, keeper, PTeb.378.4; mother-in-law, Gloss

κηδεύω.definition: take charge of, tend.S.OT1323; esp. attend to a corpse, bury, S.El.1141, cf.E.Rh.983; IG14.1860: also in Prose, Plb.5.10.4, etc.; Demad.9, cf. Plu.Alex.56; Arist.Fr.519, cf. Wilcken Chr.499 ; J.AJ14.7.4; CIG3028.3 , c…

κῆδος.definition: Dor. care about, c.gen; esp. for the dead, funeral rites, mourning, Il.5.156, etc.; 4.270; mourning for them, 22.272; Archil.9, cf. A.Ch.469 , Plu.Sol.12, etc.: sg., Pi.P.4.112, cf. N.1.54; when there is a death in th…

κηλάστρα.definition: milk-pail, Hsch; holly, Ilex Aquifolium, Id.: —also Thphr.HP3.4.5, 4.1.3:—more freq. ib.1.9.3, 3.3.1, al

κηλέω.definition: charm, bewitch, beguile, esp. by music, E.Alc.359; Pl.Ly.206b; Id.Prt.315a, cf.Luc.Ind.12; of Pericles as an orator, Eup.94.6; charm by incantation, Pl.Phdr.267d; Achae.17.2; of bribery, Theopomp.Com.30:—Pass., Archil…

κήλημα.definition: charm, spell, in pl., Ibyc.2, E.Tr.893: sg., Id.Hyps.Fr.26

κηλήτης.definition: one who is ruptured, Str.17.3.4, Gal.10.988, D.C.73.2, AP11.342, Luc.Epigr.39:—Att. Phryn.PSp.81 B

κηλιδόω.definition: Ecphant. :—stain, soil, Arist.Insomn.460a12 :—Pass., D.C.77.11: metaph., defile, sully, E.HF1318, Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.7.64:—Pass., Ph.1.156

κηλώνειον.definition: Ion. = foreg. I, Hdt.1.193, 6.119, Ar.Fr.679, Arist.Mech.857a34, Aen.Tact.39.7, PCair.Zen.155 , Gal.UP7.7:—written Apollod.Poliorc.162.8, al

κημόω.definition: muzzle a horse, X.Eq.5.3; Medic., = Sch.Ar.Eq.1147

κηπαῖος.definition: of or from a garden; garden-door, back-door, Hermipp.47.9, cf.Poll.1.76; prov., 'by the back-stairs', D.L.7.25, cf. Gal.2.98

κηπεία.definition: in pl., gardens, Pl.Lg.845d, D.S.5.43, J.BJ5.2.2

κήπευμα.definition: garden, Ar.Av.1100, cf. Apollod.Hist. ap. Ath.15.682d, Dicaearch.1.13

κηπεύω.definition: rear in a garden, Luc.VH1.34; cultivate like a garden, Thphr.CP4.6.7 , Hld.9.4 : metaph., vivify, freshen, E.Hipp.78; Philostr.VA2.26

κηπολόγος.definition: teaching in a garden, of Epicureans, AP6.307

κηποπαράδεισος.definition: garden and orchard in one, PSI8.917.5

κηποτάφιον.definition: tomb in a garden, BGU1120.7 :—also or Papers of Amer.Sch.at Athens3.621 : cf. Lat.cepotaphium

κηποτύραννος.definition: tyrant of the garden, epith. of the Epicurean philosopher Apollodorus, D.L.10.25

κηπουρός.definition: keeper of a garden; gardener, IG22.10 , Thphr.HP7.2.5, PCair.Zen.59.6 , Plb.18.6.4, Ev.Jo.20.15, Philostr.Her.Prooem.2, CIG4082 ; title of play by Antiph.:—also Archipp.44, Pl.Min.316e, PFay.101rii4

κηρέλαιον.definition: wax-oil, a kind of salve, Gal.6.445, 13.953

κηρίνη.definition: = II, Hsch., Phot; name of a plaster, Asclep. ap. Gal.13.936

κηριοελκός.definition: one who makes wax lights, PRyl.374.3

κηριόομαι.definition: Pass., to be panic-stricken, Hsch. , Suid., prob. in Anacreont.13.18

κηριτρεφής.definition: born to misery, Hes.Op.418, cf. Orac. ap. Sch.E.Ph.638

κηρίων.definition: wax light, waxen torch, Plu.2.263f; whip, Hsch. and Phot.s.v

κλώσσω.definition: cluck, prob. in Suid. s.v. cf

κνήκινος.definition: of or from PRev.Laws53.15, al. , PTeb. 122.11 , Dsc.1.36

κνηστρίον.definition: scraper, Edict.Diocl. in IG5.1115 Bi 14, 15 :—in late form IG3.238a; cf. Gloss
