κνισαλέος.definition: filled with the steam of fat, Hsch

κνισάω.definition: fill with the savour of burnt sacrifice, make them steam with sacrifice, Ar.Eq.1320, Av.1233, Orac. ap. D.21.51; E.Alc.1156; intr., raise the steam of sacrifice on . . , Orac. ap. D.21.52; Luc.JTr.22

κνισοδιώκτης.definition: Fat-hunter, name of a mouse, v.l. Batr.232

κνισοκόλαξ.definition: dinner-parasite, Asius1, cf. Phryn.PSp.81 B. cod

κνισολοιχία.definition: love of fat or roast meat, Sophil.5

κνισόω.definition: = MatroConv.82: metaph., Ph.1.628. II. turn into fatty smoke, in Pass., savoury bait, Arist.HA534b5; Antyll. ap. Orib.10.19.4; Gal.8.37, cf. 6.691, 706; Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.17. 2. burn the soup, Luc.Sat.23. III. Pass., bec…

κνυζέομαι.definition: prop. of a dog, whine, whimper, S.OC1571 , cf. Theoc.6.30; S.Fr.722, cf. Ar.V.977; of children, D.H.1.79; Theoc.2.109:—also Act. Poll.5.64 , Opp.C.1.507: , Ael.NA1.8, 11.14: Gal.19.112, Hsch.; for Sophr.53

κνυζηθμός.definition: prop. of dogs, whining, whimpering, opp. barking or snarling, Od.16.163; of wild beasts, A.R.3.884; of young bears, Opp.C.3.169 ; of children, Ath.9.376a

κνύζημα.definition: = foreg., of infants, Hdt.2.2, Him.Or.23.4, cf. Max. Tyr.41.3

κνωδακοφύλαξ.definition: warder of the pivot of the celestial sphere, PMag.Par.1.678

κνωδάλιον.definition: Dim. of sq., prob. in Hsch.s.v

κνώδαλον.definition: any wild creature, Od.17.317; Hes.Th.582; but also, of an ox or ass, h.Merc.188; of beasts generally, A.Ch.601 ; of birds and beasts, Id.Supp.1000; ib.264; of sea- monsters, Alcm.60.5, cf. A.Ch.587 ; Id.Pr.462; S.Fr.9…

κνώσσω.definition: slumber, Od.4.809, Simon.37.6, Pi.O.13.71, P.1.8, Theoc.21.65, AP5.293.11 , etc.: prov., 'you sleep like a top', Herod.8.10

κοβαλεύω.definition: carry as a porter, POxy.146 ; PLond.1.131r.296 , cf. EM524.28, Suid

κογχίον.definition: Dim. of Antiph.71, Str.16.4.17; = II.1, Gal.14.701

κογχύλιον.definition: Dim. of small kind of mussel; any mollusc or its shell, Hdt.2.12, Hp.Vict.2.48, Diocl.Fr.133; used to cover seals, Sch.Ar.V.583; fossil shell, Plu.2.367b

κοδομεύς.definition: one who roasts barley, Hsch., perh. to be read in Ostr.Strassb. 583 :—fem. Poll.1.246, Phot

κοέω.definition: contr. mark, perceive, hear, Epich.35 ; Anacr.4.14; Hellad. in Phot.Bibl.p.531 B.; Call.Fr.53, cf. Sch.Ar.Eq.198: etym. of Corn.ND17:—also and Hsch.; . . Id

κοιλάς.definition: Subst., hollow, Ps.-Phoc.173; Adj., fem. of Thphr.Sign.51 ; Tryph.194

κοιλασία.definition: in pl., indentations in beams, HeroBel.104.2

κοίλασμα.definition: hollow, LXXIs.8.14; groove, Apollod.Poliorc.182.7, Ath.Mech.36.6; interior of a lamp, HeroSpir.2.22

κοιλέμβολον.definition: hollow wedge, as an order of battle, Ael.Tact.37.7, Arr.Tact.29.6:—Adj. Ascl.Tact.11.5

κοιλία.definition: Ion. cavity of the body; belly, abdomen, Hdt.2.87, IG42.122.32 , etc.: specified as Ar.Ra.485, Hp.Ulc.3, Pl.Ti.73a, 85e, Arist.Somn.Vig.456a3, PA650a13, etc.; opp. stomach, Pl.Ti.85e, Arist.PAl.c.; alone freq. = stoma…

κοιλιαλγέω.definition: have pain in the bowels, Id.14.467

κοιλιολυσία.definition: looseness of the bowels, to take laxative medicine, Cic.Att.10.13.1, cf. Sor.1.46, AB323

κοιλιολυτέω.definition: suffer from looseness of the bowels, Hsch. s.v

κοιλογάστωρ.definition: hollow-bellied, hungry, A.Th.1040: metaph., of a hollow shield, ib.496

κοιλογένειος.definition: with a dimple in the chin, PPetr.3p.26 , PGrenf.1.10.13, 1.34.4

κοιλοσταθμέω.definition: provide with a coffered ceiling or panels, LXX3 Ki.6.9; ib.15

κοιλόσταθμος.definition: with coffered ceilings, panelled, ib.Hg.1.4; PPetr.3p.143 :—Subst. coffered ceiling, . . IG11.287 A96 :—also ib.B 146

κοιλοφθαλμιάω.definition: have sunken eyes, Cratin.288, Gal.6.444, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.98, Orib.Eup.1.13

κοίλωμα.definition: hollow, cavity, Arist.Spir.483b23; basin into which rivers discharge, Plb.4.39.2 , 8; bed of a torrent, Id.4.70.7: generally, of hollow places, low-lying land, LXXGe.23.2, Agatharch.32; BGU571.12 ; excavation, PPetr.2…

κοίλωσις.definition: cavity, Hp.Carn.15, Sor.1.82; hollowing out, of flutes, Nicom.Harm.4,10

κοίμησις.definition: lying down to sleep; the sleep of death, LXXSi.46.19, 48.13, Tab.Defix.Aud.242.30

κοίμισις.definition: putting to sleep, IG12.329; softening of the accent, Sch.D.T.p.23 H

κοινάριον.definition: Dim. of , in form cynarium, CIL13.10021.199

κοινισμός.definition: mixture of dialects, v.l. in Quint.8.3.59

κοινοβούλιον.definition: common council, Plb.28.19.1, Str.8.7.3, OGI490.12 , 568.11 , etc.; place of assembly, App.BC1.51

κοινόβουλος.definition: gloss on Sch.Ar.Th.928; Subst. member of local senate, IGRom.3.7

κοινοδήμιον.definition: common assembly of the people, Hsch

κοινόδημος.definition: common to the people, public, Ph.1.678

κοινόδικος.definition: enjoying a common right, Orac. ap. Phleg.1 J

κοινοκρατηρόσκυφος.definition: filling his cup from the common bowl, Cerc.4.16

κοινολεκτέω.definition: use the language of common life, A.D.Adv.169.20, cf. EM184.11

κοινόλεκτος.definition: in the language of common life: Adv. Sch.Theoc.6.18

κοινόλεκτρος.definition: bedfellow, consort, A.Ag.1441: as Adj., Id.Pr.560

κοινολογέομαι.definition: fut. Plb.21.39.2: aor; Pass., signs used with common significance, opp. Porph.VP12

κοινολογία.definition: consultation, Hp.Praec.8, PFay.12.15; discussion, conference, Plb.2.8.7, al., Plu.Ages.25, al., Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.296.23; philosophical dialogue, Phld.Rh.1.109: pl., ib.243 S

κοινονοημοσύνη.definition: regard for the feelings of others, M.Ant.1.16

κοινόπλοος.definition: contr. sailing in common, i.e. shipmates, S.Aj.872

κοινοποιέω.definition: make common property; generalize, Herm.in Phdr.p.128 A., Simp.in Ph.1275.6; shows the common ground of their view and that of D., Id.in Cael.617.22:—Med., Alex. Aphr.in SE17.13

κοινοπολιτεία.definition: citizenship of a or league, SIG622 B12

κοινοπραγία.definition: common enterprise, joint or concerted action, Plb.5.95.2, D.S.11.1, 15.8, Plu.Per.17

κοινοφαγία.definition: eating of what is common or profane, J.AJ11.8.7

κοινών.definition: Dor., , = which is much more freq., X.Cyr.7.5.35, 8.1.16, 36, 40; of partners in a tax-farming syndicate, PRev.Laws 10.10, al

κοινωνέω.definition: have a share of, take part in a thing, A.Supp.325; Id.Ch.165; Id.Th.1038; S.Tr.546; E.Or.1055; Id.Med.302; X.Mem.2.6.22; Arist.Pol.1268a18, etc.; share all things in common, ib.1257a22; SIG1106.7 ; Inscr.Magn.44.19 ; …

κοινωνία.definition: communion, association, partnership; joint-ownership, PLond.2.311.2 , etc

κοινωνός.definition: also companion, partner, of or; abs., partner, fellow, S.Aj.284, Pl.R.333b, Phdr.239c, etc.; D.18.21; Arist.EN1133b3; of a societas publicanorum which farmed harbour-dues, BCH10.267 ; of joint-owners, PAmh. 2.100

κοινωφελής.definition: of common utility, Ph.2.404, al., Gal.14.296, POxy.1409.19 , Just.Nov.7.2.1: Comp., Max.Tyr.41.1: Sup., Ph.1.389

κοινωφελία.definition: common utility, Phld.Rh.1.174 S. , D.S.1.51: on the form , cf. EM462.21

Κοιογενής.definition: born of Coios, i.e. Latona, Pi.Fr.88.2:—fem. A.R.2.710

κοιρανίδης.definition: member of a ruling house, S.Ant.940 , Sammelb.5829

κοιτάζω.definition: put to bed, Hsch.; esp. of cattle; Med., Dor. aor. go to bed, sleep, Pi.O.13.76, cf. LXXDe.6.7

κοιτίς.definition: Dim. of VI, box, AP6.254.6 , Philostr.VA4.39; v.l. for in Hld.4.11; gloss on Sch.A.R.3.802; basket, Men.Epit.164; Arr.An.3.4.3; of Moses' ark, J.AJ2.9.5

κόκκινος.definition: scarlet, Herod.6.19, Ep.Hebr.9.19; Subst. scarlet clothes, Arr.Epict.3.22.10, 4.11.34; PHolm.21.41: sg., LXXEx.25.4

κοκκίον.definition: Dim. of I, Dsc.3.55; Dim. of III, pill, Gal.12.496, Alex. Trall.5.4

κοκκολογέω.definition: sift grains of weeds from wheat, POxy.1031.16 ; = Lat. racemor, Dosith.p.432 K., Gloss

κοκκυγέα.definition: wig-tree, Rhus Cotinus, cj. in Thphr.HP3.16.6, cf. Plin.HN13.121:—but , Hsch

κοκκύγινος.definition: purple-red, and dye red, Hsch. s.v

κοκκυμηλέα.definition: plum-tree, Prunus domestica, Arar.20, Thphr.HP3.6.4, Dsc.1.121, Gal.12.32; sebesten, Cordia Myxa, Thphr.HP4.2.10

κοκκύμηλον.definition: plum, Archil.173, Hippon.81, Alex.272.5, Thphr.HP1.10.10, Gal.6.613

κολαβρισμός.definition: name of such dance, Ath.14.629d; Pass., to be derided, LXXJb.5.4

κόλαβρος.definition: a song to which the was; young pig, Hsch., Suid

κολάζω.definition: fut. And.1.136, Lys.31.29, X.Cyr.7.5.8; chastise, punish, E.Ba.1322, Ar.Nu.7, etc.; use your proud words in reproving them, S.Aj.1108: c. dat. modi, ib.1160; E.Hel.1172, Lys.28.3; Pl.Lg.784d, Isoc.1.50; Pl.Plt.309a:—M…

κολακεία.definition: flattery, fawning, Democr.268, Pl.R.590b, Grg.463c, 465b, Thphr.Char.2, etc.; Aeschin.3.162, cf.Cic.Att.13.27.1; title of treatise by Phld

κολάκευμα.definition: piece of flattery, X.Oec.13.12; of a person, Sch.S.Aj.381

κολακευτέος.definition: to be flattered, Luc.Merc; one must flatter, Ap.Ty.Ep.7, Sch.rec.A.Th.705

κολακεύω.definition: c. acc., flatter, And.4.16, X.HG5.1.17, Isoc.4.155, Ephipp.6, etc.; Pl.Alc.1.120b: metaph., Muson.Fr.18A p.97 H.:—Pass., to be flattered, be open to flattery, Democr.115, D.8.34, etc

κολάπτω.definition: carve, engrave, ib.9.341 ; IG14.256 , cf. 952 , 1.30 , Luc.Dips.6, PLeid.X.36

κόλασις.definition: checking the growth of trees, esp; chastisement, correction, Hp.Praec.5, Pl.Ap.26a, al., Th.1.41; opp. Arist.Rh.1369b13; of divine retribution, Ev.Matt.25.46, al.: pl., Pl.Prt.323e, al., Phld.Ir.p.52 W

κόλασμα.definition: chastisement, Ar.Fr.385, X.Cyr.3.1.23, Critias25.4 D., AP5.217.7

κολαστήριος.definition: Subst. house of correction, Luc.Nec.14, VH2.30; instrument of correction, of the whips of Xerxes, Plu.2.342f

κολαστής.definition: chastiser, punisher, A.Pers.827, cf. S.OT1148, E.Heracl.388, Pl.Lg.863a, Epicur.Sent.34, Phld.Mort.17, etc.; Lys.27.3, cf. Gorg.Fr.6; Critias25.6 D.; tormentor, in Hades, Plu.2.567d

κολαφίζω.definition: slap, buffet, Ev.Matt.26.67, Sammelb.6263.23:— Pass., 1 Ep.Cor.4.11

κόλαφος.definition: buffet, = Epich.1 , cf. Hsch.,Gloss.; cf. Lat. colaphus

κολλαβίζω.definition: play a game, in which one holds his eyes, while the other strikes him, and bids him guess which hand he has been struck with, Poll.9.129

κολλάω.definition: join one metal or other substance to another, i.e. make [a crown] inlaid with gold and ivory, Pi.N.7.78:—Pass., glued together, opp. Ar.Eq.463; welded iron, Plu.2.619a; POxy.1449.23

κολλήγας.definition: = Lat. collega, IG14.1063 : gen. pl., Sammelb.7252.25

κολλητής.definition: one who glues or fastens, PTeb.316.70 , Sammelb.805 , Gloss

κολλούρα.definition: roll or loaf of bread, PLond.ined.2172; cf

κολλυβιστής.definition: small money-changer, Lys.Fr.149 S., Men.1023, PPetr. 3p.173 , Ev.Matt.21.12, etc.: condemned by Phryn.404

κολλύρα.definition: prob. = I, Ar.Pax123, Fr.413; used of , Thphr. ap. Hsch

κολλύριον.definition: Dim. of pessary; eye-salve, Apoc.3.18, IG14.966.16 , PFlor.177.20 ; stamped with the physician's seal, CIL13.10021.64, al.: freq. in pl., Arr.Epict.2.21.20, 3.21.21, etc.; salve in general, POxy.1088 :—on 1.1 and 1.2,…

κολλυριοποιέομαι.definition: to be made into collyrium, Dsc.Eup.1.197

κολοβοδιέξοδος.definition: having a curtailed passage, of stars whose rising and setting is invisible owing to sunrise and sunset, Ptol.Phas.p.8 H., al

κολοβοκέρατος.definition: with stunted horns, short-horned, Sch. Il.16.117

κολοβομάχη.definition: the interrupted battle, name for Il. 8, Sch.B Il.8 init.; also Sch.Leid.Il.13.745 in Valck. Animadv.ad Ammon.p.181; cf. 3

κολοκύνθινος.definition: made or obtained from gourds; a kind of vine, PCair.Zen.33.14

κολόκυνθος.definition: = AP9.532 tit., PLond.5.1881 ; Ps.-Dsc.4.176:— written PTeb.131

κολοσσιαῖος.definition: colossal, D.S.11.72 , al.; Ph.1.2; Luc.Herm.71; Hdn.1.15.9, BGU362 vi 5

κόλουσμα.definition: that which is cut off, a piece, Hsch

κολπάριον.definition: Dim. of III.6, Archig. ap. Aët.9.39

κολπίας.definition: swelling in folds, A.Pers.1060; name of a wind, blowing from the gulf, Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10, Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.33

κολπίζω.definition: form into a bosom or fold, Suid

κολπόω.definition: form into a swelling fold; esp. make a sail belly, . . AP9.363.10 ; Luc.VH1.9; ib.13:—Pass., swell out, of membranes, Hp.Nat.Puer.16; Arist.HA510b32; of Europa's garment, Mosch.2.129; AP10.5 ; of a bay, curve, Plb.34.…

κόλπωμα.definition: bellying or bulging out, of the; garment with ample folds, worn by kings in Tragedy, Poll.4.116, An.Par.1.19

κολυμβητής.definition: one who draws water from a well, Hsch

κολυμβίς.definition: diver, name of a bird, prob. grebe, Podiceps minor, Ar.Av.304, Arist.HA593b17, Alex.Mynd. ap. Ath.9.395d; cf. II.1: as Adj., Arat.296

κόλυμβος.definition: = Paus.2.35.1, cf.Str.16.2.42, AP9.82 , Plu.2.162f , Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.39.3, Antyll.ib.6.27.4, X.Ep.3.2

κόμβος.definition: roll, band, girth, Anon. ap. Suid.; cf

κομβόω.definition: bind up, fasten, Gloss.:—Med., gird oneself, Hsch

κόμβωμα.definition: robe, Id.: in pl., ornamental bands, Suid

κομίστρια.definition: fem. of = AB 267, Hsch.; as epith. of Nature, Orph.H.10.16

κομμάτιον.definition: Dim. of II.1: in pl., small logs; metrical phrase, Eup.362

κομμόω.definition: beautify, embellish, Arist.SE164b20, cf. Luc.Bis Acc.31 ; Them.Or.27.336c, cf. Or.28.343b:—Med., Eup.421

κόμμωσις.definition: embellishment, Ath.13.568a; stop-wax, prob. in Arist.HA623b31, cf. Plin.HN11.16, Hsch

κομμωτής.definition: dresser, esp. hairdresser, in pl., Arr.Epict.2.23.14, Them.Or.20.238a; beautifier, embellisher, Luc.Merc.Cond.32: metaph., Plu.2.348f: abs., Gal.Thras.35

κομμώτρια.definition: fem. of dresser, tirewoman, Ar.Ec.737, Pl.R.373c, Jul.Caes.335b

κομπάζω.definition: fut. B.7.42:— = boast, brag; = I.2, ring a jar to test its soundness, PLond. ined.2327

Κομπασεύς.definition: Com. word, one of the Bragsman, Ar.Av.1126

κόμπασμα.definition: usu. in pl., boasts, A.Pr.363, Th.551,794, Ar.Ra.940, Alex. ap. POxy.1801.51: sg., Arr.Ind.5.10

κομπολακέω.definition: talk big, be an empty braggart, Ar.Ra.961:—also Tz.H.9.414

κομπολακύθης.definition: or braggart, Ar.Ach.589, 1182, perh. with a play on Lamachus

κόμψευμα.definition: ingenious invention, Arist.Mete.349a30; Luc.Am.54 ; quibble, Gal.6.228

κομψότης.definition: elegance, prettiness, daintiness, esp. of language, Isoc.12.1 , Pl.Ep.358c ; Plu.2.353e

κόναβος.definition: ringing, clashing, din, . . Od.10.122, v.l. for ap. Sch.Hes.Th.709.—Ep. word, once in Trag., A.Th.160 , cf. Luc.Hist.Conscr.22

κονβενταρχέω.definition: to be president of a conventus civium Romanorum, IGRom.4.818

κονδομονόβολον.definition: name of a gambling game, Cod.Just.3.43.1.4

κονδυλίζω.definition: strike with the fist, Hyp.Fr.98 , Aristid.2.95 J.: metaph., maltreat, oppress, LXXMa.3.5; ib.Am.2.7; also Lib.Decl.26.20:—Pass., inured to buffetings, Longin.44.4, cf. D.L.2.21

κονδύλιον.definition: Dim. of IG11.147B10 (Delos; Dim. of f.l. in Axionic.6.3

κονδυλισμός.definition: striking with the fist, maltreatment, Artem.2.15, LXXZe.2.8

κονδυλόομαι.definition: Pass., swell up, Aspasia ap.Aët.16.118, cf. Hsch

κόνδυλος.definition: knuckle, Arist.HA493b28: pl., Hp.Art.2; generally, knuckle of any joint, as of the humerus, Gal.18.617; of the humerus and elbow, Poll.2.141; of the finger , Ruf.Onom.84; Luc.Ocyp.28

κονδύλωμα.definition: knob, callous lump, Hp.Haem.4,5, Dsc.Eup.1.209, Gal.13.533

κονία.definition: pearl-ash, lye, soap-powder, Ar.Lys.470 , cf. Ach.18, Ra.711, Pl.R.430b: pl., Thphr.HP4.10.4

κονιάζω.definition: in Pass., to be sprinkled with ashes, Gp.13.4.2; v.l. for Sm.2 Ki.1.2

κονίαμα.definition: Ion. stucco, plaster, Hp.Epid.7.11, Arist.GA726b27, Col.791b27, 794b32, Thphr.CP4.16.1, PSI5.545.19 , etc.: in pl., D.S.20.8; also, whitewashing, D.13.30

κονίασις.definition: plastering with stucco, whitening, IG11.1246 , 7.2712.35 , 42.102.39, al. , 22.1672.203, Gp.2.27.5, cj. in Thphr.HP4.10.4

κονιάτης.definition: = foreg., IG11.146 A74 , Sammelb.6823.20 , POxy.1450.6 ; gloss on Gal.19.98, cf. Sch.Ar.Av.1150; title of play by Amphis

κονίζω.definition: name of a garment, dub. in Hsch. s.v

κονιορτός.definition: dust raised or stirred; generally, dirt, sweepings, . . Wilcken Chr.198.16

κονίστρα.definition: place covered with dust: hence, rolling; arena in a wrestling school, Lyc.867, Plu.2.638c; Ael.NA11.10, cf. 6.15, Eust.382.32; also in a theatre, Suid. s.v

κοντοπαίκτης.definition: acrobat who balanced a pole on his head, SIG847.4 , AB652

Κοντοπορεία.definition: short road, as pr. n., Ptol.Everg.6 J., Plb.16.16.4

κοπάζω.definition: aor. : pf. Hsch.:—grow weary, LXXJo.14.15; ib.Es.2.1; of an abnormal pulsation, abate, Hp.Epid.7.2; esp. of natural phenomena, Hdt.7.191, cf. Ev.Matt.14.32; Arist.Pr.935a18; LXXNu.11.2; of heat, Longus1.8

κοπία.definition: rest from toil, Hsch. ; but, = Lat. labor, Serv.Dan.ad Virg.G.1.150

κοπιάτης.definition: grave-digger, Cod.Theod. 13.1.1, 16.2.15, Just.Nov.59.2, Gloss.:—also in dat. pl. BCH24.306

κοπιάω.definition: fut. aor. Men.Phasm.36; work hard, toil, Ev.Matt.6.28, etc.; Vett.Val.266.6; 1 Ep.Ti.4.10, cf. Ep.Rom.16.6; 1 Ep.Ti.5.17; LXXJo.24.13: c. inf., strive, struggle, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.37.7

κοπίζω.definition: talk idly, lie, Hsch; celebrate the II), Ath.4.138f

κόπος.definition: striking, beating; toil and trouble, suffering, A.Supp.210 ; Id.Fr.132 ap.Ar.Ra.1265; pain of a disease, S.Ph.880; to give trouble, Ev.Matt.26.10, al., PTeb.21.10 , BGU844.10 ; Phld. Mus.p.62 K.; SIG761 B6

κοπόω.definition: weary, D.Chr.11.96; Id.18.6:—Pass., = Batr.189, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.1.1, Plu.2.312f, Gal.18.914; J.AJ2.15.3

κοπρία.definition: dunghill, Semon.7.6; refuse, LXXSi.27.4; manure, Ev.Luc.13.8

κοπροθέσιον.definition: place where dung is put, Gp.2.22.3

κοπρολόγος.definition: dung-gatherer, Ar.Pax9; scavenger, Arist.Ath.50.2: hence, dirty fellow, Ar.V.1184

κοπροξύστης.definition: one who clears out manure, UPZ119.40

κοπροφορέω.definition: cover with dung or dirt, Ar.Eq.295

κοπροφόρος.definition: carrying dung, Poll.7.134; Id.1.226; dung-basket, X.Mem.3.8.6

κοπρόω.definition: fut. Sch.Ar.Pl.313:—befoul with dung, Arr.Epict.4.11.34:—Pass., ib.29.18

κοπρών.definition: place for dung, privy, Ar.Th.485, D.25.49, Eub.53.2, IG2.1058.11, etc.: prov., of uselesswork, Phot.s.v

κόρειος.definition: the festival of Kore , Plu.Dio56, Hsch; her temple, IG14.217 , Ath.Mitt.49.5

κορεύομαι.definition: Pass., fut. ib.313; to be deflowered, Pherecyd.92 J

κόρημα.definition: sweepings, refuse, Ar.Fr.474: in; besom, broom, Ar.Pax59, Eup.157, 228.4, Gal.12.93

κορίσκομαι.definition: = become saturated, c. gen., Hp.Gland.6; ib.14: abs., to be irked, Id.Art.35

κοροπλάθος.definition: modeller of small figures, imagemaker, Pl.Tht.147b, Isoc.15.2, Luc.Lex.22; name of a play by Antiphanes: —in Hellenistic Gr. EM530.11, Moer.p.234 P

Κορυβάντειος.definition: Corybantian, AP6.165; temple of the Corybantes, Str.10.3.21

κορυμβάς.definition: string running round a net, Hsch

κορυμβόομαι.definition: Pass., to be formed into a Nic.Dam.62 J

κορύνησις.definition: putting forth of knobby buds, Thphr.HP3.5.1, Phan.Hist.25, Arr.Fr.24 J

κορυνηφόρος.definition: club-bearing, Epic. in; peasants at Sicyon, Poll.3.83

κόρυνθος.definition: kind of cake, Id; epith. of Apollo, near Asine

κορύπτω.definition: fut. Orac. ap. Luc.JTr.31:—butt with the head, Theoc.3.5, perh. to be read in Lucil.1241 Marx; etym. of Str.10.3.21; butt at, Tz.ad Lyc.558:—Med., v. ad fin

κορυφαῖος.definition: head man, chief, leader; as Adj., at the top, the apex of the Roman flamen, Plu.Marc.5; the crowning fruits of . . , Hdn.8.3.5; Id.7.5.2; Phld.Po.2.41

κορυφή.definition: head, top: hence; crown, top of the head, of a horse, Il.8.83, X.Eq.1.11; of a man or god, h.Ap.309, Pi.O.7.36, Hdt.4.187, Sammelb.6003.8 : between and Arist.HA491a34; Hp.VC2

κορυφιστής.definition: fillet or diadem, esp. as a woman's head-dress; also, = Hsch

κόρυφος.definition: = I.3, IG42.71.17, al; pet name for a child , PTeb.414.7

κορώνη.definition: a sea-bird, possibly shearwater, Puffinus; crow , Hes.Op.747; Archil.19: distd. from Ar.Av.5 ; Hes.Fr.171; Ar.Av.609; ib.967; having lived out twice a full crow's-age, Babr.46.9; Poll.2.16: prov., 'caught a Tartar', A…

κορώνιος.definition: with crumpled horns, Hsch; name of month at Cnossus, GDI5015.28

κορωνοπόδιον.definition: Dim. of Aët.1.224, Gp.20.9, PMag. Osl.1.283

κορωνόπους.definition: hartshorn, Plantago Coronopus, ib.7.8.3, CP2.5.4, Dsc.2.130, Gal.12.40

κοσκινευτής.definition: one who sifts, winnows, PSI4.365.18 , PCair.Zen. 292.484 , al

κοσκινεύω.definition: sift, in Pass., Democr.164, PHib.1.98.19 , etc.; Gp.3.7.1

κοσκίνιον.definition: Dim. of Chrysipp. Tyan. ap. Ath.14.647 f

κοσκίνισις.definition: sifting, PFlor.388.9 , Phlp.in GA54.2: interlinear gloss on Et.Gud

κόσμημα.definition: ornament, decoration, esp. in dress, X.Cyr.7.3.7, Luc.Salt.32, etc.; Pl.Lg.956b; of adornments buried with the dead, BGU1024. iv 44 : metaph., of the virtues, Luc.Im.11

κόσμησις.definition: ordering, arrangement, Pl.Grg.504 d, cf. Criti.117 b: adornment, Arist.Oec.1344a19; pl., Plu.Thes.23: metaph., dignity, BGU 1024 viii 10

κοσμήτειρα.definition: fem. of Orph.H.10.8; title of a female magistrate at Ephesus, SIG1228 , CIG2823

κοσμητεύω.definition: hold office of , IG22.1009.49, PFlor.57.75 , CPR20.1 , IG3.735, al., BGU362ix 6 : —also IG3.736

κοσμητής.definition: orderer, director, Epigr. ap; at Athens and elsewhere, magistrate in charge of the Arist.Ath.42.2, IG 22.665.10, 17 , 1009.33 , al., Pl.Ax.366e, Telesp.50 H., POxy.519.8 , PFay.85 , etc

κοσμίδιον.definition: Dim. of II, adornment, metaph., Mélanges Beyrouth 7.395

κόσμιον.definition: Dim. of D.S.25.15, Plu.2.141 d, BGU1024 v 27 ; Secund.Sent.5; the insignia of office, D.S.38/9.16; Plu.Demetr.45; Id.Ant.17

κόσμιος.definition: of persons, orderly, well-behaved, ib.89; Lys.21.19; Pl.R.329 d; Id.Phd.108 a; Nicopho16; Anaxandr.56, cf. Arist.Pol.1277b23; Pl.R.408 b; Id.Smp.193 a; Id.R.564 e; of a patient, quiet, Hp.Acut.65: freq. in Oratt., of …

κοσμιότης.definition: propriety, decorum, Ar.Pl.564, Pl.Plt.307 b, Zeno Stoic.1.58, etc.; Pl.Grg.508 a; opp. Arist.EN1109a16: pl., Phld.Mus.p.44 K

κοσμοκράτωρ.definition: lord of the world, epith; of the Emperors, IG14.926, Sammelb.4275, cf. Ptol.Tetr.175, Heph.Astr.1.1

κοσμολογικός.definition: title of work by Ion, Sch.Ar.Pax835

κοσμοπλόκος.definition: holding together the world, of Apollo, AP9.525.11

κοσμοποιέω.definition: make the world, Ph.1.5, Plu.2.719d, 877c; frame a system or theory of the world, Arist.Metaph.1091a18, Cael.301a13; assert them to be worlds, Placit.2.13.15

κοσμοποιητής.definition: creator of the world, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

κοσμόπολις.definition: a magistrate among the Locrians, Plb.12.16.6 , and 9 ; at Thasos, IG12.386, 459; at Lyttus in Crete, CIG2583; at Cibyra, IGRom.4.908; at Miletus, title of the Milet.1.230, 231

κοσμοπολίτης.definition: citizen of the world, Ph.1.1, al., D.L.6.63:—fem. as Adj., Ph.1.657

κοσμοσάνδαλον.definition: Dor. = larkspur, Delphinium Ajacis, Cratin.98, Pherecr.131.4, Paus.2.35.5

κοσμοτρόφος.definition: feeding the world, of Egypt, Man.1.2; IG14.1108c19

κοσμουργέω.definition: create the world, Procl.in Ti.1.334 D

κοσύμβη.definition: = Att. Poll.2.30 (v.l; = shepherd's coat, D.Chr.72.1, EM311.5, cf. 349.45:—written or Hsch

κοτταβισμός.definition: = foreg., prescribed as a cure for Philum. ap.Orib.Syn.9.21.5, Paul.Aeg.3.47

κοτύλη.definition: anything hollow; small vessel, cup, Il.22.494, Od.15.312, 17.12, Ar.Fr.350, cf. Ath.11.478d: prov., ib.e, Zen.5.71

κοτυληδών.definition: any cup-shaped hollow or cavity; in pl., suckers on the arms of the poulp or octopus, Od.5.433, in Ep. dat. cf. Arist.HA524a2, PA685b3, Thphr.HP9.13.6, Ath.11.479b; also on the feet of the Arist.HA527a25: sg., Luc.Mus…

κοτυλιαῖος.definition: holding a Antig.Car. ap.Ath.10.420a, D.L.2.139; Hippoloch. ap. Ath.3.129b:— also written PCair.Zen.89.4

κουρόσυνος.definition: youthful, ib.6.156 ; wrongly expld. as Suid

κουρότερος.definition: Comp. form of , young, opp. elder, Il.4.316, Od.21.310, Hes.Op.[447]: as fem., A.R.1.684

κουροτροφέω.definition: rear as a child, Str.10.3.19; breed men, Philostr.VA8.7

κουστουμηνᾶτον.definition: drink made from Crustumerian pears, ibid

κούφισις.definition: lightening, alleviation, relief, Th.7.75; J.AJ17.6.2, D.C.42.28

κουφόλιθος.definition: talc or talc-powder, PHolm.2.21, al., PLeid.X.6, Alex.Aphr.in Mete.161.6, 15, Aët.2.68

κουφοφορέομαι.definition: Pass., rise by one's own lightness, S.E.M.9.71

κραιπάλη.definition: drinking-bout, Ar.Ach.277; intoxication, Men.Kol.47, Alciphr.1.37, Them.Or.2.36a

κραμάτιον.definition: Dim. of wine and water, Dsc.Eup.1.197, Sor.1.63

κραμβίον.definition: decoction of cabbage, Hp.Mul.1.63, 2.121, Gal.19.114: Sicel. for Erot., Hsch.:—written POxy.1479.10

κραμβοφάγος.definition: Cabbage-eater, name of a frog, v.l. in Batr.218

κράνειον.definition: fruit of Amphis38, Anaxandr.41.54 , Thphr.HP3.2.1: dat. pl. written ib.4.4.5:—later Gal.6.620, al

κρανοποιέω.definition: make helmets: metaph., of one who talks big and warlike, Ar.Ra.1018:—hence Poll.7.155

κράντειρα.definition: fem. of sq. II, APl.4.220 , Orph.Fr.176

κράσπεδον.definition: edge, border, skirt, esp. of cloth; metaph., mostly in pl., skirts or edge of a country, S.Fr.602, E.Fr.381; of a mountain, X.HG4.6.8; on the skirts of the army, E.Supp.661; X.HG3.2.16: also in sg., Plu.Tim.11; AP7.78

κρασπεδόομαι.definition: Pass., to be bordered or edged, E.Ion1423

κραστίζομαι.definition: consume green fodder, Sophr.166, cf. EM535.23, AB273

κραταιβάτης.definition: Dor. striding in might, epith. of Zeus, IG4.669

κραταίβιος.definition: strong with violence, Choerob. in An.Ox.2.318, Eust.1938.1

κραταιίς.definition: of the stone of Sisyphus; as pr.n., the Mighty one, name of the mother of Scylla, Od.12.124

κραταιόγονον.definition: willow-weed, Polygonum Persicaria, Dsc.3.124, Gal.12.44; cf

κραταιόχθων.definition: wielding power over the earth, PMag.Lond.121.353, PMag.Par.1.1355

κραταιόω.definition: strengthen, LXX1 Ki.23.16; Pass., to be determined, ib.Ru.1.18

κραταίπεδος.definition: with hard ground or soil, Od.23.46

κρατερόφρων.definition: gen. stout-hearted, dauntless, epith. of Heracles, Il.14.324; the Dioscuri, Od.11.299; Odysseus, 4.333; a wild beast, Il.10.184; Hes.Op.147, cf. Orph.Fr.164; of Athena, IG12.503

κρατιστεύω.definition: to be mightiest, best, most excellent; to be superior, X.Mem.1.4.14; ib.2.6.26; Id.Cyr.1.5.1

κρατοβρώς.definition: devourer of heads or brains, Lyc.1066

κρατοπλαγής.definition: struck on the head, cj. Lob. for in Man.4.284

κρατυντήριος.definition: strengthening, making firm, Hp.Mul.1.78; title of work of Democritus in support of his doctrines, S.E.M.7.136, D.L.9.47, Suid.; Hsch

Κραυγασίδης.definition: as if a Patron. of Croaker, name of a frog in Batr.243

κραυγαστής.definition: crier, bawler, gloss on AB223:—fem. Hsch.s.v

κραῦρα.definition: fever, a disease in swine and cattle, Suid., Phot., prob. in GDI5001

κραυρόομαι.definition: Pass., become dry or parched, Ph.2.174, D.C.66.21

κραῦρος.definition: = Arist.HA604a14; also, a disease of bees, prob. in Hsch; also Arist.PA655a25:— brittle, friable , Pl.Ti.60d ; of wood, Thphr.HP1.6.2, al., Eust.1906.11; opp. Arist.PAl.c., GA734b32; of meat, dry and cold, Eub.7

κρειττόομαι.definition: Pass., of the vine, to be diseased, have excrescences, Thphr.HP4.14.6, CP5.9.13:—Subst. ibid

κρεμαστήρ.definition: stalk by which a grape-cluster hangs, Gp.5.2.11, 5.17.5; = I, Eust.1625.14

κρεμβαλιάζω.definition: mark time with castanets, Hermipp.31 , cf. Hsch

κρεμβαλιαστύς.definition: rattling with castanets, to give the time in dancing, h.Ap.162

κρεοδαισία.definition: distribution of meat, Demetr.Sceps. ap. Ath.10.425c, Plu.2.643a

κρεοδαίτης.definition: distributor of meat, carver at a public meal, Plu.Lys.23, Ages.8, Poll.6.34, 7.25: Phld.Vit.p.26 J.:—fem. Poll.6.34

κρεοθηκάριος.definition: one who has charge of the larder, title of priest, Supp.Epigr.4.357

κρεοκόπος.definition: cutter up of flesh, D.H.12.2.8 , Gloss

κρεοπώλης.definition: seller of meat, butcher, Macho ap.Ath.13.580c, cf. AP11.212 , Thphr.Char.9.4

κρεοπώλιον.definition: butcher's shop, D.S.12.24, Str.17.2.4, Plu.2.277e, Poll.7.25

κρεουργέω.definition: cut up like a butcher, J.AJ13.12.6: hence, butcher, mangle, Luc.Syr.D.55, D.L.9.108:—Pass., Ph.2.544, D.C.75.7

κρεοφαγέω.definition: Ion. eat flesh, Hp.Salubr.7, Plb.2.17.10 , Str.16.4.17, Ph.2.398 :—Pass., D.S.2.54

κρεοφαγία.definition: Ion. eating of flesh, Hp.Acut.37, D.S.3.31, Ph.2.235 , Porph.Abst.1.15, al.; Str.16.4.9; Plu.2.132a

κρήμνημι.definition: = hang, . . Pi.P.4.25, cf.Arist.Mir.831a8 ; . . E.Fr.1111 ; crucify, App.Mith.97:—Pass., hang, be suspended, E.El.1217 , App.BC1.71; float in air, A.Th.229

κρημνίζω.definition: hurl down headlong, LXX2 Ma.6.10: metaph., Plu.2.5b:—Pass., J.BJ2.3.3, Cat.Cod. Astr.8.156

κρημνοβατέω.definition: haunt precipices, Ctes. ap. Lyd.Mens.4.14, Str.15.1.56, Ph.2.444, S.E.M.11.126, Longus3.28

κρημνοκοπέω.definition: boast, indulge in 'tall talk', Phot., Suid

κρημνοφοβέομαι.definition: to be afraid of precipices, Hp.Ep.19

κρηναῖος.definition: of, from a spring or fountain, = Od.17.240; spring water, Hdt.4.181; S.Tr.14, Ph.21; E.Hipp.225 ; i.e. the water of Dirce, A.Pers.483; AP9.549 ; the gate of Dirce , E.Ph.1123

κρηνίς.definition: = E.Hipp.208; pl. ancient name for Philippi in Macedonia, Str.7Fr.34, App.BC4.105; as local place-name, IG12.544 B2.47

κρηνοφύλαξ.definition: warden of the springs; bronze lion which stood over the spring that supplied the Poll.l.c., Phot

κρηπιδαῖον.definition: basement of a house, Lys.Fr.185 S.:—also IG14.915

κρηπιδιαῖος.definition: belonging to a substructure or foundation, ib.12.313.90, cf. Rev.Phil.50.67

κρησέρα.definition: Ion. Elean , flour-; fine net for fishing, Phot

κρησφύγετον.definition: place of refuge, retreat, Hdt.5.124, al., D.H.4.15, Luc.Eun.10, al

Κρητίζω.definition: speak like a Cretan, D.Chr.[11.23]; play the Cretan, i.e. lie, or 'diamond cut diamond', Plb.8.18.5, Plu.Aem.23, Lys.20

κριβανάριος.definition: in form armoured; baker, dub. in CIL4.677, Stud.Pal.20.131.4

κριβάνη.definition: or a cake, Alcm.20 , cf. Hsch

κριβανίτης.definition: baked in a pan , of bread, Ar.Fr.125, Epich.52, Amips.5, Sophr.27 , Gal.6.489, etc.; loaf so baked, Ar.Ach.1123: hence, comically, ib.87

κριθάριον.definition: Dim. of BGU33.11 , PTeb.420.21 , Thom.Mag.p.202 R

κριθάχυρον.definition: mixture of barley and chaff, PFlor.377.14

κριθιάω.definition: of a horse, suffer from; = wax wanton, Cleanth.Stoic.1.132, Cerc.17.36, Babr.62.2, cf. Poll.7.24

κρίθινος.definition: made of or from barley, Hippon.35, Luc.Macr.5; Thphr.HP8.4.1, PEleph.5.25 , Plu.2.397a; Hp.Acut.64; ib. 30; beer, Plb.34.9.15; Plu.2.752b: metaph., 'gingerbread Demosthenes', nickname of Dinarchus, Hermog.Id.2.11

κριθόμαντις.definition: one who divined by barley, Suid. s.v

κριθοπομπία.definition: sending of barley, Eratosth. ap. Hsch.s.v

κριθόπυρον.definition: wheat mixed with barley, PPetr.3p.206, al. , PSI5.532.6 , PFay.101 iii 4 : acc. pl. PCair.Zen.498

κριθοφάγος.definition: living on barley, D.C.Fr.43.33, cf. Sch.Ar.Av.232

κριθοφυλακία.definition: office of controller of export of barley, Hsch

κριθώλεθρος.definition: barley-wasting, of horses that will not fatten, Phryn.PSp.79 B

κρικέλλιον.definition: Dim. of sq., hoop of a ring, Alex.Trall.8.2

κρικηλασία.definition: trundling of hoops, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.26.1

κρικοποιέομαι.definition: to be formed into a ring, Heracl. ap. Orib.48.13.1

κρίκος.definition: Homeric form of ring, on a; eyelet-hole in sails, through which the reefingropes were drawn, Hdt.2.36, cf. Poll.1.94, PLond.3.11648

κρίμνος.definition: a purple dye, PHolm.8.43 ; Ps.-Democr. Alch.p.42 B.; Hsch

Κρινόεις.definition: name of one of the Idaean; like a lily, dub. cj. in Supp.Epigr.4.386

κρινωνιά.definition: prop. bed of lilies, Suid.; but, = Thphr.HP2.2.1, 6.6.9

κριοβόλιον.definition: sacrifice of a ram, IG14.1018 (iv A

κριοκοπέω.definition: batter with a battering-ram, Plb.1.42.9, App.Mith.36: abs., Ath.Mech.14.11, Apollod.Poliorc.143.7

κριοπρόσωπος.definition: ram-faced, Hdt.2.42; with a ram as figurehead, Nymphis18

κριόστασις.definition: station, position for a battering-ram, Ph.Bel.92.19

κριοτάφος.definition: one who buries sacred rams, PTeb.72.411

κριοφάγος.definition: devouring rams, epith. of a divinity, Hsch

κριοφόρος.definition: carrying battering-rams; bearing a ram, epith. of Hermes, Paus.9.22.1

κριόω.definition: pf. part. Pass. made into a ram, Hsch.s.v

κριτήριον.definition: means for judging or trying, standard; court of judgement, tribunal, Pl.Lg.767b; Plb.9.33.12, cf. PHib.1.29 , 1 Ep.Cor.6.2, IG14.951.20, Paus.2.20.7, POxy.2134.6 , etc

Κριτιάζω.definition: imitate the style of Critias, Philostr.VS1.16.2; ib.2.1.14

κρόκινος.definition: of or made from saffron; yellow, Stratt.69, Thphr.HP1.13.1, 3.4.5, POxy. 1679.5 , Democr.Eph. ap. Ath.12.525c:—the form in Artem.1.77 is corrupt

κροκοβαφής.definition: = foreg., Sch.Pi.N.1.58: metaph., the sallow, sickly blood-drop such as might be supposed to run to the heart of dying men, A.Ag.1121

κροκοδιλοβοσκός.definition: feeder of sacred crocodiles, BGU734 ii 7

κροκοδιλοειδής.definition: in the form of a crocodile, PMag. Leid.V.3.15

κροκόδιλος.definition: prop. Ion. word for lizard, acc. to; crocodile found in the Nile, Hdt.2.68 sq.; also in Indian rivers, Id.4.44, cf. Ael.NA12.41; Arist.HA492b24, cf. 558a18. , PTeb.63.25 , etc.; later PAmh.2.45.8 , etc., freq. in codd…

κροκοδιλοτάφιον.definition: burial-place of sacred crocodiles, PGrenf.2.14 , PTeb.88.4 , BGU1303.9

κροκόπεπλος.definition: with yellow veil, Il.8.1, 19.1, al.; Hes.Th.273; of a river-nymph, ib.358; of the Muses, Alcm.85 A

κροκυδίζω.definition: pick loose flocks off a garment, Philyll.22, Gal.10.928; of persons in delirium, twitch the blankets, Aret.CA1.1

κροκυδισμός.definition: picking of flocks, Gal.19.412:—hence Dim. of Id.10.867, Theognost.Can.125

Κρονίδης.definition: Patron., son of Cronos, i.e; Lacon. an aged man, Hsch

Κρόνιος.definition: of Cronos or Saturn; Astrol., i.e. disaster, Hld.2.24

Κρονίων.definition: son of Cronos, i.e. Zeus, Il.1.397; name of a month at Samos, etc., SIG976.2 , al. [Hom. has in in other cases but Tyrt.2.1, Pi.P.4.23, etc., use in

κροσσόω.definition: assumed as etym. of sq., EM541.8, Et.Gud.349.33

κροταλίστρια.definition: female castanet-player, Sammelb.6945 ; Lat. crotalistria, of the stork, from the noise made by its mandibles, Publilius ap.Petron.55

κροτάφιος.definition: on or of the temples, Gal.14.720

κροταφίς.definition: pointed hammer, resembling the IG22.1672.120, Poll.10.147

κροταφιστής.definition: one who strikes on the temples, Gloss., Hsch. s.v

κροταφίτης.definition: temporal muscle, Hp.Art.30, Gal.UP16.6, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.2, Arch.Pap.4.270 :—fem. blows on the temples, Hp.l.c

κρόταφος.definition: side of the forehead, Il.4.502, 20.397; generally, side edge, profile, Procl.Hyp.3.6; ib.17; of a brick, PMag.Par.1.30; sideways, horizontally, HeroBel.98.2, Ph.Bel.64.25, cf. 60.7; on its side, ib.66.13

κρότησις.definition: clapping, striking, as a sign of grief, Pl.Ax.365a; Ph.Bel.71.44 ; D.H.Comp.14

κροτωνοφόρος.definition: bearing castor-oil plants, Sammelb.6797.16, al. , PPetr. 2p.110

κρουμάτιον.definition: Dim. of musical phrase, Ach.Tat.1.5, Sch.Ar.Eq.276, Pl.290

κρουματοποιός.definition: musician, Macho ap. Ath.8.337c, Aristodem.8; composer of instrumental music, Phld. Mus.pp.95,99 K

κρουνίσκος.definition: = foreg., cock, tap of the clepsydra, Sch.Luc.Pisc.28

κρουνισμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., small nozzle or spout, HeroSpir.1.8; small pipe, ib.29

κρουνισμός.definition: gushing out of water, Aq. 2 Ki.5.8; Medic., douche, Aët.5.119, Paul.Aeg.2.52

κρουνός.definition: spring, well head, whence streams; metaph., E.Rh.790, cf. Hec.568; streams of lava from Etna, Pi.P.1.25; of streaming perspiration, Hp.Aph.7.85, Lib.Ep.316.3: metaph., torrent of words, Ar.Ra.1005

κρουπεζόομαι.definition: Pass., have wooden shoes on, Hsch

κρουπεζοφόρος.definition: wearing wooden shoes, of the Boeotians, Cratin.310

κρουσιδημέω.definition: parody on cheat the people, Ar.Eq.859

κρουσίθυρος.definition: knocking at the door: serenade, Trypho ap.Ath.14.618c

κρουσιμετρέω.definition: cheat in measuring corn, by striking off too much from the top of the measure, Hsch., Poll.4.169

κρουσμός.definition: = 4, Procl. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.320; gnashing of teeth, Aus.Ep.8.8

κρούω.definition: fut. E.El.180: aor. X.An.4.5.18, Hyp.Fr.201: pf. Diogenian.3.38, Pl.Phdr.228e, D.21.206:-Med., aor. Th.7.40:-Pass., aor. Eratosth.Cat.32: pf. X.HG7.4.26, or Ar.Ach.459:-strike, smite, S.Fr.501; E.Fr.779.6; Lys.Fr.83; …

κρύβηλος.definition: hidden, Hsch.:—also one hidden in the earth, and = Id

κρύβω.definition: late form of Conon50.2, Phlp.in APr.448.17, PMag.Par.1.385, PMag.Leid.V.10.10, Gp.2.24.2, Sch.E.Hec.739:—Pass., LXX4 Ki.11.3, al. ; mostly found in compds

κρυμώσσω.definition: to be stiff with cold, Theognost.Can.21

κρυπτεύω.definition: hide oneself, lie concealed, E.Ba.888 , X.Cyr.4.5.5:—Pass., = , E.Hel.541

κρυπτήριος.definition: convenient for concealing, Orac. ap. Paus.8.42.6; dungeon, prob. l. in E.Cret.48

κρυσταίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be congealed with cold, freeze, Nic.Al.314

κρυσταλλίζω.definition: to be clear as crystal, Apoc.21.11

κρυστάλλιον.definition: rock-crystal, in pl., PHolm.11.43, Anon.Alch.p.359 B

κρυσταλλοειδής.definition: like ice, Epicur.Ep.2p.45U; like crystal, Dsc.5.142; the crystalline lens, Ruf.Onom.153, Gal.UP8.5, al.; Poll.2.71: Astron., the crystalline sphere, Placit.2.14.3

κρυσταλλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be frozen, Ph.2.174, Anon. ap.Gell.17.8.7

κρυσταλλόπηκτος.definition: congealed to ice, frozen, E.Rh.441:— also A.Pers.501

κρυφαῖος.definition: also Phld.Piet.101; secret, clandestine, A.Pers.360; ib.385; S.Fr.935; Phld.l.c. Adv. A.Pers.370, Aen. Tact.18.8

κρύφιμος.definition: = Man.1.159, al., PMag.Par.1.1353, PMag.Lond.122.15, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.185: Comp., Dam.Pr.275

κρυφιότης.definition: secrecy, obscurity, Suid. s.v. Sch.Opp.H.2.258, Sch.E.Ph.1214

κρυψίνοος.definition: contr. hiding one's thoughts, dissembling, X.Cyr.1.6.27, Gal.8.362, D.C.67.1, Eun.Hist.p.254 D.; opp. X.Ages.11.5. Adv. Poll.4.51

κρώζω.definition: fut. prop. croak, of the Hes.Op.747, cf. Ar.Av.2, 24, Arat.953, Luc.Asin.12, Poll.5.89; also of other birds, as cranes, Ar.Av.710; of young halcyons, Luc.VH2.40; also, of men, croak out, Ar.Lys.506, Pl.369; of a wagon…

κτέανον.definition: usu. in pl. possessions, property, Hes.Op.315, Sol.4.12, Pi.O.3.42, N.9.32; Xenoph.2.8; used in lyr. by A.Th.729, Ag.1573, E.Ion490; by S. in hexam. ap. Sch.S.OC378 ; by Eub. in a mock heroic line, 139: in Prose, Hp.E…

κτενίζω.definition: comb, Anaxil.39, cf. PSI4.404.4 ; curry horses, E.Hipp.1174: metaph., D.H.Comp.25:—Med., comb one's hair, Hdt.7.208: so abs., Ar.Fr.603, Antiph.148.4:—Pass., with one's hair combed, Archil.165, cf. Semon.7.65; Hippiat…

κτένιον.definition: Dim. of 1, POxy.1142.7; in pl., = 3, Hsch

κτηματίδιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., small estate, PMasp.21.19

κτηνοτροφία.definition: cattle-keeping, Str.17.2.3, D.H.3.36 , Ph.1.304, BGU969.12, al. , Plu.Publ.11

κτηνοτρόφος.definition: keeping cattle, pastoral, D.S.1.74; a land of pasture, LXXNu.32.4: as Subst., cattle-keeper, Ph.1.304: pl., PFay.18 , Dsc.2.147, BGU969.11

κτησείδιον.definition: Dim. of Arr.Epict.1.1.10; v.l. for in Jul.Ep.4

κτήσιος.definition: belonging to property; domestic, the protector of house and property, A.Supp.445, Hp.Insomn.89, Orac. ap. D.21.53, Antipho1.16: pl., Anticl.13; also Hp. l.c.; Plu.2.828a; the altar of A.Ag.1038; = Lat. Penates, D.H.8.41

κτήσιππος.definition: possessing horses, pr. n. in Od., cf. Luc.Fug.26

κτήτωρ.definition: possessor, owner, D.S.34/5.2.31, POxy. 237 viii 31 , A.D.Pron.22.6, AP7.206 , Procop.Arc.26: c. gen., Act.Ap.4.34

κτίννυμι.definition: collat. form of App.BC1.71 , 4.35; Polyaen.1.23, 25, Plot.3.2.15:—Pass., App.BC1.2; J.AJ18.8.3:—more freq. in compd. , cf. Phryn.PSp.51 B.; and are correct acc. to Choerob.in An.Ox.2.233

κτίσμα.definition: colony, foundation; = II, LXXWi.9.2 , 3 Ma.5.11, Ep.Jac.1.18

κτιστεῖον.definition: sanctuary of a founder, PLips.97 xiii7

κτίστωρ.definition: = Pi.Fr.105; E.Ion74; of Zeno, Ath.9.370c; . . Diph.138

κτοίνα.definition: or Rhod. name for a local division, like Att. township, IG12.694, 1033, al.; cf. Hsch

κτύπημα.definition: = Critias25.32 D.; D.C.51.17, cf. Jul.Or.7.220b; E.Andr.1211

κτυπητής.definition: one who makes a noise, Suid. s.v

κτύπος.definition: crash, bang, din, Il.20.66, cf. 12.338, A.Th.100, etc.; of thunder, S.OC1463 , A.Pr.923; of the trampling of feet, Od.16.6, cf. S.Ph.202; rattling of chariots or sound of horses' feet, Il.10.535, al., S.El.714, Ar.Eq.…

κυαθιαῖος.definition: contained in a a ladleful of water, Them.in Ph.135.26, Simp.in Ph.174.30, Phlp.in Mete.24.22, Id.in GA92.22

κυαμιαῖος.definition: of the size of a bean, Dsc.2.133, Luc.Herm.40

κυαμών.definition: field of I.2, Thphr.HP4.8.8, Str.17.1.15, BGU1119.11

κυαναυγής.definition: dark-gleaming, E.Alc.261 ; Alciphr.3.1; of the sea, D.P.169, etc.; Supp.Epigr.4.467.25 ; com. of dithyrambs, Ar.Av.1389

κυάνεος.definition: of the colour of dark-blue, glossy, of the swallow, Simon.74; of the halcyon, Arist.HA616a15; of the skin of the porpoise, ib.566b12; of the deep sea, E.IT7, cf. Arist.Pr.932a31; Xenarch.1.7; Pl.l.c.; Thphr.Sens.77

κυανέω.definition: to be dark in colour, D.P.1111, Phryn.PSp.80 B. metri gr.]

κυανίζω.definition: = foreg., Dsc.1.1, Placit.3.5.12; of varicose veins, Gal.13.460

κυανοειδής.definition: dark-blue, deep-blue, E.Hel.179 , cf. Arist.GA779b33, Col.796a18

κυανόπεζα.definition: with feet of Il.11.629. metri gr.]

κυανόπεπλος.definition: dark-veiled, of Demeter mourning for her daughter, h.Cer.319, 360, 374; of Leto, Hes.Th.406. metri gr.]

κυανόπρῳρος.definition: darkprowed, of ships, Il.15.693, 23.852, Od.9.482, 539: fem. B.16.1

κυανόπτερος.definition: with blue-black feathers, like the raven, E.Andr.862 : generally, dark- winged, Hes.Sc.393

κυανοχαίτης.definition: dark-haired, in Hom. usu. of Poseidon, perh. in reference to the dark blue of the sea, Il.20.144, Od.9.536, cf. Hes.Th.278; Thebais4; of a horse, dark-maned, Il.20.224, Hes.Sc.120: voc. h.Cer.347:—also nom. Il.13.563,…

κυανόχροος.definition: dark in hue, E.Hel.1502 ; Nech. ap. Vett.Val.241.18; Opp.H.2.599

κυανόχρωτος.definition: = foreg., Orph.H.70.6, Man.1.327. metri gr., Orph.l.c.; Man. l.c.]

κυβάζω.definition: set on the head, turn upside down, Hsch

κυβέρνησις.definition: metaph., government, of cities, Pi.P.10.72 , cf. 1 Ep.Cor.12.28 ; by a god, Plu.2.162a

κυβερνητήρ.definition: Dor. = Od.8.557, etc.: metaph., Pi.P.4.274: as Adj., Opp.C.1.96

κυβευτής.definition: dicer, gambler, S.Fr.947, Eup.11.8 D., X.HG6.3.16, Men.965, Vett.Val.202.6; name of plays by Antiphanes, etc

κυβεύω.definition: play at dice, Cratin.195, Ar.Ec.672; metaph., run a risk or hazard, X.HG6.3.16, cf. Plu.Art.17; Pl.Prt.314a; Plb.Fr.6

κυβίζω.definition: make into a cube, Plu.2.979f; of numbers, raise to the cube, HeroMetr.3.22:—Pass., Procl.Hyp.4.102, Theol.Ar.33; to be multiplied, Hippol.Haer.1.2.10

κυβοειδής.definition: like a cube, cubical, Epicur.Nat.14.5, Str.16.1.5, Dsc.5.98, Gal.5.668, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.4.47; Gal.UP3.7, al

κυβόκυβος.definition: cube multiplied by cube, i.e. sixth; sixth power of unknown quantity, x6, Dioph.1Def.1, Sch.Iamb.in Nic.p.131 P..:—hence , fraction corresponding to 1/x6, Dioph.1Def.3

κυδάζω.definition: revile, abuse, Epich.6:—in Med., c.dat., Id.35.6; A.Fr.94: c. acc., A.R.1.1337:—Pass., to be reviled, S.Aj.722

κυδάλιμος.definition: also IG5.599 : :—glorious, renowned, in Hom. epith. of heroes, Il.17.378, Od.14.206, al.; of nations, Il.6.184, 204; a noble heart, of Agamemnon and Achilles, 10.16, 18.33; the suitor Eurymachus, Od.21.247; the lion, …

κύδιμος.definition: = epith. of Hermes, h.Merc.46, al., Hes.Th.938; Pi.O.14.24

κυδοιμός.definition: din of battle, uproar, hubbub, Il.10.523, cf. 18.218; Ar.Ach.573; cock-fights, personified, as companion of and Il.5.593, 18.535, cf. Emp.128.1, Ar.Pax255.—Ep. word, used by Ar. and in later Prose, as Plb.5.48.5, Luc.…

κυδωνέα.definition: quince-tree, Pyrus Cydonia, PCair.Zen.486.2 , Gp.4.1.12:—also ib.10.24

Κυδωνιάτης.definition: inhabitant of Cydonia in Crete, Plb.4.55.4, Str.10.4.12, etc

κυδωνιάω.definition: swell like a quince, APl.4.182 ; Aristaenet.1.1, cf. 3

Κυδώνιος.definition: Cydonian, quinces; metaph., swelling like a quince, of a young girl's breasts, Ar.Ach.1199

κυητήριος.definition: aiding conception, Hp.Nat.Mul.109: as Subst. Id.Mul.1.75, al

κυΐσκομαι.definition: Pass., of the female, conceive, become; Act. in same sense, Hp.Aph.5.62, Philostr.VA1.22, Gp.14.1.3, Gal.4.513; but

κυκλεύω.definition: traverse, Str.6.3.7, cf. J.AJ9.3.1, Supp.Epigr.2.530 ; Cleom.1.2

κυκλίσκιον.definition: Dim. of sq.I.2, Dsc.2.83, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.95

κυκλίσκος.definition: Dim. of small circle in a; small round cake of wax, Dsc.2.83; lozenge, = Hp.Mul.2.188, Gal.12.276, Lycus ap. Orib.8.25.23, Aët.15.37

κυκλισμός.definition: circular motion, circularity, Simp.in Ph.1280.33, Olymp.in Phd.pp.141,145 N., Hsch. s.v

Κυκλοβορέω.definition: brawl like the torrent Cycloborus, Ar.Ach.381

κυκλογραφέω.definition: describe a circle, S.E.M.3.26, 9.420; use periphrasis, D.H.Dem.19

κυκλογραφία.definition: description, tracing of a circle, Simp.in Cael.210.5

κυκλοδίωκτος.definition: driven round in a circle, AP9.301

κυκλοειδής.definition: circular, Euc.Opt.36, Onos.21.6, Ath.7.328d; Plu.2.1004c. Adv. Gal.Phil.Hist.100, Porph.in Cat.133.4

κυκλοπορέω.definition: go by a circuitous way, Str.7.1.4

κυκλοπορία.definition: going round, circuitous way, Id.2.1.39, 11.13.4: pl., Id.16.4.23

κυκλοτερής.definition: made round by turning : generally, round, circular, stretched it into a circle, Il.4.124; Od.17.209; Hes.Th.145, Sc.208; Emp.27.4; Id.45; Hdt.4.184; Id.1.194; of the sockets of bones, Hp.Art.61; Pl.Smp.190a; Henioch.1…

κυκνόμορφος.definition: swan-shaped, or white as a swan, A.Pr.795

κυμάτιον.definition: Dim. of I.3, IG12.372.166, al; groove, HeroAut.3.1

κυματοειδής.definition: like waves: stormy, Arist.Pr.942a6. Adv. Democr.126

κωδωνόκροτος.definition: of or with jingling bells, S.Fr.859 ; E.Rh.383

κωλικεύομαι.definition: Pass., suffer from colic, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.73, Alex. Trall.8.2

κωλυμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., catch or clutch in a machine, HeroSpir.1.17, al

κωλυσανέμας.definition: or checking the winds, epith. of Empedocles, Timae.94, Suid. s.v. cf

κωλυσιδρόμης.definition: one who obstructs the course, Luc.Trag.198

κωλυσιεργέω.definition: hinder, obstruct operations, Plb.6.15.5, Ph.1.64, 240, J.AJ15.11.7

κωλυτήριος.definition: preventive, of . . , D.H.11.62; Iamb.VP28.141, Apollon.Mir.4: as Subst. Dsc.1.103

κατακρύβδην.definition: Adv. in private, in secret, opp. Ptol.Tetr.64

καταλοφάδεια.definition: Adv., = on the neck, Od.10.169: by metrical lengthening for , v. Eust. ad loc.--Perh. to be read divisim, cf

καταμελεϊστί.definition: Adv. limb by limb, Arat.624 metri gr.]

κάταντα.definition: Adv. downhill, Il.23.116, cf. Luc.Merc.Cond.26: c. gen., below, prob. in PFlor.370.7

καταπαραλλήλως.definition: Adv. along a parallel of latitude, Vit. Pyth.ap.Phot.Bibl.p.440 B

καταπεφρονηκότως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Act. of; Adv.pf.part. Pass

καταστρεπτικῶς.definition: Adv. so as to end, opp. Stoic.3.34 ap.Sch.Luc.Bis Acc.22

καταστροφικῶς.definition: Adv. by way of conclusion, Ath.10.453c

κατατεθαρρηκότως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Act. of boldly, confidently, Plb.1.86.5, Plu.Ant.27

κατατεταγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., in order, D.S.9.10 , eagerly)

καταυτόθι.definition: Adv. on the spot, A.R.2.16, 776, etc.; but in Hom. shd. be read, for belongs to the Verb, v. Hdn.Gr. ad Il.10.273 on the accent

καταφυλαδόν.definition: Adv. in tribes, by clans, Il.2.668, Opp.H.3.644

κατεβλακευμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of slothfully, tardily, Ar.Pl.325, AP4.3a.16

κάτεγγυς.definition: Adv. near, c. gen., prob. in Hippon.42

κατεζητημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. from in a farfetched, recondite style, Vett. Val.301.29

κατέναντα.definition: Adv. over against, opposite, c. gen., Cydias1, Pancrat.Oxy.1085.24, Q.S.1.552, Man.3.176: c. dat., Id.6.277: abs., Id.3.132:—also LXXEx.19.2; ib.Ez.11.1; Ev.Marc.11.2, cf. UPZ79.11 , Inscr.Prien.37.170

κατεσκολιωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. as if from crookedly, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.1

κατευθύ.definition: Adv. straight forward, X.Smp.5.5, cf. Luc.Jud.Voc.11; Paus.2.11.3: c. gen., Plu.2.3b; on the same side , Ruf. ap.Paul.Aeg.3.45

κατηγγειωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., by means of blood-vessels, Sor.1.73

κατηκριβωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., precisely, Gal.18.861

κατηναγκασμένως.definition: Adv.pf.part.Pass., of necessity, D.S.15.50, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.45, Diog.Oen.33, Alex.Aphr.Fat.181.23

κατηπειγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., hurriedly, Hld.8.1, Sch.E.Or.1433

κατιθύς.definition: Adv. opposite, c. gen., Babr.95.42, Q.S.7.136:—also Herod.8.60, Man.1.30; cf. II.2

κατόπιν.definition: Adv., behind, after, Hp.Mul.1.12; of Time, after, hereafter, f.l. in Thgn.280; Thphr.HP7.13.7; 'too late for the fair', Pl.Grg.447a; Plb.1.46.7, Phld.Ind.Sto.19; Plu.Cam.43; AP9.70

κάτωθεν.definition: rarely Eub.16, Alex.128.3, Theoc.4.44; below, beneath, Pl.Cra.408d; D.2.10; the law below, Id.23.28, cf. Did. ap. Harp. s.v. S.Ant.521; ib.1070, cf. E.Alc.424

κατωκάρα.definition: Adv. head downwards, Pi.Fr.161, Ar.Ach.945 , Ph.1.207, Agath.2.2; heels over head, Ar.Pax153

κατωρθωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., successfully, Phlp.in Ph.142.10

καυληδόν.definition: Adv. like a stalk, Opp.C.2.511; surgical name of a kind of fracture, Sor.Fract.10, Paul.Aeg.6.89

κεκορεσμένως.definition: Adv., to satiety, gloss on EM16.42

κεκρατημένως.definition: Adv., in a masterly manner; vigorously, v.l. in D.H.Comp.25

κελευσματικῶς.definition: Adv. by way of command, Eust.1080.63

Κελτιστί.definition: Adv. in the language of the Celts, Arr.Tact.43.2, Luc.Alex.51

κεφαληδόν.definition: Adv. like a head, f.l. in Opp.C.3.437; individually, Inscr.Prien.362.25

κεχαρισμένως.definition: Adv., acceptably, Ar.Ach.248, Pl.Phdr.273e, D.S.17.47; Isoc.2.15, cf. X.Eq.Mag.1.1 ; Plu.2.6b

κεχιασμένως.definition: Adv., like a X, cross-wise, Theol.Ar.19

κιονηδόν.definition: Adv., like a pillar, i.e. in verticallines from top to bottom, Sch.D.T.pp.183,191 H

κλαγγηδόν.definition: Adv. with a clang, noise, din, Il.2.463:—also Babr.124.13, prob. in Id.135.3

κλέβδην.definition: Dor. Adv. by stealth, A.D.Adv.198.6, EM103.13

κλιμακηδόν.definition: Adv., like a ladder or stairs, A.D.Adv.197.19: wrongly written in Hsch. s.v

κλωκυδά.definition: Adv. in a squatting position, Hsch

Κολωνῆθεν.definition: Adv. from the deme , D.21.64, IG22.650, etc

κομιδῇ.definition: entirely, altogether, quite, with Verbs, Pl.Smp.215d, cf. Antiph.74.12; Id.191.14; Plu.Cic.30: more freq. with Adjs., Pl.Tht.159a; . . D.1.22; Id.18.295; Antiph.218.4; Eub.41.7; Arist.EN1114a10; ib.1166b5: with Substs…

κοσκινηδόν.definition: Adv. as in a sieve, Luc.Tim.3, Sat.24

κρατιστίνδην.definition: Adv. by choosing the best, Poll.1.176

κρεουργηδόν.definition: Adv. like a butcher, in pieces, Hdt.3.13

κρουνηδόν.definition: Adv. like a spring, gushing, LXX2 Ma.14.45, Ph.2.96, Harp.Astr.inCat.Cod. Astr.8.136

κρυβῆ.definition: Adv., = v.l. in LXX2 Ki.12.12, cf. 3 Ma.4.12, POxy.83.14 :—also Corp.Herm.13.1

κρυφηδόν.definition: Adv., = foreg., opp. Od.14.330, cf. Q.S.14.60

κυκληδόν.definition: Adv. in a circle, Posidon.36 J

κυκλόθεν.definition: Adv. from all around, Lys.7.28, cf. Hp.Fract.33, Thphr.HP4.6.10 , etc.: c. gen., LXX3 Ki.18.32, al., Apoc.4.3: c. dat., LXX3 Ki.6.5: spelt IPE12.175 , and sts. in codd., but this spelling is condemned by Theognost.Can…

Κυκλωπικῶς.definition: Adv. like the Cyclopes, to live an unsocial life, Arist.EN1180a28

κυνηδόν.definition: Adv., like a dog, S.Fr.722, Ar.Eq.1033, Nu.491, Luc.Tim.54

κυνοκεφαλιστί.definition: Adv. after the manner of the PMag.Lond.46.27

κυριωνυμικῶς.definition: Adv. by a proper name, Pediasim. ad Theoc.Syrinx3

κωμηδόν.definition: Adv. in villages, Str.3.2.15; D.S.5.6, D.H.1.9, etc
